children.title: Bilinearly Coupled Composite Saddles
children.top_down_role: Canonical composite saddle models with proximable primal and dual components.

knowledge_statements.title: Bilinearly Coupled Composite Saddles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical convex-concave representation of a proximable composition through Fenchel dualization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be real Hilbert spaces, let \(K:X\to Y\) be bounded linear, and let \(f\in\Gamma_0(X)\) and \(g\in\Gamma_0(Y)\). The composite problem and its bilinearly coupled saddle representation are
\[\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+g(Kx)\}=\inf_{x\in X}\sup_{y\in Y}\{f(x)+\langle Kx,y\rangle-g^*(y)\}.\]
A pair \((\bar x,\bar y)\) is a saddle point precisely when
\[0\in\partial f(\bar x)+K^*\bar y,\qquad 0\in\partial g^*(\bar y)-K\bar x.\]
Under a standard Fenchel qualification, such as \(0\in\operatorname{sri}(K\operatorname{dom}f-\operatorname{dom}g)\), its saddle value equals the primal optimum and the dual optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fenchel dualization replaces a proximable composition by a convex-concave saddle whose primal and dual optimality conditions involve separate subdifferentials and the coupling operator.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in\Gamma_0(X)\) and \(g\in\Gamma_0(Y)\).
\(K:X\to Y\) is bounded linear.
\(0\in\operatorname{sri}(K\operatorname{dom}f-\operatorname{dom}g)\) when value equality and attainment are asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_x(f(x)+g(Kx))=\inf_x\sup_y(f(x)+\langle Kx,y\rangle-g^*(y))\), with the displayed primal-dual inclusions characterizing saddle points.

notation.meaning: Proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions on X.

children.title: Smooth-Composite Saddle Models
children.top_down_role: Saddle models with an explicitly treated smooth component in addition to proximable terms.

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth-Composite Saddle Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite saddle form with a forward-treated smooth primal term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X,Y\) be real Hilbert spaces, \(K:X\to Y\) bounded linear, \(f\in\Gamma_0(X)\), \(g\in\Gamma_0(Y)\), and let \(h:X\to\mathbb R\) be convex and Fréchet differentiable with \(L_h\)-Lipschitz gradient. Then
\[\min_{x\in X} f(x)+h(x)+g(Kx)=\min_{x\in X}\max_{y\in Y} f(x)+h(x)+\langle Kx,y\rangle-g^*(y).\]
A pair \((\bar x,\bar y)\) is saddle-optimal exactly when
\[0\in\partial f(\bar x)+\nabla h(\bar x)+K^*\bar y,\qquad 0\in\partial g^*(\bar y)-K\bar x.\]
Thus \(\partial f\) and \(\partial g^*\) remain available for backward steps, while \(\nabla h\) is an explicit single-valued component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A differentiable convex term augments the standard composite saddle; its gradient is explicit while the nonsmooth primal and dual terms remain separated.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in\Gamma_0(X)\) and \(g\in\Gamma_0(Y)\).
\(h\) is convex, Fréchet differentiable, and \(\nabla h\) is \(L_h\)-Lipschitz.
\(K:X\to Y\) is bounded linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The smooth-composite problem has the displayed saddle representation and coupled first-order optimality system.

notation.meaning: A Lipschitz constant of the gradient of h.

children.title: Linearly Constrained Lagrangian Saddles
children.top_down_role: Lagrangian saddle representations of separable objectives with linear equality coupling.

knowledge_statements.title: Linearly Constrained Lagrangian Saddles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian saddle representation for two-block separable equality-constrained convex optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X,Z,Y\) be real Hilbert spaces, let \(A:X\to Y\) and \(B:Z\to Y\) be bounded linear, let \(c\in Y\), and let \(f\in\Gamma_0(X)\) and \(g\in\Gamma_0(Z)\). For
\[\inf_{x\in X,\,z\in Z}\{f(x)+g(z):Ax+Bz=c\},\]
the Lagrangian is \(\mathcal L(x,z,y)=f(x)+g(z)+\langle y,Ax+Bz-c\rangle\). A triple \((\bar x,\bar z,\bar y)\) is a Lagrangian saddle point exactly when
\[0\in\partial f(\bar x)+A^*\bar y,\qquad 0\in\partial g(\bar z)+B^*\bar y,\qquad A\bar x+B\bar z=c.\]
If the primal value is finite and
\[0\in\operatorname{sri}\bigl(A\operatorname{dom}f+B\operatorname{dom}g-\{c\}\bigr),\]
then Fenchel–Rockafellar duality gives no duality gap and attainment of the dual optimum; consequently, primal and dual optimizers form a Lagrangian saddle point exactly when the displayed system holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separable convex objective with linear equality coupling has a Lagrangian saddle representation. Its saddle conditions are block stationarity and primal feasibility; a stated strong-relative-interior qualification yields dual attainment and no duality gap.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in\Gamma_0(X)\) and \(g\in\Gamma_0(Z)\).
\(A:X\to Y\) and \(B:Z\to Y\) are bounded linear.
The primal value is finite and \(0\in\operatorname{sri}(A\operatorname{dom}f+B\operatorname{dom}g-\{c\})\) when dual attainment and no duality gap are asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed stationarity and feasibility conditions characterize Lagrangian saddle points; under the stated qualification, primal and dual optimizers satisfy them with no duality gap.

notation.meaning: Hilbert adjoints of A and B.

children.title: Multi-Operator Saddle Models
children.top_down_role: Saddle models exposing several independently accessible operator components.

knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Operator Saddle Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-family saddle representation separating several composed convex terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) and \(Y_i\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), be real Hilbert spaces, let \(K_i:X\to Y_i\) be bounded linear, and let \(f\in\Gamma_0(X)\), \(g_i\in\Gamma_0(Y_i)\). The multi-composite problem admits the representation
\[\min_{x\in X}\left(f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m g_i(K_i x)\right)=\min_{x\in X}\max_{y_i\in Y_i}\left(f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\bigl(\langle K_i x,y_i\rangle-g_i^*(y_i)\bigr)\right).\]
Its saddle points satisfy
\[0\in\partial f(\bar x)+\sum_{i=1}^mK_i^*\bar y_i,\qquad 0\in\partial g_i^*(\bar y_i)-K_i\bar x\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).\]
A standard Fenchel qualification is required when equality of attained primal and dual values is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Several linearly composed convex terms are dualized independently, yielding one primal stationarity inclusion and one dual inclusion per component.
assumptions_latex: \(m<\infty\), \(f\in\Gamma_0(X)\), and \(g_i\in\Gamma_0(Y_i)\).
Each \(K_i:X\to Y_i\) is bounded linear.
A Fenchel qualification holds when strong duality and attainment are asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The multi-composite objective equals the displayed saddle formulation, with componentwise primal-dual optimality inclusions.

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugate of the ith component function.
Hilbert adjoint of the ith coupling operator.

children.title: Product-Space Saddle Lifts
children.top_down_role: Lifted saddle formulations organized in replicated or block product spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Product-Space Saddle Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-space lift converting componentwise couplings into one block operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m<\infty\), let \(X,Y_1,\ldots,Y_m\) be real Hilbert spaces, let \(f\in\Gamma_0(X)\), and let \(g_i\in\Gamma_0(Y_i)\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). Form \(\mathcal Y=Y_1\oplus\cdots\oplus Y_m\) with its canonical inner product. Given bounded linear operators \(K_i:X\to Y_i\), define \(K:X\to\mathcal Y\) by \(Kx=(K_1x,\ldots,K_mx)\), and define \(G:\mathcal Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) by \(G(y)=\sum_{i=1}^m g_i(y_i)\). Then
\[\sum_{i=1}^m g_i(K_i x)=G(Kx),\qquad G^*(v)=\sum_{i=1}^m g_i^*(v_i),\qquad K^*v=\sum_{i=1}^mK_i^*v_i.\]
Consequently, the componentwise saddle expression is identical to the two-block product-space expression
\[\inf_{x\in X}\sup_{v\in\mathcal Y}\bigl(f(x)+\langle Kx,v\rangle-G^*(v)\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stacking the component spaces, operators, functions, and dual variables converts the finite multi-operator saddle expression into an identical two-block saddle expression on a product Hilbert space.
assumptions_latex: \(m<\infty\) and \(\mathcal Y\) has the canonical product Hilbert structure.
\(f\in\Gamma_0(X)\) and \(g_i\in\Gamma_0(Y_i)\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,m\).
Each \(K_i:X\to Y_i\) is bounded linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The componentwise saddle model is identical to the single block-operator saddle model on \(X\times\mathcal Y\).

notation.meaning: Hilbert direct sum of the component dual spaces.

children.title: Component Coupling Geometry
children.top_down_role: Coupling patterns linking the exposed primal or dual components.

knowledge_statements.title: Component Coupling Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm and adjoint geometry of a finite stacked linear coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K_i:X\to Y_i\) be bounded linear and equip \(\mathcal Y=\bigoplus_{i=1}^mY_i\) with the weighted inner product \(\langle y,v\rangle_{\mathcal Y}=\sum_{i=1}^m\omega_i\langle y_i,v_i\rangle\), where \(\omega_i>0\). For \(Kx=(K_i x)_{i=1}^m\),
\[\|Kx\|_{\mathcal Y}^2=\sum_{i=1}^m\omega_i\|K_i x\|^2,\qquad K^*y=\sum_{i=1}^m\omega_iK_i^*y_i,\]
and
\[\|K\|^2=\left\|\sum_{i=1}^m\omega_iK_i^*K_i\right\|\leq\sum_{i=1}^m\omega_i\|K_i\|^2.\]
Thus the aggregate coupling geometry, including admissible scalar step-size bounds based on \(\|K\|\), is governed by the positive operator \(\sum_i\omega_iK_i^*K_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stacked coupling’s adjoint and norm are determined by a weighted sum of component adjoints and Gram operators, which controls aggregate step-size restrictions.
assumptions_latex: \(m<\infty\) and \(\omega_i>0\).
Each \(K_i:X\to Y_i\) is bounded linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K^*y=\sum_i\omega_iK_i^*y_i\) and \(\|K\|^2=\|\sum_i\omega_iK_i^*K_i\|\leq\sum_i\omega_i\|K_i\|^2\).

children.title: Primal-Dual Optimality Inclusions
children.top_down_role: Coupled primal and dual optimality systems represented as a single inclusion.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Optimality Inclusions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single product-space inclusion encoding the optimality system of a composite saddle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\in\Gamma_0(X)\), \(g\in\Gamma_0(Y)\), and let \(K:X\to Y\) be bounded linear. On \(X\oplus Y\), define
\[\mathcal A(x,y)=\partial f(x)\times\partial g^*(y),\qquad \mathcal S(x,y)=(K^*y,-Kx).\]
Then the coupled saddle conditions
\[0\in\partial f(x)+K^*y,\qquad 0\in\partial g^*(y)-Kx\]
are equivalent to the single inclusion
\[0\in(\mathcal A+\mathcal S)(x,y).\]
Here \(\mathcal A\) is maximally monotone, while \(\mathcal S\) is bounded linear and skew-adjoint; consequently \(\langle z,\mathcal Sz\rangle=0\) for every \(z\in X\oplus Y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The two saddle optimality conditions combine into one product-space zero involving a block-diagonal subdifferential and a skew linear coupling.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in\Gamma_0(X)\) and \(g\in\Gamma_0(Y)\).
\(K:X\to Y\) is bounded linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal-dual system is equivalent to \(0\in(\mathcal A+\mathcal S)(x,y)\), with \(\mathcal A\) maximally monotone and \(\mathcal S^*=-\mathcal S\).

children.title: Linearly Composed Monotone Inclusions
children.top_down_role: Inclusions connected through a linear operator and its adjoint.

knowledge_statements.title: Linearly Composed Monotone Inclusions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual representation of a monotone inclusion containing a linear composition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A:X\rightrightarrows X\) and \(B:Y\rightrightarrows Y\) be maximally monotone, and let \(K:X\to Y\) be bounded linear. The linearly composed primal inclusion is
\[0\in Ax+K^*B(Kx).\]
A primal-dual pair \((\bar x,\bar y)\) solves its extended system when
\[-K^*\bar y\in A\bar x,\qquad K\bar x\in B^{-1}\bar y,\]
equivalently,
\[0\in A\bar x+K^*\bar y,\qquad 0\in B^{-1}\bar y-K\bar x.\]
Every such pair yields a primal solution. Conversely, a primal solution admits such a dual variable whenever the defining membership in \(K^*B(K\bar x)\) is attained by some \(\bar y\in B(K\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A monotone inclusion containing a linear composition expands into coupled primal and dual inclusions linked by an operator and its adjoint.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(B\) are maximally monotone.
\(K:X\to Y\) is bounded linear.
Dual existence is asserted only when a realizing \(\bar y\in B(K\bar x)\) exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The extended primal-dual system implies \(0\in A\bar x+K^*B(K\bar x)\), with the stated converse under dual-variable attainment.

children.title: Skew Product-Space Inclusions
children.top_down_role: Lifted inclusions that isolate primal-dual coupling in a skew component.

knowledge_statements.title: Skew Product-Space Inclusions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block decomposition isolating linear primal-dual interaction as a skew operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For maximally monotone \(A:X\rightrightarrows X\), \(B:Y\rightrightarrows Y\), and bounded linear \(K:X\to Y\), define on \(\mathcal H=X\oplus Y\)
\[\mathcal M(x,y)=Ax\times B^{-1}y,\qquad \mathcal S(x,y)=(K^*y,-Kx).\]
Then
\[0\in(\mathcal M+\mathcal S)(x,y)\]
is exactly the pair of inclusions
\[0\in Ax+K^*y,\qquad 0\in B^{-1}y-Kx.\]
Moreover, \(\mathcal S^*=-\mathcal S\), so \(\mathcal S\) is monotone because \(\langle z,\mathcal Sz\rangle=0\), and \(\mathcal M\) is maximally monotone. This decomposition separates the componentwise resolvent structure in \(\mathcal M\) from all cross-space coupling in \(\mathcal S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A product-space lift separates blockwise maximal monotone terms from the linear interaction, which appears as a bounded skew-adjoint operator.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(B\) are maximally monotone on real Hilbert spaces.
\(K:X\to Y\) is bounded linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coupled inclusions equal \(0\in(\mathcal M+\mathcal S)(x,y)\), where \(\mathcal M\) is maximally monotone and \(\mathcal S\) is skew-adjoint.

children.title: Partial-Inverse Inclusions
children.top_down_role: Inclusion representations organized around partial-inverse constructions.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Inverse Inclusions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spingarn partial inverse of an operator relative to a closed vector subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(V\subset H\) be a closed vector subspace, and let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\). The partial inverse of \(A\) with respect to \(V\) is the relation \(A_V:H\rightrightarrows H\) defined by
\[y\in A_Vx\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad P_Vy+P_{V^\perp}x\in A\bigl(P_Vx+P_{V^\perp}y\bigr).\]
Equivalently, the transformation from \(\operatorname{gra}A\) to \(\operatorname{gra}A_V\) exchanges the \(V^\perp\)-components of the argument and value while retaining their \(V\)-components. If \(A\) is maximally monotone, then \(A_V\) is maximally monotone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The partial inverse swaps the orthogonal-complement components of an operator’s graph variables while preserving their subspace components; maximal monotonicity is retained.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a closed vector subspace of the real Hilbert space \(H\).
\(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximally monotone when preservation of maximal monotonicity is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\in A_Vx\) exactly under the displayed projection relation, and maximal monotonicity of \(A\) implies maximal monotonicity of \(A_V\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed Spingarn partial-inverse definition and maximal-monotonicity preservation claim are mathematically standard, but the record supplies no citation. An authoritative definition and theorem locator are required.

children.title: Constraint-Splitting Inclusions
children.top_down_role: Inclusion representations isolating constraint operators from other components.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Splitting Inclusions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal-cone splitting of a monotone inclusion constrained to a closed subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(V\subset H\) be a closed vector subspace, and let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\). The subspace-constrained inclusion
\[0\in Ax+N_Vx\]
is equivalent to finding \((x,u)\in V\times V^\perp\) such that
\[-u\in Ax.\]
Indeed, for \(x\in V\), the normal cone satisfies \(N_Vx=V^\perp\), while \(N_Vx=\varnothing\) for \(x\notin V\). Hence the constraint and the operator membership can be handled as distinct components. With the partial inverse convention
\[y\in A_Vx\Longleftrightarrow P_Vy+P_{V^\perp}x\in A(P_Vx+P_{V^\perp}y),\]
the pair condition is also equivalent to \(0\in A_V(x-u)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subspace-constrained zero separates into a feasible primal point and an orthogonal multiplier; the pair can also be encoded as a partial-inverse zero.
assumptions_latex: \(V\subset H\) is a closed vector subspace.
\(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is a set-valued operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in Ax+N_Vx\) is equivalent to the existence of \(u\in V^\perp\) with \(x\in V\) and \(-u\in Ax\), equivalently \(0\in A_V(x-u)\).

notation.meaning: Partial inverse of A with respect to V.

children.title: Subspace Coupling Interface
children.top_down_role: Structural interaction between subspace constraints and the remaining inclusion components.

knowledge_statements.title: Subspace Coupling Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal projection interface separating feasible and multiplier components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space and \(V\subset H\) a closed vector subspace. Every \(z\in H\) has the unique decomposition
\[z=P_Vz+P_{V^\perp}z,\qquad P_VP_{V^\perp}=0,\qquad P_V+P_{V^\perp}=I.\]
For a set-valued operator \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\), a pair \((x,u)\) satisfies the subspace coupling interface precisely when
\[x=P_Vx,\qquad u=P_{V^\perp}u,\qquad -u\in Ax.\]
Equivalently, writing \(z=x-u\), the interface variables are recovered without ambiguity as
\[x=P_Vz,-u=P_{V^\perp}z,\]
and they certify \(0\in Ax+N_Vx\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Orthogonal projections uniquely encode the feasible primal component and its orthogonal multiplier, providing an interface between operator evaluation and subspace enforcement.
assumptions_latex: \(V\subset H\) is a closed vector subspace.
\(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is a set-valued operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projection identities uniquely recover \((x,u)\in V\times V^\perp\) from \(z=x-u\), and \(-u\in Ax\) certifies the constrained inclusion.

children.title: Fenchel-Rockafellar Dualization
children.top_down_role: Conjugate-based dualization of composite objectives with linear mappings.

knowledge_statements.title: Fenchel-Rockafellar Dualization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional composite convex duality under a relative-interior qualification and finite primal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X,Y\) be finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, let \(K:X\to Y\) be linear, and let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, convex functions. Suppose \(0\in\operatorname{ri}(K\operatorname{dom}f-\operatorname{dom}g)\) and \(\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+g(Kx)\}\in\mathbb R\). Then
\[
\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+g(Kx)\}=\max_{y\in Y}\{-f^*(-K^*y)-g^*(y)\}.
\]
A primal-dual pair \((x^*,y^*)\) is optimal precisely when its objective values are finite and \(-K^*y^*\in\partial f(x^*)\) and \(Kx^*\in\partial g^*(y^*)\), equivalently \(y^*\in\partial g(Kx^*)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the relative-interior qualification and a finite primal value, the composite convex problem and its conjugate dual have equal optimal values, the dual optimum is attained, and optimal pairs satisfy the stated subgradient inclusions.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
\(K:X\to Y\) is linear between finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces.
\(0\in\operatorname{ri}(K\operatorname{dom}f-\operatorname{dom}g)\).
\(\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+g(Kx)\}\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+g(Kx)\}=\max_{y\in Y}\{-f^*(-K^*y)-g^*(y)\}\), with the stated primal-dual optimality inclusions.

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugate of a proper convex function h

knowledge_statements.title: Attouch-Théra Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attouch-Théra dual inclusion and its coupled Kuhn-Tucker pairs for a sum of maximally monotone operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space and let \(A,B:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximally monotone. Define \(B^{-\oplus}=(-\operatorname{Id})\circ B^{-1}\circ(-\operatorname{Id})\). The Attouch-Théra primal and dual inclusions are
\[
0\in Ax+Bx
\quad\text{and}\quad
0\in A^{-1}u+B^{-\oplus}u.
\]
Define the associated Kuhn-Tucker set by
\[
\mathcal K=\{(x,u)\in H\times H:u\in Ax\text{ and }-u\in Bx\}.
\]
Every \((x,u)\in\mathcal K\) has \(x\) solving the primal inclusion and \(u\) solving the dual inclusion. Conversely, a primal solution \(x\) and dual solution \(u\) form an associated pair exactly when \((x,u)\in\mathcal K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An associated Attouch-Théra primal-dual pair consists of a primal zero and a dual zero coupled by opposing values of the two operators.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space.
\(A,B:H\rightrightarrows H\) are maximally monotone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \((x,u)\in\mathcal K\), then \(0\in Ax+Bx\) and \(0\in A^{-1}u+B^{-\oplus}u\); the coupling is characterized by \(u\in Ax\) and \(-u\in Bx\).

notation.meaning: reflected inverse operator, equal to minus the inverse of B evaluated at the negated argument
Attouch-Théra Kuhn-Tucker set of associated primal-dual pairs

children.title: Augmented-Lagrangian Dualization
children.top_down_role: Dual representations underlying multiplier and alternating-direction methods.

knowledge_statements.title: Augmented-Lagrangian Dualization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained convex representation underlying multiplier and alternating-direction methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X,Z,Y\) be finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Z\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, convex functions, and let \(A:X\to Y\) and \(B:Z\to Y\) be linear. Consider
\[
p^*=\inf_{x\in X,\,z\in Z}\{f(x)+g(z):Ax+Bz=c\}.
\]
Assume \(p^*\in\mathbb R\) and that some feasible \((x,z)\) belongs to \(\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\times\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g)\). For \(\rho>0\), define
\[
L_\rho(x,z,y)=f(x)+g(z)+\langle y,Ax+Bz-c\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Ax+Bz-c\rVert^2
\]
and \(d_\rho(y)=\inf_{x\in X,\,z\in Z}L_\rho(x,z,y)\). If \(d_0\) denotes the ordinary Lagrange dual function, then
\[
\sup_{y\in Y}d_\rho(y)=\sup_{y\in Y}d_0(y)=p^*.
\]
Alternating minimization of \(L_\rho\) in the two primal blocks followed by multiplier ascent gives the standard ADMM update architecture.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under an explicit convex qualification, the augmented and ordinary Lagrangian duals have the same optimal value as the equality-constrained primal problem; blockwise augmented-Lagrangian minimization leads to the ADMM architecture.
assumptions_latex: \(X,Z,Y\) are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces.
\(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
\(A\) and \(B\) are linear and \(p^*\in\mathbb R\).
There is a feasible \((x,z)\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\times\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{y\in Y}d_\rho(y)=\sup_{y\in Y}d_0(y)=p^*\).

notation.meaning: augmented Lagrangian with penalty parameter rho

children.title: Variable-Copy Lifts
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary-variable representations that replicate coupled decision variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Copy Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact lifting by local copies joined through equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional vector space and let \(f_i:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). The shared-variable problem
\[
\min_{x\in X}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x)
\]
has the exact lifted representation
\[
\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_m,z\in X}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)
\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_i=z\ \text{for every }i.
\]
Projection of any feasible lifted point onto \(z\) gives an original feasible point with the same objective value, and copying any original point into every \(x_i\) gives a lifted feasible point. Hence the optimal values and minimizers correspond under copying and projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sum sharing one variable can be separated into local variable copies constrained to equal a common coordinator, without changing solutions or objective values.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite-dimensional.
Each \(f_i:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is an extended-real objective term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original and lifted problems have equal optimal values, and their minimizers correspond through \(x_i=z=x\).

notation.meaning: local copy used by objective term i

children.title: Consensus Constraint Lifts
children.top_down_role: Lifted representations using agreement constraints between variable copies.

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus Constraint Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear consensus-subspace formulation of equality among local decision variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(m\ge 2\), let \(\mathbf{x}=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in X^m\) and define the consensus subspace
\[
\mathcal C=\{\mathbf{x}\in X^m:x_1=\cdots=x_m\}.
\]
For functions \(f_i:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), the consensus lift is
\[
\min_{\mathbf{x}\in X^m}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)+\delta_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf{x}).
\]
It is equivalent to minimizing \(\sum_i f_i(x)\) over one shared \(x\). More generally, if a linear map \(D:X^m\to W\) satisfies \(\ker D=\mathcal C\), then the indicator term can be replaced by the constraint \(D\mathbf{x}=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consensus is imposed by restricting all local copies to the diagonal subspace, equivalently by a linear constraint whose nullspace is exactly that subspace.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional vector space and \(m\ge2\).
\(D\) is linear with \(\ker D=\mathcal C\) when the linear form is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbf{x}\in\mathcal C\iff x_1=\cdots=x_m\), and the consensus lift is equivalent to the shared-variable problem.

notation.meaning: diagonal consensus subspace of the product space
indicator function of the consensus subspace

children.title: Graph-Based Copying Structures
children.top_down_role: Copying patterns indexed by graph incidence or local neighborhood structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Graph-Based Copying Structures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus encoded by the incidence operator of a connected undirected graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph with an arbitrarily oriented incidence matrix \(B_G\in\mathbb R^{|E|\times|V|}\), and let \(\mathbf{x}=(x_i)_{i\in V}\in X^{|V|}\). Edgewise equality of neighboring copies is
\[
(B_G\otimes I_X)\mathbf{x}=0.
\]
If \(G\) is connected, then \(\ker(B_G\otimes I_X)=\{\mathbf{1}\otimes x:x\in X\}\); hence edge constraints enforce global consensus. If \(G\) is disconnected, the nullspace instead permits one independent value per connected component, so edgewise equality does not enforce global consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incidence constraints enforce equality along edges; they imply one global shared value exactly when the underlying undirected graph is connected.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite undirected graph with an oriented incidence matrix.
\(X\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Connectedness gives \(\ker(B_G\otimes I_X)=\{\mathbf 1\otimes x:x\in X\}\); disconnectedness yields componentwise rather than global consensus.

notation.meaning: oriented vertex-edge incidence matrix of G
product-space vector having value x at every vertex

children.title: Arrow-Hurwicz Methods
children.top_down_role: Classical simultaneous and alternating primal-dual gradient architectures.

knowledge_statements.title: Arrow-Hurwicz Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected simultaneous descent-ascent for a differentiable convex-concave saddle problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given nonempty closed convex sets \(X\) and \(Y\), a differentiable function \(L:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\) convex in \(x\) and concave in \(y\), initial \((x^0,y^0)\in X\times Y\), and steps \(\tau_k,\sigma_k>0\), the Arrow-Hurwicz iteration is
\[
x^{k+1}=P_X\bigl(x^k-\tau_k\nabla_xL(x^k,y^k)\bigr),\qquad
y^{k+1}=P_Y\bigl(y^k+\sigma_k\nabla_yL(x^k,y^k)\bigr).
\]
Stop when a prescribed saddle residual or iterate-change tolerance is met, and return the last iterate or a declared ergodic average. The two signs implement primal descent and dual ascent at the same current pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arrow-Hurwicz simultaneously takes a projected gradient-descent step in the primal variable and a projected gradient-ascent step in the dual variable.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are nonempty closed convex subsets of finite-dimensional inner-product spaces.
\(L\) is differentiable, convex in its first argument, and concave in its second.
\(\tau_k,\sigma_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed projected descent-ascent recurrence defines the Arrow-Hurwicz iterates and stated output convention.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto a closed convex set C

children.title: Uzawa Methods
children.top_down_role: Classical saddle methods centered on primal subproblem resolution with multiplier evolution.

knowledge_statements.title: Uzawa Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact primal Lagrangian minimization followed by multiplier ascent for affine equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a nonempty closed convex subset of a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, and consider
\[
\min_{x\in X}f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,
\]
where \(A\) is linear. Define \(L(x,y)=f(x)+\langle y,Ax-b\rangle\). Given \(y^0\) and steps \(\alpha_k>0\), the classical Uzawa iteration chooses
\[
x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}L(x,y^k),
\qquad
y^{k+1}=y^k+\alpha_k(Ax^{k+1}-b).
\]
The iteration requires the displayed primal minimizer to exist at each current multiplier. A declared feasibility and multiplier-step tolerance may be used as a stopping rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For affine equality constraints, Uzawa exactly minimizes the Lagrangian in the primal variable and then ascends in the multiplier using the resulting constraint residual.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex in a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.
\(f\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(A\) is linear and the displayed primal minimizer exists at every iteration.
\(\alpha_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed primal minimization and update \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\alpha_k(Ax^{k+1}-b)\) define the classical equality-constrained Uzawa iteration.

children.title: Dual-Ascent Methods
children.top_down_role: Multiplier-based methods viewed through ascent on a dual objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Ascent Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Supergradient ascent on the concave Lagrange dual function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(L(x,y)=f(x)+\langle y,Ax-b\rangle\), define \(d(y)=\inf_{x\in X}L(x,y)\). Given \(y^0\) and \(\alpha_k>0\), compute
\[
x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}L(x,y^k),
\qquad s^k=Ax^{k+1}-b,
\qquad y^{k+1}=y^k+\alpha_k s^k.
\]
Then \(s^k\in\partial^+d(y^k)\), where \(\partial^+\) denotes the concave superdifferential. If multipliers must lie in a closed convex set \(Y\), use \(y^{k+1}=P_Y(y^k+\alpha_k s^k)\). Stop using a declared dual or feasibility tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual ascent maximizes the concave dual function using a constraint residual obtained from a Lagrangian-minimizing primal response as a supergradient.
assumptions_latex: The Lagrangian infimum is attained at each current multiplier.
\(d\) is the concave dual function and \(\alpha_k>0\).
The multiplier set is all space or a specified nonempty closed convex set \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s^k=Ax^{k+1}-b\in\partial^+d(y^k)\), so the multiplier recurrence is a supergradient-ascent step on \(d\).

notation.meaning: dual supergradient given by the constraint residual

children.title: Uzawa–Dual-Ascent Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Representational links between Uzawa architectures and dual-ascent interpretations.

knowledge_statements.title: Uzawa–Dual-Ascent Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identification of the Uzawa multiplier update with dual supergradient ascent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(d(y)=\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\langle y,Ax-b\rangle\}\), and suppose \(x(y)\) attains the infimum. Then
\[
Ax(y)-b\in\partial^+d(y).
\]
Consequently, the Uzawa updates
\[
x^{k+1}=x(y^k),\qquad y^{k+1}=y^k+\alpha_k(Ax^{k+1}-b)
\]
are exactly supergradient-ascent updates for maximizing the concave dual function \(d\). With constrained multipliers, projected Uzawa is projected dual ascent. Thus the two descriptions differ only in whether the primal-response step or the induced dual supergradient is emphasized.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The residual generated by Uzawa’s primal minimization is a dual supergradient, making Uzawa exactly dual ascent, or projected dual ascent for constrained multipliers.
assumptions_latex: The Lagrangian infimum defining \(d(y)\) is attained at \(x(y)\).
The equality constraint is affine and \(\alpha_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Uzawa multiplier recurrence coincides with supergradient ascent on \(d\), with projection when multipliers are constrained.

notation.meaning: a Lagrangian-minimizing primal response at multiplier y
superdifferential of the concave dual function

children.title: Extragradient Saddle Methods
children.top_down_role: Predictor-corrector methods for monotone saddle operators.

knowledge_statements.title: Extragradient Saddle Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-evaluation predictor-corrector method for a monotone Lipschitz saddle operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space, let \(Z\subseteq H\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(F:Z\to H\) be monotone and \(L\)-Lipschitz, where \(L>0\). Given \(z^0\in Z\) and \(0<\gamma<1/L\), compute
\[
\widehat z^k=P_Z\bigl(z^k-\gamma F(z^k)\bigr),
\qquad
z^{k+1}=P_Z\bigl(z^k-\gamma F(\widehat z^k)\bigr).
\]
For a differentiable convex-concave saddle function \(\mathcal L(x,y)\), take \(z=(x,y)\) and \(F(z)=(\nabla_x\mathcal L(x,y),-\nabla_y\mathcal L(x,y))\). A prescribed variational-inequality residual may be used as a stopping rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extragradient predicts a projected point, reevaluates the ambient-space monotone saddle operator there, and corrects from the original iterate using the new evaluation.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space and \(Z\subseteq H\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(F:Z\to H\) is monotone and \(L\)-Lipschitz for some \(L>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed predictor-corrector recurrence defines the extragradient method for the associated variational inequality or saddle operator.

notation.meaning: monotone variational-inequality or saddle operator with values in the ambient space

children.title: Baseline PDHG
children.top_down_role: The canonical two-sided proximal method for bilinearly coupled saddle models.

knowledge_statements.title: Baseline PDHG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical Chambolle-Pock iteration with full primal extrapolation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X,Y\) be finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces, let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, convex functions, and let \(K:X\to Y\) be linear. The composite problem has the saddle representation
\[
\min_{x\in X}\{f(x)+g(Kx)\}=\min_{x\in X}\sup_{y\in Y}\{f(x)+\langle Kx,y\rangle-g^*(y)\}.
\]
Assume that the saddle problem has a saddle point. Choose \(\tau,\sigma>0\) with \(\tau\sigma\lVert K\rVert^2<1\), initialize \(x^0\in X\), \(y^0\in Y\), and \(\bar x^0=x^0\), and iterate
\[
y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma g^*}(y^k+\sigma K\bar x^k),
\]
\[
x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau f}(x^k-\tau K^*y^{k+1}),
\qquad
\bar x^{k+1}=2x^{k+1}-x^k.
\]
A prescribed primal-dual residual or gap tolerance may be used as a stopping rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Baseline PDHG applies a dual proximal step, a primal proximal step, and full primal extrapolation to the Fenchel saddle representation, with step sizes controlled by the operator norm.
assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces.
\(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
\(K:X\to Y\) is linear and the saddle problem has a saddle point.
\(\tau,\sigma>0\) and \(\tau\sigma\lVert K\rVert^2<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed dual-proximal, primal-proximal, and extrapolation updates define baseline PDHG for the composite Fenchel saddle model.

notation.meaning: proximal mapping of lambda times h

children.title: Relaxed PDHG
children.top_down_role: PDHG variants governed by relaxation of the primal-dual transition.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed PDHG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Krasnosel'skii–Mann relaxation applied after a complete Euclidean PDHG sweep.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the saddle problem \(\min_x\max_y f(x)+\langle Kx,y\rangle-g^*(y)\), choose \(\tau,\sigma>0\), extrapolation \(\theta\in[0,1]\), and relaxation \(\rho_k\in(0,1]\). Initialize \(x^0,y^0\) and set \(\bar x^0=x^0\). Given \((x^k,y^k,\bar x^k)\), compute
\[\widehat y=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma g^*}(y^k+\sigma K\bar x^k),\qquad \widehat x=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau f}(x^k-\tau K^*\widehat y),\]
then set
\[x^{k+1}=x^k+\rho_k(\widehat x-x^k),\quad y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho_k(\widehat y-y^k),\quad \bar x^{k+1}=x^{k+1}+\theta(x^{k+1}-x^k).\]
Stop when a prescribed primal-dual residual tolerance holds and return \((x^{k+1},y^{k+1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxed PDHG forms a complete provisional PDHG update, then averages both provisional variables with the current iterate before constructing the next extrapolated primal point.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, lower-semicontinuous convex functions on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
\(K\) is linear and \(\tau\sigma\lVert K\rVert^2<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x^{k+1},y^{k+1})\) is the relaxed PDHG iterate produced by the displayed sweep.

children.title: Extrapolated PDHG
children.top_down_role: PDHG variants using extrapolated primal or dual quantities.

knowledge_statements.title: Extrapolated PDHG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal extrapolation used as the argument of the subsequent dual proximal step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, let \(K:X\to Y\) be linear, and consider
\[\min_{x\in X}\max_{y\in Y} f(x)+\langle Kx,y\rangle-g^*(y).\]
Choose \(\tau,\sigma>0\) and \(\theta\in[0,1]\), initialize \(x^0\in X\) and \(y^0\in Y\), and set \(\bar x^0=x^0\). For \(k\ge 0\), compute
\[y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma g^*}(y^k+\sigma K\bar x^k),\qquad x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau f}(x^k-\tau K^*y^{k+1}),\]
\[\bar x^{k+1}=x^{k+1}+\theta(x^{k+1}-x^k).\]
The auxiliary point \(\bar x^{k+1}\) is used in the next dual update, while the reported primal-dual iterate is \((x^{k+1},y^{k+1})\). Stop when a prescribed primal-dual residual or gap criterion is satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extrapolated PDHG feeds a linear prediction of the new primal iterate into the next dual proximal update while retaining the unextrapolated point as the reported primal variable.
assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper, lower-semicontinuous convex functions.
\(K:X\to Y\) is linear and \(\tau\sigma\lVert K\rVert^2<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed recursion defines the primal-extrapolated Chambolle–Pock PDHG sequence \((x^k,y^k)\).

children.title: Relaxation–Extrapolation Placement
children.top_down_role: Architectural choices determining where relaxation or extrapolation enters the method.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation–Extrapolation Placement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes outer relaxation from extrapolation inside a sequential PDHG sweep.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Z\) be the state space of an ordered PDHG sweep and let \(P:Z\to Z\) denote the complete sweep map. For \(\rho\in\mathbb R\), define its outer relaxation by
\[R_\rho=(1-\rho)I+\rho P.\]
For primal iterates in a Hilbert space \(X\), define
\[E_\theta(x^k,x^{k-1})=x^k+\theta(x^k-x^{k-1}).\]
In primal-extrapolated PDHG, \(E_\theta(x^k,x^{k-1})\) is formed before the dual proximal evaluation and changes its argument:
\[y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma g^*}\!\left(y^k+\sigma K E_\theta(x^k,x^{k-1})\right).\]
By contrast, outer relaxation is applied after the complete sweep:
\[z^{k+1}=R_\rho(z^k)=z^k+\rho\bigl(P(z^k)-z^k\bigr).\]
Because proximal maps are generally nonlinear, inserting extrapolation before a proximal evaluation and averaging the completed sweep generally define different update maps; equality requires additional special structure or degenerate parameter choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extrapolation modifies an input inside the PDHG sweep, whereas outer relaxation averages the completed sweep with the current state; because proximal maps are generally nonlinear, these placements are generally inequivalent.
assumptions_latex: \(P:Z\to Z\) is a fixed ordered PDHG update map on a vector space \(Z\).
\(K:X\to Y\) is linear, and the displayed proximal map and parameters \(\rho\), \(\theta\), and \(\sigma\) are well-defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: In general, internal extrapolation and post-sweep relaxation are not interchangeable operations.

notation.meaning: one complete ordered PDHG sweep map
complete PDHG state before the k-th sweep

children.title: Preconditioned PDHG
children.top_down_role: PDHG variants using nontrivial primal or dual preconditioners.

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioned PDHG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: PDHG in fixed positive-definite primal and dual metrics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, let \(K:X\to Y\) be linear, and consider
\[\min_{x\in X}\max_{y\in Y} f(x)+\langle Kx,y\rangle-g^*(y).\]
Let \(T:X\to X\) and \(S:Y\to Y\) be self-adjoint positive-definite operators. Initialize \(x^0\in X\) and \(y^0\in Y\), set \(\bar x^0=x^0\), and choose \(\theta\in[0,1]\). For \(k\ge0\), compute
\[y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}^{S^{-1}}_{g^*}(y^k+SK\bar x^k),\qquad x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}^{T^{-1}}_f(x^k-TK^*y^{k+1}),\]
\[\bar x^{k+1}=x^{k+1}+\theta(x^{k+1}-x^k).\]
For a positive-definite operator \(M\), the metric proximal map is
\[\operatorname{prox}^{M}_q(v)=\underset{u}{\operatorname{argmin}}\;\left\{q(u)+\tfrac12\lVert u-v\rVert_M^2\right\}.\]
Stop at a prescribed residual tolerance and return \((x^{k+1},y^{k+1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preconditioned PDHG replaces scalar step sizes by positive-definite primal and dual metric operators and evaluates the corresponding metric proximal maps.
assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper, lower-semicontinuous convex functions.
\(T:X\to X\) and \(S:Y\to Y\) are self-adjoint and positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed recursion is a fixed-metric preconditioned PDHG iteration on \(X\times Y\).

notation.meaning: proximal map in the metric induced by M
metric squared norm equal to the inner product of Mw with w

children.title: Diagonally Scaled PDHG
children.top_down_role: PDHG variants using coordinatewise or block-diagonal scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagonally Scaled PDHG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise specialization of fixed-metric preconditioned PDHG.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\mathbb R^n\), \(Y=\mathbb R^m\), and let \(K:X\to Y\) be linear. Choose
\[T=\operatorname{diag}(t_1,\ldots,t_n),\qquad S=\operatorname{diag}(s_1,\ldots,s_m),\]
with \(t_j>0\) for every \(j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(s_i>0\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\). For
\[\min_{x\in X}\max_{y\in Y} f(x)+\langle Kx,y\rangle-g^*(y),\]
choose \(\theta\in[0,1]\), initialize \(x^0\in X\) and \(y^0\in Y\), and set \(\bar x^0=x^0\). For \(k\ge0\), compute
\[y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}^{S^{-1}}_{g^*}(y^k+SK\bar x^k),\qquad x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}^{T^{-1}}_f(x^k-TK^*y^{k+1}),\]
\[\bar x^{k+1}=x^{k+1}+\theta(x^{k+1}-x^k).\]
Require
\[\lVert S^{1/2}KT^{1/2}\rVert<1.\]
Stop using a prescribed residual criterion and return the current primal-dual pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonally scaled PDHG assigns separate positive scales to each primal and dual coordinate while imposing the usual metric compatibility condition on the linearly coupled variables.
assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper, lower-semicontinuous convex functions.
\(K:X\to Y\) is linear.
Every diagonal entry of \(T\) and \(S\) is strictly positive, and \(\lVert S^{1/2}KT^{1/2}\rVert<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed method is the diagonal-metric specialization of preconditioned PDHG on \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\).

notation.meaning: positive scale of primal coordinate j
positive scale of dual coordinate i
proximal map in the metric induced by M

children.title: Block-Metric Scaling Regimes
children.top_down_role: Metric choices adapted to heterogeneous block and coupling scales.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Metric Scaling Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissibility condition for block-diagonal primal and dual PDHG metrics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\bigoplus_{j=1}^pX_j\), \(Y=\bigoplus_{i=1}^qY_i\), and let \(K_{ij}:X_j\to Y_i\) be the blocks of \(K\). A fixed block-metric scaling regime consists of
\[T=\operatorname{diag}(T_1,\ldots,T_p),\qquad S=\operatorname{diag}(S_1,\ldots,S_q),\]
where every \(T_j\) and \(S_i\) is self-adjoint positive definite. It is strictly PDHG-admissible when
\[\lVert S^{1/2}KT^{1/2}\rVert<1,\]
equivalently when the block operator
\[\begin{pmatrix}T^{-1}&-K^*\\-K&S^{-1}\end{pmatrix}\]
is positive definite. Under this predicate, the primal and dual block metrics jointly dominate the coupling induced by \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block metrics are admissible when all blocks are positive definite and their joint scaling makes the normalized coupling operator have norm below one.
assumptions_latex: The decompositions of \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite orthogonal direct sums.
\(K\) is bounded and linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The norm inequality and positive-definite block-operator test characterize the same strict fixed-metric regime.

notation.meaning: coupling from primal block j to dual block i

children.title: Accelerated PDHG
children.top_down_role: PDHG variants adapted to one-sided or two-sided curvature regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Accelerated PDHG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chambolle–Pock acceleration under strong convexity of the primal proximable term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(f\) is \(\gamma\)-strongly convex with \(\gamma>0\). Initialize \(x^0,y^0\), set \(\bar x^0=x^0\), and choose \(\tau_0,\sigma_0>0\) with \(\tau_0\sigma_0\lVert K\rVert^2<1\). For \(k\ge0\), compute
\[y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma_k g^*}(y^k+\sigma_kK\bar x^k),\qquad x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau_k f}(x^k-\tau_kK^*y^{k+1}),\]
then set
\[\theta_k=(1+2\gamma\tau_k)^{-1/2},\quad \tau_{k+1}=\theta_k\tau_k,\quad \sigma_{k+1}=\sigma_k/\theta_k,\quad \bar x^{k+1}=x^{k+1}+\theta_k(x^{k+1}-x^k).\]
Return the current primal-dual pair when the stopping criterion holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong primal curvature permits coordinated shrinking of primal steps, enlargement of dual steps, and varying extrapolation in an accelerated PDHG recursion.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, lower-semicontinuous convex functions.
A saddle point exists for \(f(x)+\langle Kx,y\rangle-g^*(y)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed variable-parameter recursion is the one-sided strongly convex accelerated PDHG scheme.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact PDHG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: PDHG with summably controlled residuals in both proximal subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the saddle problem \(\min_x\max_y f(x)+\langle Kx,y\rangle-g^*(y)\), choose \(\tau,[σ>0\), \(\theta\in[0,1]\), initialize \(x^0,y^0\), and set \(\bar x^0=x^0\). Select \(y^{k+1}\) and \(x^{k+1}\) satisfying
\[e_y^{k+1}\in \partial g^*(y^{k+1})+\sigma^{-1}(y^{k+1}-y^k)-K\bar x^k,\]
\[e_x^{k+1}\in \partial f(x^{k+1})+\tau^{-1}(x^{k+1}-x^k)+K^*y^{k+1},\]
then set \(\bar x^{k+1}=x^{k+1}+\theta(x^{k+1}-x^k)\). Require \(\sum_k(\lVert e_x^{k+1}\rVert+\lVert e_y^{k+1}\rVert)<\infty\). Stop at the prescribed outer residual tolerance and return \((x^{k+1},y^{k+1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inexact PDHG permits approximate proximal solves whose optimality-inclusion residuals are absolutely summable across iterations.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, lower-semicontinuous convex functions.
\(K\) is linear and \(\tau\sigma\lVert K\rVert^2<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inclusions define a summable-residual inexact PDHG iteration.

children.title: Condat-Vũ Splitting
children.top_down_role: Primal-dual forward-backward splitting for smooth, proximable, and linearly composed components.

knowledge_statements.title: Condat-Vũ Splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional primal-dual forward-backward splitting for one smooth and two proximable convex terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, let \(K:X\to Y\) be linear, and consider
\[\min_{x\in X} f(x)+h(x)+g(Kx).\]
Choose \(\tau,\sigma>0\), initialize \(x^0\in X\) and \(y^0\in Y\), and for \(k\ge0\) compute
\[\widetilde x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau f}\!\left(x^k-\tau\bigl(\nabla h(x^k)+K^*y^k\bigr)\right),\]
\[\widetilde y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma g^*}\!\left(y^k+\sigma K(2\widetilde x^{k+1}-x^k)\right),\]
\[(x^{k+1},y^{k+1})=(\widetilde x^{k+1},\widetilde y^{k+1}).\]
If \(L\) is a Lipschitz constant of \(\nabla h\), require
\[\tau^{-1}-\sigma\lVert K\rVert^2>\frac{L}{2}.\]
Stop at a prescribed fixed-point residual tolerance and return \((x^{k+1},y^{k+1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In its primal-first ordering, Condat–Vũ combines a forward gradient step with a primal proximal step and then evaluates a dual proximal step at the reflected new primal point.
assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper, lower-semicontinuous convex functions.
\(h:X\to\mathbb R\) is convex and differentiable, and \(\nabla h\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz continuous.
\(K:X\to Y\) is linear, and a primal-dual solution exists.
\(\tau^{-1}-\sigma\lVert K\rVert^2>L/2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed recursion defines the unrelaxed primal-first Condat–Vũ splitting scheme for \(f+h+g\circ K\).

notation.meaning: Lipschitz constant of the gradient of h

children.title: Combettes-Pesquet Primal-Dual Splitting
children.top_down_role: Product-space primal-dual splitting for sums of composite monotone operators.

knowledge_statements.title: Combettes-Pesquet Primal-Dual Splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-space forward-backward-forward splitting for coupled monotone inclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Solve \(0\in Ax+Cx+\sum_{i=1}^mL_i^*v_i\) and \(0\in B_i^{-1}v_i+D_i^{-1}v_i-L_ix\). Given \(\gamma>0\), compute
\[p=J_{\gamma A}\bigl(x-\gamma(Cx+\sum_iL_i^*v_i)\bigr),\qquad q_i=J_{\gamma B_i^{-1}}\bigl(v_i+\gamma(L_ix-D_i^{-1}v_i)\bigr),\]
then update
\[x^+=p+\gamma\bigl(Cx-Cp+\sum_iL_i^*(v_i-q_i)\bigr),\]
\[v_i^+=q_i+\gamma\bigl(L_i(p-x)+D_i^{-1}v_i-D_i^{-1}q_i\bigr).\]
Choose \(\gamma\) below the reciprocal Lipschitz bound of the joint forward operator. Iterate until a product-space residual tolerance holds and return \((x,(v_i)_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Combettes–Pesquet scheme applies resolvents blockwise to set-valued operators and uses a second forward correction for all Lipschitz monotone couplings.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and every \(B_i\) are maximally monotone.
\(C\) and every \(D_i^{-1}\) are single-valued monotone Lipschitz operators.
Each \(L_i\) is bounded linear and the primal-dual solution set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed recursion is a product-space primal-dual forward-backward-forward iteration.

notation.meaning: adjoint of the i-th coupling operator

children.title: Primal-Dual Fixed-Point Methods
children.top_down_role: Fixed-point primal-dual architectures for composite minimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Fixed-Point Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-space fixed-point representation of a primal-dual splitting iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Z=X\times Y\) carry a positive-definite product metric \(M\), and let the primal-dual optimality system be \(0\in\mathcal A z+\mathcal B z\), where \(\mathcal A\) is maximally monotone and \(\mathcal B\) is cocoercive in that metric. Define
\[T=J_{M^{-1}\mathcal A}(I-M^{-1}\mathcal B).\]
Then
\[z^\star=Tz^\star\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in\mathcal A z^\star+\mathcal B z^\star.\]
A relaxed primal-dual fixed-point method is
\[z^{k+1}=z^k+\lambda_k(Tz^k-z^k),\]
with relaxation parameters chosen in an admissible averaged-operator range. The algorithm stops when \(\lVert Tz^k-z^k\rVert_M\) meets the prescribed tolerance and returns the primal and dual components of \(z^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-dual optimality inclusion can be encoded as a product-space fixed-point equation and solved by relaxed iteration of its forward-backward map.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is bounded, self-adjoint, and strongly positive.
The step metric makes \(T\) an averaged operator and \(\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Zeros of \(\mathcal A+\mathcal B\) coincide exactly with fixed points of \(T\).

notation.meaning: metric resolvent of the set-valued part

knowledge_statements.title: PD3O Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual three-operator splitting for smooth, proximable, and linearly composed terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min_x f(x)+q(x)+h(Ax)\), where \(q\) is smooth. Choose \(\gamma,[δ>0\), initialize \(z^0,s^0\), and for \(k\ge0\) compute
\[x^k=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(z^k),\]
\[s^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\delta h^*}\bigl((I-\gamma\delta AA^*)s^k+\delta A(2x^k-z^k-\gamma\nabla q(x^k))\bigr),\]
\[z^{k+1}=x^k-\gamma\nabla q(x^k)-\gamma A^*s^{k+1}.\]
Choose \(0<\gamma<2\beta\) when \(\nabla q\) is \(\beta\)-cocoercive and require \(\gamma\delta\lVert A\rVert^2<1\). Stop at a prescribed fixed-point residual tolerance and return \(x^k\) with dual variable \(s^{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PD3O combines one primal proximal map, one gradient evaluation, and one dual proximal map for a linearly composed third term.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(h\) are proper, lower-semicontinuous convex functions.
\(q\) is convex differentiable and \(\nabla q\) is \(\beta\)-cocoercive.
A primal-dual solution exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed recursion defines a standard PD3O primal-dual three-operator iteration.

notation.meaning: dual state associated with h composed with A

children.title: Primal-Dual Davis–Yin Family
children.top_down_role: Primal-dual forms derived from Davis–Yin three-operator splitting.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Davis–Yin Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-space Davis–Yin iteration for a primal-dual three-operator inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal K\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(A,B:\mathcal K\rightrightarrows\mathcal K\) be maximally monotone, and let \(C:\mathcal K\to\mathcal K\) be \(\beta\)-cocoercive for some \(\beta>0\). To solve \(0\in Au+Bu+Cu\), choose \(z^0\in\mathcal K\), \(0<\gamma<2\beta\), and relaxation parameters satisfying \(0<\lambda_k<2-\gamma/(2\beta)\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), compute
\[
u^k=J_{\gamma B}z^k,\qquad p^k=J_{\gamma A}\bigl(2u^k-z^k-\gamma Cu^k\bigr),\qquad z^{k+1}=z^k+\lambda_k(p^k-u^k).
\]
Here \(J_{\gamma A}=(I+\gamma A)^{-1}\). In primal-dual applications, \(\mathcal K\) is a product space and the components of \(u^k\) are primal and dual iterates. Exact equality \(p^k=u^k\) certifies a solution; a practical stopping rule may use \(\lVert p^k-u^k\rVert\leq\varepsilon\) for a prescribed \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply Davis–Yin splitting on a primal-dual product space using two resolvent evaluations, one cocoercive-operator evaluation, and relaxation within the explicit admissible interval.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal K\) is a real Hilbert space and \(A,B:\mathcal K\rightrightarrows\mathcal K\) are maximally monotone.
\(C:\mathcal K\to\mathcal K\) is \(\beta\)-cocoercive for some \(\beta>0\).
\(0<\gamma<2\beta\) and \(0<\lambda_k<2-\gamma/(2\beta)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^k=u^k\) implies \(0\in Au^k+Bu^k+Cu^k\).

notation.meaning: Resolvent of the scaled operator gamma A.
The two resolvent points at iteration k.

children.title: Three-Operator Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural equivalences and distinctions between the two primal-dual lineages.

knowledge_statements.title: Three-Operator Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT product-space representation as a three-operator monotone inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal H\) and \(\mathcal G\) be real Hilbert spaces, let \(f\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\) and \(g\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal G)\), let \(L:\mathcal H\to\mathcal G\) be bounded linear, and let \(h:\mathcal H\to\mathbb R\) be convex and Fréchet differentiable. On \(\mathcal K=\mathcal H\times\mathcal G\), define
\[
A(x,v)=(\partial f(x),\partial g^*(v)),\qquad S(x,v)=(L^*v,-Lx),\qquad C(x,v)=(\nabla h(x),0).
\]
Then
\[
0\in A(x,v)+S(x,v)+C(x,v)
\]
is equivalent to
\[
0\in\partial f(x)+\nabla h(x)+L^*v,
\qquad
Lx\in\partial g^*(v).
\]
Thus the primal-dual optimality system for minimizing \(f(x)+h(x)+g(Lx)\) has a three-operator product-space representation. A particular three-operator splitting may be applied when its additional assumptions on \(A\), \(S\), \(C\), step sizes, and any preconditioner are satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal-dual optimality system for a smooth-plus-composite convex problem is exactly a three-operator inclusion on the primal-dual product space; applying a particular splitting additionally requires that method's hypotheses.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) and \(\mathcal G\) are real Hilbert spaces, and \(L:\mathcal H\to\mathcal G\) is bounded linear.
\(f\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\) and \(g\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal G)\).
\(h:\mathcal H\to\mathbb R\) is convex and Fréchet differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,v)\in\operatorname{zer}(A+S+C)\) if and only if \(x\) and \(v\) satisfy the displayed primal-dual optimality system.

notation.meaning: Set of points u satisfying zero in T(u).

knowledge_statements.title: Tseng-Type Primal-Dual Splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward-backward-forward splitting applied to a coupled product-space inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A:\mathcal K\rightrightarrows\mathcal K\) be maximally monotone and \(B:\mathcal K\to\mathcal K\) be monotone and \(L_B\)-Lipschitz. Given \(z^0\in\mathcal K\) and \(0<\gamma<1/L_B\), Tseng's forward-backward-forward iteration is
\[
y^k=J_{\gamma A}(z^k-\gamma Bz^k),\qquad z^{k+1}=y^k-\gamma(By^k-Bz^k).
\]
When \(\mathcal K\) is a primal-dual product space, \(A\) collects the resolvent-accessible primal and dual blocks, while \(B\) contains the bounded linear skew coupling and any explicit monotone Lipschitz terms. The method returns \(y^k\) when \(\lVert y^k-z^k\rVert\leq\varepsilon\); exact equality implies that \(y^k\) solves \(0\in Ay^k+By^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tseng splitting uses a resolvent predictor followed by a second explicit evaluation that corrects the forward treatment of the coupled Lipschitz operator.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is maximally monotone on the real Hilbert space \(\mathcal K\).
\(B\) is monotone and \(L_B\)-Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y^k=z^k\) implies \(0\in Ay^k+By^k\).

children.title: Variable-Metric Forward-Backward-Forward Methods

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric Forward-Backward-Forward Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric-scaled Tseng iteration for monotone primal-dual inclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A:\mathcal K\rightrightarrows\mathcal K\) be maximally monotone, let \(B:\mathcal K\to\mathcal K\) be monotone and Lipschitz, and let \(U_k\) be self-adjoint strongly positive operators with uniformly bounded norms and inverses. Choose step sizes \(\gamma_k>0\) satisfying the forward-backward-forward stability bound in the \(U_k^{-1}\)-metric. Starting from \(z^0\in\mathcal K\), set
\[
y^k=J_{\gamma_kU_kA}(z^k-\gamma_kU_kBz^k),
\]
\[
z^{k+1}=y^k-\gamma_kU_k(By^k-Bz^k).
\]
A controlled metric variation, such as \(U_{k+1}\preccurlyeq(1+\eta_k)U_k\) with \(\sum_k\eta_k<\infty\), preserves the quasi-Fejér convergence framework. The output convention is the first \(y^k\) satisfying the prescribed fixed-point residual tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A changing positive-definite metric preconditions both forward evaluations and the backward resolvent, subject to uniform conditioning and summably controlled metric variation.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is maximally monotone and \(B\) is monotone Lipschitz on \(\mathcal K\).
\(U_k\) and \(U_k^{-1}\) are uniformly bounded and \(U_k\) is strongly positive.
\(U_{k+1}\preccurlyeq(1+\eta_k)U_k\) for a summable nonnegative sequence \((\eta_k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed iteration is the forward-backward-forward method in the changing metric induced by \(U_k^{-1}\).

children.title: Projective Primal-Dual Splitting
children.top_down_role: Primal-dual methods organized through projective separation mechanisms.

knowledge_statements.title: Projective Primal-Dual Splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relaxed projection driven by primal-dual affine separators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Z\subseteq\mathcal K\) be the primal-dual solution set. At iteration \(k\), construct a nonconstant affine function \(\phi_k:\mathcal K\to\mathbb R\) satisfying \(Z\subseteq H_k\), where \(H_k=\{z\in\mathcal K:\phi_k(z)\leq0\}\). Write \(a_k=\nabla\phi_k\), choose \(0<\lambda_k<2\), and update
\[
z^{k+1}=z^k-\lambda_k\frac{[\phi_k(z^k)]_+}{\lVert a_k\rVert^2}a_k.
\]
If \(\phi_k(z^k)\leq0\), set \(z^{k+1}=z^k\). Otherwise the update is a relaxed projection toward the separator half-space and strictly decreases the distance to every point of \(Z\). Terminate when the separator violation \([\phi_k(z^k)]_+\) and the graph-evaluation residuals satisfy their prescribed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each iteration builds a half-space containing all primal-dual solutions and relaxes the current point toward that half-space.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) is a nonempty subset of the real Hilbert space \(\mathcal K\).
\(\phi_k\) is affine, nonconstant, and nonpositive on \(Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(z^\star\in Z\), if \(\phi_k(z^k)>0\), then \(\lVert z^{k+1}-z^\star\rVert<\lVert z^k-z^\star\rVert\).

notation.meaning: Separator half-space containing the solution set.
Normal vector of the affine separator.

children.title: Half-Space Primal-Dual Splitting
children.top_down_role: Primal-dual methods organized around separating half-spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Half-Space Primal-Dual Splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A separating half-space as a verifiable primal-dual localization certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Z\subseteq\mathcal K\) denote the Kuhn–Tucker solution set, and let \(a_k\in\mathcal K\setminus\{0\}\) and \(b_k\in\mathbb R\) be computed from primal-dual graph evaluations. If every \(z^\star\in Z\) satisfies
\[
\langle a_k,z^\star\rangle\leq b_k,
\]
then \(H_k=\{z\in\mathcal K:\langle a_k,z\rangle\leq b_k\}\) is a valid outer half-space for \(Z\). For a current point \(z^k\), the scalar
\[
\delta_k=\frac{[\langle a_k,z^k\rangle-b_k]_+}{\lVert a_k\rVert}
\]
is exactly the distance from \(z^k\) to \(H_k\). Thus \(\delta_k>0\) certifies separation of the current point from the half-space, while projection onto \(H_k\) cannot exclude any primal-dual solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine inequality valid for every Kuhn–Tucker point certifies a solution-containing half-space and gives an exactly computable distance to it.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) is the Kuhn–Tucker solution set in a real Hilbert space \(\mathcal K\).
\(a_k\neq0\) and \(\langle a_k,z^\star\rangle\leq b_k\) for every \(z^\star\in Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z\subseteq H_k\) and \(d_{H_k}(z^k)=[\langle a_k,z^k\rangle-b_k]_+/\lVert a_k\rVert\).

children.title: Separator Geometry
children.top_down_role: Geometric structure of separators used by projective primal-dual families.

knowledge_statements.title: Separator Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine separator and projection formulas in a Hilbert product space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\phi:\mathcal K\to\mathbb R\) be the affine functional \(\phi(z)=\langle a,z\rangle-b\), where \(a\in\mathcal K\setminus\{0\}\), and define \(H=\{z:\phi(z)\leq0\}\). Then the metric projection and distance are
\[
P_Hz=z-\frac{[\phi(z)]_+}{\lVert a\rVert^2}a,
\qquad
d_H(z)=\frac{[\phi(z)]_+}{\lVert a\rVert}.
\]
If a primal-dual solution set \(Z\) satisfies \(Z\subseteq H\), then for every \(z^\star\in Z\) and \(0<\lambda<2\), the relaxed point \(z^+=z+\lambda(P_Hz-z)\) obeys
\[
\lVert z^+-z^\star\rVert^2\leq\lVert z-z^\star\rVert^2-\lambda(2-\lambda)d_H(z)^2.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine separator determines explicit projection and distance formulas, and relaxed projection yields a quantified Fejér decrease toward every enclosed solution.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal K\) is a real Hilbert space and \(a\neq0\).
\(Z\subseteq H=\{z:\langle a,z\rangle-b\leq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Relaxed projection onto \(H\) decreases squared distance to each \(z^\star\in Z\) by at least \(\lambda(2-\lambda)d_H(z)^2\).

children.title: Infimal Postcomposition Technique
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary-variable transformations for linearly composed operators.

knowledge_statements.title: Infimal Postcomposition Technique
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator-level infimal postcomposition used to expose a dual auxiliary variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A:\mathcal H\rightrightarrows\mathcal H\) and let \(L:\mathcal H\to\mathcal G\) be bounded linear. The infimal postcomposition of \(A\) by \(L\) is the set-valued operator
\[
L\mathbin{\triangleright}A=(L A^{-1}L^*)^{-1}:\mathcal G\rightrightarrows\mathcal G.
\]
Equivalently, for \(y,w\in\mathcal G\),
\[
w\in(L\mathbin{\triangleright}A)y
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\text{there exists }x\in\mathcal H\text{ such that }Lx=y\text{ and }L^*w\in Ax.
\]
Thus an occurrence of \(L\mathbin{\triangleright}A\) can be lifted to the auxiliary variable \(x\), replacing the postcomposed operator relation by one linear equation and one graph inclusion accessible to primal-dual splitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infimal postcomposition converts a linearly postcomposed inverse operator into an auxiliary-variable graph inclusion plus a linear constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) and \(\mathcal G\) are real Hilbert spaces.
\(L:\mathcal H\to\mathcal G\) is bounded linear.
\(A:\mathcal H\rightrightarrows\mathcal H\) is set-valued.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w\in(L\mathbin{\triangleright}A)y\) exactly when some \(x\) satisfies \(Lx=y\) and \(L^*w\in Ax\).

notation.meaning: Infimal postcomposition of A by L.

children.title: Dualization Technique
children.top_down_role: Construction of accessible dual blocks through conjugacy and operator inversion.

knowledge_statements.title: Dualization Technique
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-variable lifting of a linearly composed monotone inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A:\mathcal H\rightrightarrows\mathcal H\), \(B:\mathcal G\rightrightarrows\mathcal G\), and let \(L:\mathcal H\to\mathcal G\) be bounded linear. The primal inclusion
\[
0\in Ax+L^*B(Lx)
\]
holds if and only if there exists \(v\in\mathcal G\) such that
\[
0\in Ax+L^*v,
\qquad
0\in B^{-1}v-Lx.
\]
Indeed, the second relation is equivalent to \(v\in B(Lx)\), which makes the first relation the original inclusion. This dualization replaces the generally inaccessible composition \(L^*BL\) by separate evaluations involving \(A\), \(B^{-1}\), \(L\), and \(L^*\). When \(B=\partial g\), the inverse block is \(B^{-1}=\partial g^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Introduce a dual variable in the graph of the composed operator, replacing one difficult composition by two coupled but separately accessible inclusions.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) and \(\mathcal G\) are real Hilbert spaces.
\(L:\mathcal H\to\mathcal G\) is bounded linear.
\(A\) and \(B\) are set-valued operators on their respective spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in Ax+L^*B(Lx)\) if and only if some \(v\) satisfies \(0\in Ax+L^*v\) and \(0\in B^{-1}v-Lx\).

notation.meaning: Adjoint of the coupling map L.

children.title: Variable-Metric Technique
children.top_down_role: Metric redesign used to separate coupling while retaining accessible resolvents.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric Technique
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-definite preconditioning that preserves zeros and redesigns resolvent structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T:\mathcal K\rightrightarrows\mathcal K\), and let \(U:\mathcal K\to\mathcal K\) be bounded, self-adjoint, and strongly positive. Since \(U\) is invertible,
\[
0\in Tz\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad0\in UTz.
\]
Hence the metric-resolvent step
\[
z^+=J_{UT}z=(I+UT)^{-1}z
\]
has the same fixed points as the original inclusion: \(z^+=z\) if and only if \(0\in Tz\). On a primal-dual product space, a block positive-definite choice of \(U\) may absorb or triangularize linear coupling so that \(J_{UT}\) decomposes into accessible primal and dual resolvents. Strong positivity is essential: it defines the equivalent norm \(\lVert z\rVert_{U^{-1}}^2=\langle U^{-1}z,z\rangle\) used in the transformed analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invertible positive-definite preconditioning preserves the solution set while changing the metric and potentially making coupled resolvents separable.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal K\) is a real Hilbert space.
\(U\) is bounded, self-adjoint, and strongly positive.
\(T:\mathcal K\rightrightarrows\mathcal K\) is set-valued.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{zer}(UT)=\operatorname{zer}T\), and \(\operatorname{Fix}(J_{UT})=\operatorname{zer}T\).

notation.meaning: Resolvent of the preconditioned operator UT.

children.title: Gaussian-Elimination Technique
children.top_down_role: Block elimination used to expose reduced primal-dual fixed-point forms.

knowledge_statements.title: Gaussian-Elimination Technique
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schur-complement elimination of one block in a coupled primal-dual system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal H\) and \(\mathcal G\) be real Hilbert spaces. Let \(M:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H\) be bounded linear with a bounded inverse, let \(K:\mathcal H\to\mathcal G\) and \(N:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G\) be bounded linear, and let \(r\in\mathcal H\) and \(s\in\mathcal G\). The block system
\[
Mx+K^*v=r,
\qquad
Kx-Nv=s
\]
is equivalent to
\[
\bigl(N+KM^{-1}K^*\bigr)v=KM^{-1}r-s,
\qquad
x=M^{-1}(r-K^*v).
\]
Thus block Gaussian elimination replaces the coupled system by a reduced equation involving the Schur-complement operator \(N+KM^{-1}K^*\), followed by recovery of the eliminated primal block. In primal-dual fixed-point derivations, the same substitution identifies the metric and coupling combinations whose invertibility or positive definiteness is required for a reduced update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For specified primal and dual right-hand sides, eliminate the invertible primal block, solve the resulting Schur-complement equation for the dual block, and recover the primal variable by substitution.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) and \(\mathcal G\) are real Hilbert spaces.
\(M:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H\) is bounded linear with a bounded inverse.
\(K:\mathcal H\to\mathcal G\) and \(N:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G\) are bounded linear, while \(r\in\mathcal H\) and \(s\in\mathcal G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The block equations and the reduced Schur-complement equation with back-substitution have exactly the same solution pairs \((x,v)\in\mathcal H\times\mathcal G\).

children.title: Linearization Technique
children.top_down_role: Explicit treatment of difficult smooth or quadratic coupling components.

knowledge_statements.title: Linearization Technique
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward linearization of a cocoercive block inside a resolvent inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A:\mathcal H\rightrightarrows\mathcal H\) be maximally monotone and let \(C:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H\) be \(\beta\)-cocoercive. Instead of evaluating the generally difficult resolvent \(J_{\gamma(A+C)}\), linearize \(C\) at the current point and perform
\[
x^{k+1}=J_{\gamma A}\bigl(x^k-\gamma Cx^k\bigr),
\qquad 0<\gamma<2\beta.
\]
The fixed-point equation is exact:
\[
x=J_{\gamma A}(x-\gamma Cx)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
0\in Ax+Cx.
\]
For a smooth convex term \(h\) with Lipschitz gradient, take \(C=\nabla h\); the update then treats \(h\) explicitly while retaining a backward step only for the nonsmooth or set-valued block \(A\). Stop when the fixed-point residual meets the requested tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace a difficult joint resolvent by an explicit step on the smooth cocoercive block followed by the accessible resolvent of the remaining block.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is maximally monotone on the real Hilbert space \(\mathcal H\).
\(C\) is \(\beta\)-cocoercive for some \(\beta>0\).
\(0<\gamma<2\beta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Fix}(J_{\gamma A}(I-\gamma C))=\operatorname{zer}(A+C)\).

notation.meaning: Explicit cocoercive operator, often a gradient.

children.title: Product-Space Lifting Technique
children.top_down_role: Replication and lifting used to make multiple operators separately accessible.

knowledge_statements.title: Product-Space Lifting Technique
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite product-space reformulation for separately accessible composite terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\ge 1\), let \(\mathcal G=\prod_{i=1}^m\mathcal G_i\), and define \(L:\mathcal H\to\mathcal G\) and \(g:\mathcal G\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) by \(Lx=(L_1x,\ldots,L_mx)\) and \(g(y_1,\ldots,y_m)=\sum_{i=1}^m g_i(y_i)\). Then \[g(Lx)=\sum_{i=1}^m g_i(L_i x),\qquad L^*(y_1,\ldots,y_m)=\sum_{i=1}^m L_i^*y_i,\] and hence \[\min_{x\in\mathcal H}f(x)+g(Lx)=\min_{x\in\mathcal H}f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m g_i(L_i x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite sum of composite terms is represented by one separable function and one stacked linear operator on a product space, exposing each component independently.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) and \(\mathcal G_i\) are real Hilbert spaces.
\(f\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\), \(g_i\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal G_i)\), and \(L_i:\mathcal H\to\mathcal G_i\) are bounded linear maps.
The number of component terms \(m\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\min_{x\in\mathcal H} f(x)+g(Lx)=\min_{x\in\mathcal H} f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m g_i(L_i x),\qquad L^*(y_1,\ldots,y_m)=\sum_{i=1}^m L_i^*y_i.\]

notation.meaning: Hilbert product space with its canonical product inner product.

children.title: Stochastic PDHG Methods
children.top_down_role: PDHG variants that sample separable primal or dual blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic PDHG Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Serial randomized dual-block PDHG with stored aggregate gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_x f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m g_i(K_i x)\), choose probabilities \(p_i>0\), initialize \(x^0\) and \(y_i^0\), and store \(s^0=\sum_iK_i^*y_i^0\). At iteration \(k\), sample \(I_k=i\) with probability \(p_i\), set \[y_i^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma_i g_i^*}(y_i^k+\sigma_iK_i\bar x^k),\qquad y_j^{k+1}=y_j^k\quad(j\ne i),\] update \(s^{k+1}=s^k+K_i^*(y_i^{k+1}-y_i^k)\), and set \[x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau f}(x^k-\tau s^{k+1}),\qquad \bar x^{k+1}=x^{k+1}+\theta(x^{k+1}-x^k).\] Stop by a prescribed iteration budget or primal-dual residual test and return \((x^k,y^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One sampled dual block receives a proximal update, its contribution to the stored adjoint aggregate is refreshed, and the primal variable then receives a proximal step.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and every \(g_i\) are proper, lower-semicontinuous, convex functions on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
Each \(K_i\) is linear and every sampling probability satisfies \(p_i>0\).
Steps \(\tau,\sigma_i>0\) are chosen under a convergence-compatible blockwise PDHG condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x^k,y^k)\) is the stochastic PDHG output sequence generated by the displayed sampled-block updates.

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugate of the block function.
