children.title: Randomized Coordinate Primal-Dual Methods
children.top_down_role: Coordinate and block-coordinate updates of coupled primal-dual fixed points.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Coordinate Primal-Dual Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Randomized block activation of an averaged primal-dual fixed-point map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal Z=\prod_{i=1}^m\mathcal Z_i\) and let \(T:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Z\) be an averaged operator whose fixed points encode the target primal-dual solutions. Initialize \(z^0\in\mathcal Z\). Independently at iteration \(k\), sample a nonempty activation set \(S_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) with \(\mathbb P(i\in S_k)=p_i>0\), choose \(0<\lambda_k<1/\alpha\) when \(T\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged, and update \[z_i^{k+1}=\begin{cases}z_i^k+\lambda_k(T_i z^k-z_i^k),&i\in S_k,\\z_i^k,&i\notin S_k.\end{cases}\] Stop by a fixed budget or fixed-point residual criterion and return the current primal and dual blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomly selected primal or dual coordinates apply a relaxed fixed-point update, while unselected coordinates remain unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged on the product Hilbert space for some \(0<\alpha<1\).
Every block has positive activation probability, and activations are independent of the current iterate.
The fixed-point set \(\operatorname{Fix}T\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed rule defines a randomized coordinate primal-dual fixed-point iteration with every solution-relevant block activated recurrently almost surely.

notation.meaning: The ith coordinate of the fixed-point operator.
Random block-activation set at iteration k.
Marginal probability that block i is activated.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Forward-Backward Primal-Dual Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stochastic explicit evaluation combined with a resolvent step on a primal-dual space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the primal-dual inclusion \(0\in Az+Bz\) on a Hilbert space \(\mathcal Z\), where \(A\) contains proximable primal-dual terms and \(B\) is single-valued. Initialize \(z^0\in\mathcal Z\). Given a filtration \((\mathcal F_k)\), obtain an estimator \(G_k\) of \(Bz^k\), choose \(\gamma_k>0\), and compute \[z^{k+1}=z^k+\lambda_k\left(J_{\gamma_k A}(z^k-\gamma_kG_k)-z^k\right),\qquad J_{\gamma_kA}=(I+\gamma_kA)^{-1}.\] Stop by an iteration budget or an expected-residual criterion and return the primal and dual components of \(z^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unbiased stochastic estimate replaces the explicit forward operator evaluation, while all nonsmooth primal-dual terms are handled through a resolvent.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is maximally monotone and \(B\) is cocoercive on \(\mathcal Z\).
\(\mathbb E[G_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=Bz^k\) and the conditional noise has controlled second moment.
Steps and relaxation parameters satisfy the stochastic forward-backward summability and stability conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed recursion is a stochastic forward-backward primal-dual splitting sequence for the zeros of \(A+B\).

notation.meaning: Resolvent of the scaled maximally monotone operator.
Stochastic estimator of the forward operator at the current iterate.
History available before the kth stochastic oracle call.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Sum Oracle Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Indexed oracle for finite averages used by sampled primal-dual methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N\ge 1\), let \(\mathcal Z\) be a finite-dimensional space, and let \(G(z)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N G_i(z)\). A finite-sum first-order oracle is an interface that accepts \((z,i)\in\mathcal Z\times\{1,\ldots,N\}\) and returns the indexed component quantity \(G_i(z)\), such as a gradient, a selected subgradient, or an operator value, without evaluating the full mean. If an index \(I\) is sampled with \(\mathbb P(I=i)=p_i>0\), then \[\widehat G(z)=\frac{G_I(z)}{Np_I}\] satisfies \(\mathbb E[\widehat G(z)]=G(z)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-sum oracle evaluates one indexed component and returns its first-order or operator value without forming the full average; probability correction gives an unbiased estimate of that average.
assumptions_latex: \(N\ge 1\) is finite and each component \(G_i(z)\) is defined at the query point.
The sampled index distribution is known and satisfies \(p_i>0\) for every sampled index.
The random component quantity is integrable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathbb E\!\left[\frac{G_I(z)}{Np_I}\right]=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N G_i(z)=G(z).\]

notation.meaning: Returned component first-order or operator quantity.
Full finite-sum mean of the component quantities.

children.title: Mini-Batch Oracle Interfaces

knowledge_statements.title: Mini-Batch Oracle Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Batch-averaged stochastic oracle with explicit sampling and aggregation conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given component quantities \(G_i(z)\) with uniform mean \(G(z)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N G_i(z)\), a size-\(b\) mini-batch oracle samples a multiset or subset \(B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}\) according to a declared design and returns \[\widehat G_B(z)=\frac1b\sum_{i\in B}G_i(z)\] for uniform sampling with replacement. For nonuniform independent samples \(I_1,\ldots,I_b\) with probabilities \(p_i>0\), it instead returns \[\widehat G_B(z)=\frac1b\sum_{r=1}^b\frac{G_{I_r}(z)}{Np_{I_r}},\] so that \(\mathbb E[\widehat G_B(z)]=G(z)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mini-batch oracle aggregates several component queries, declaring the sampling design and applying weights that preserve unbiasedness.
assumptions_latex: \(1\le b\le N\) for subset sampling, while repeated indices are allowed under sampling with replacement.
Every sampled component quantity is integrable and each active sampling probability is positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned aggregate is an unbiased estimator of the full finite-sum mean under either displayed sampling convention.

notation.meaning: Sampled batch, interpreted as a subset or multiset according to the design.
Number of component oracle calls in the batch.

knowledge_statements.title: Sampling-Granularity Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact variance and oracle-cost scaling for independent uniform mini-batches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_1,ldots,I_b\) be independent indices sampled uniformly with replacement from \(\{1,ldots,N\}\). Define \[G(z)=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N G_i(z),\qquad \widehat G_b(z)=\frac1b\sum_{r=1}^b G_{I_r}(z),\qquad \sigma^2(z)=\mathbb E\|G_{I_1}(z)-G(z)\|^2.\] Then \[\mathbb E\|\widehat G_b(z)-G(z)\|^2=\frac{\sigma^2(z)}b.\] If one component evaluation has unit oracle cost, computing \(\widehat G_b(z)\) has component-oracle cost \(b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For independent uniform sampling, averaging b component calls divides estimator variance by b but multiplies component-oracle cost per iteration by b.
assumptions_latex: The sampled vectors \(G_{I_r}(z)\) are independent, identically distributed, and square-integrable.
Sampling is uniform with replacement from \(N\) finite-sum components.
One component evaluation has unit oracle cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathbb E\|\widehat G_b(z)-G(z)\|^2=\frac{\sigma^2(z)}b,\qquad \operatorname{cost}(\widehat G_b)=b.\]

notation.meaning: Average of b independent sampled component quantities.
Single-sample mean-square deviation from the full mean.

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Primal-Dual Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-delay asynchronous coordinate fixed-point iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Z\) be a primal-dual fixed-point operator on \(\mathcal Z=\prod_{i=1}^m\mathcal Z_i\), and let shared memory store \(z^k\). At logical iteration \(k\), a worker reads \(\widehat z^k=(z_1^{k-d_{k,1}},\ldots,z_m^{k-d_{k,m}})\), selects a block \(I_k\), and atomically writes \[z_{I_k}^{k+1}=z_{I_k}^k+\lambda_k\bigl(T_{I_k}\widehat z^k-\widehat z_{I_k}^k\bigr),\qquad z_j^{k+1}=z_j^k\quad(j\ne I_k).\] The worker repeats this operation until a prescribed budget or asynchronous residual criterion is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A worker evaluates one primal or dual block from a stale read and atomically writes a relaxed correction while other blocks remain unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is averaged and \(\operatorname{Fix}T\ne\varnothing\).
Delays satisfy \(0\le d_{k,i}\le D<\infty\), and every block is activated with positive probability.
Relaxations are restricted according to the averagedness, delay bound, and activation probabilities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed rule defines a bounded-delay asynchronous primal-dual coordinate iteration with atomic single-block writes.

notation.meaning: Possibly inconsistent delayed read used by a worker.
Age of block i in the kth read.
Block selected for the kth atomic update.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: AD-LPMM for a composite linear-map problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linearized proximal alternating-direction multiplier iteration with scalar majorization parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_1,f_2\) be proper closed convex functions, \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(x^0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(z^0,y^0\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(\rho>0\). Choose \(\alpha\ge\rho\lambda_{\max}(A^TA)\) and \(\beta\ge\rho\). For every \(k\ge0\), set \[\begin{aligned}x^{k+1}&=\operatorname{prox}_{f_1/\alpha}\left(x^k-\frac{\rho}{\alpha}A^T\left(Ax^k-z^k+\rho^{-1}y^k\right)\right),\\z^{k+1}&=\operatorname{prox}_{f_2/\beta}\left(z^k+\frac{\rho}{\beta}\left(Ax^{k+1}-z^k+\rho^{-1}y^k\right)\right),\\y^{k+1}&=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}-z^{k+1}).\end{aligned}\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AD-LPMM alternates a linearized proximal update for x, a proximal update for z, and an unscaled multiplier update. Its majorization parameters satisfy alpha at least rho times the largest eigenvalue of A^T A and beta at least rho.
assumptions_latex: f_1:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ and }f_2:\mathbb{R}^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ are proper, closed, and convex}
A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}
x^0\in\mathbb{R}^n,\ z^0,y^0\in\mathbb{R}^m
\rho>0
\alpha\ge\rho\lambda_{\max}(A^TA)
\beta\ge\rho
k\ge0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}x^{k+1}&=\operatorname{prox}_{f_1/\alpha}\left(x^k-\frac{\rho}{\alpha}A^T(Ax^k-z^k+\rho^{-1}y^k)\right),\\z^{k+1}&=\operatorname{prox}_{f_2/\beta}\left(z^k+\frac{\rho}{\beta}(Ax^{k+1}-z^k+\rho^{-1}y^k)\right),\\y^{k+1}&=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}-z^{k+1}).\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Block Separable Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical equality-coupled convex model for two-block ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A two-block separable ADMM model is the constrained convex problem \[\underset{x\in\mathcal X,\,z\in\mathcal Z}{\operatorname{minimize}}\quad f(x)+g(z)\qquad\text{subject to}\qquad Ax+Bz=c,\] where \(\mathcal X,\mathcal Z,\mathcal Y\) are finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, \(f\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal X)\), \(g\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal Z)\), \(A:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y\) and \(B:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Y\) are linear, and \(c\in\mathcal Y\). The two objective terms are separately accessible, while their variables interact only through the displayed linear equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The canonical ADMM model minimizes two separate closed convex functions whose variables are coupled by one linear equality.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(\{(x,z):Ax+Bz=c\}\) is nonempty.
Both objective functions are proper, lower-semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The problem has the two-block separable structure required by the canonical ADMM architecture.

notation.meaning: Proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions on the indicated space.

knowledge_statements.title: Composite Linear-Map Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variable-splitting representation of a convex composite objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal X)\), \(g\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal Z)\), and let \(K:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Z\) be linear. Introducing a copy variable \(z\) for the image \(Kx\) gives the exact representation \[\underset{x\in\mathcal X}{\operatorname{minimize}}\ f(x)+g(Kx)\quad\equiv\quad\underset{x\in\mathcal X,\,z\in\mathcal Z}{\operatorname{minimize}}\ f(x)+g(z)\quad\text{subject to}\quad Kx-z=0.\] Feasible pairs are precisely \((x,Kx)\), so the two formulations have identical objective values, infima, and corresponding minimizers. The right-hand problem is a two-block separable ADMM model with \(A=K\), \(B=-I\), and \(c=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Introducing z = Kx converts a composite objective into an equivalent two-block equality-constrained model directly compatible with ADMM.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) and \(\mathcal Z\) are finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
\(f\) and \(g\) are proper, lower-semicontinuous, convex functions, and \(K\) is linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The composite model and its lifted two-block constrained model have identical infima and corresponding minimizers \(z=Kx\).

notation.meaning: Linear map inside the composite term.
Auxiliary copy of the image Kx.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equality-constrained representation of a composite linear-map problem

Let \(f_1:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), \(f_2:\mathbb{R}^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), and \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\). Introducing \(z\in\mathbb{R}^m\) gives the equivalent representation
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\{f_1(x)+f_2(Ax)\}

\min_{\substack{x\in\mathbb{R}^n,\,z\in\mathbb{R}^m\\Ax-z=0}}\{f_1(x)+f_2(z)\}.
\]

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global-variable consensus formulation for distributed separable objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(m\ge 2\) agents with local functions \(f_i\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal X)\), the problem \[\min_{z\in\mathcal X}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(z)\] has the consensus representation \[\underset{x_1,\ldots,x_m,z\in\mathcal X}{\operatorname{minimize}}\quad\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\qquad\text{subject to}\qquad x_i-z=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).\] Feasibility forces \(x_1=\cdots=x_m=z\), so feasible objective values coincide. Every minimizer \(z^\star\) of the original problem corresponds to the lifted minimizer \(x_i^\star=z^\star\) for all \(i\), and every lifted minimizer projects to a minimizer of the original problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent receives a local copy of one decision variable, and equality constraints force every copy to agree with a global consensus variable.
assumptions_latex: \(m\ge2\), \(\mathcal X\) is a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, and each \(f_i\) is proper, lower-semicontinuous, and convex.
The original sum has at least one point with finite objective value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original aggregate problem and the copy-constrained consensus problem have identical optimal values and corresponding minimizers.

notation.meaning: Local decision copy held by agent i.

knowledge_statements.title: Sharing Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregate-coupled separable model with local variables sharing a common cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\ge 1\), let \(f_i\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal X_i)\), let \(A_i:\mathcal X_i\to\mathcal Y\) be linear, and let \(g\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal Y)\). The sharing problem \[\underset{x_i\in\mathcal X_i}{\operatorname{minimize}}\quad\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)+g\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i\right)\] has the exact lifted representation \[\underset{x_i\in\mathcal X_i,\ z\in\mathcal Y}{\operatorname{minimize}}\quad\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)+g(z)\qquad\text{subject to}\qquad \sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i-z=0.\] Feasible lifted points satisfy \(z=\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i\), so the formulations have identical feasible objective values, infima, and corresponding minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent local objectives are coupled through one function of the aggregate resource; an auxiliary aggregate variable yields an equivalent equality-constrained ADMM model.
assumptions_latex: All spaces are finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
The functions \(f_i\) and \(g\) are proper, lower-semicontinuous, and convex, and each \(A_i\) is linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The aggregate-coupled objective and its lifted sharing formulation have identical feasible objective values, infima, and corresponding minimizers.

notation.meaning: Contribution of local block i to the shared aggregate.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m\geq 2\). For \(i=1,\ldots,m\), let \(X_i\) and \(Y_i\) be finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces, let \(Z\) be a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space, let \(f_i:X_i\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Z\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex functions, let \(A_i:X_i\to Y_i\) and \(B_i:Z\to Y_i\) be linear, and let \(c_i\in Y_i\). A copy–aggregate coupling is a model
\[
\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_m,z}\ \sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)+g(z)\quad\text{subject to}\quad A_i x_i+B_i z=c_i,\quad i=1,\ldots,m.
\]
The variables \(x_i\) are local copies coupled through the shared aggregate variable \(z\). When \(X_i=Z=Y_i\), ordinary consensus is recovered by \(A_i=I\), \(B_i=-I\), and \(c_i=0\), which gives \(x_i=z\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate local copies are coupled through one shared aggregate variable; ordinary consensus is the special case requiring every copy to equal that aggregate.

children.title: Graph-Form Models
children.top_down_role: Models organized around the graph of a linear operator.

knowledge_statements.title: Graph-Form Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex objectives separated across the graph of one linear operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X,Y\) be finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces, let \(A:X\to Y\) be linear, and let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex functions. A graph-form model is
\[
\min_{x\in X,\,y\in Y}\ f(x)+g(y)\quad\text{subject to}\quad y=Ax.
\]
Equivalently, it minimizes \(f(x)+g(Ax)\). Introducing \(C=\{(x,y):y=Ax\}\), the constrained formulation is \(\min_{x,y} f(x)+g(y)+\delta_C(x,y)\), so the linear operator appears only through its graph constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graph-form model separates two objective terms by introducing an output variable constrained to equal a linear image of the input.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces.
\(A:X\to Y\) is linear.
\(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The graph constraint \(y=Ax\) makes the constrained model equivalent to \(\min_x f(x)+g(Ax)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Block Separable Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linearly coupled separable convex programs with at least three primal blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m\geq 3\). For finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces \(X_i,Y\), linear maps \(A_i:X_i\to Y\), vectors \(b\in Y\), and proper closed convex functions \(f_i:X_i\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), a multi-block separable model is
\[
\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_m}\ \sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\quad\text{subject to}\quad \sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i=b.
\]
A direct multi-block ADMM minimizes the augmented Lagrangian successively in individual blocks. Grouped architectures instead partition the blocks into two superblocks; corrected architectures add proximal, prediction-correction, or back-substitution steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Three or more separable objective blocks share one linear constraint; ADMM may update them directly, group them into two blocks, or add corrections.
assumptions_latex: \(m\geq 3\) and all spaces are finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces.
Each \(f_i\) is proper, closed, and convex.
Each \(A_i\) is linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed separable objective and coupling equation define the multi-block model class; grouping produces a two-superblock reformulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Unscaled ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-block convex ADMM in the original Lagrange-multiplier coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min_{x,z} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), choose \(\rho>0\), \(z^0\), and multiplier \(y^0\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), compute
\[
 x^{k+1}\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_x f(x)+\langle y^k,Ax+Bz^k-c\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax+Bz^k-c\|^2,
\]
\[
 z^{k+1}\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_z g(z)+\langle y^k,Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c\|^2,
\]
\[
 y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c).
\]
Stop when prescribed primal- and dual-residual tolerances hold; return the latest primal pair and multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unscaled ADMM alternately minimizes the augmented Lagrangian in two primal blocks and then updates the original, unscaled multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
\(A\) and \(B\) are linear maps between finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces.
Each displayed subproblem admits a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is \((x^{k+1},z^{k+1},y^{k+1})\), where \(y^k\) is the original Lagrange multiplier.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recurrence is the standard unscaled two-block ADMM algorithm and the algorithm content kind fits, but the only citation is specifically to function-linearized proximal ADMM. A direct section, theorem, or algorithm locator supporting the classical unscaled recurrence and its residual stopping terminology is required.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies the three update equations only; the extract does not state initialization or convergence conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\rho>0\) and \(L>0\), the AD-LPMM iteration is
\[
\begin{aligned}
x^{k+1}&=x^k-\frac1L A^\top\left(Ax^k-z^k+\frac1\rho y^k\right),\\
z^{k+1}&=T_{1/\rho}\left(Ax^{k+1}-b+\frac1\rho y^k\right)+b,\\
y^{k+1}&=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}-z^{k+1}).
\end{aligned}
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Take a linearized x-step with scale 1/L, update z by thresholding the shifted residual, and update the unscaled multiplier y by the primal residual.
assumptions_latex: \rho>0
A,x^k,z^k,y^k,b\text{ have conformable dimensions}
T_\tau\text{ denotes the thresholding map used by the iteration}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x^{k+1},z^{k+1},y^{k+1})\text{ is defined by the displayed AD-LPMM recurrence.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lifted unscaled ADMM with two proximal blocks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A lifted ADMM formulation using the copy constraints \(Ax=z\) and \(x=w\), with two original-coordinate multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the composite linear-map problem, initialize \(x^0,w^0,y_2^0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(z^0,y_1^0\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and choose \(\rho>0\). For each \(k\geq0\), set
\[
\begin{aligned}
x^{k+1}&=(I+A^TA)^{-1}\left(A^T\left(z^k-\rho^{-1}y_1^k\right)+w^k-\rho^{-1}y_2^k\right),\\
z^{k+1}&=\operatorname{prox}_{f_2/\rho}\left(Ax^{k+1}+\rho^{-1}y_1^k\right),\\
w^{k+1}&=\operatorname{prox}_{f_1/\rho}\left(x^{k+1}+\rho^{-1}y_2^k\right),\\
y_1^{k+1}&=y_1^k+\rho\left(Ax^{k+1}-z^{k+1}\right),\\
y_2^{k+1}&=y_2^k+\rho\left(x^{k+1}-w^{k+1}\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lifted method solves a linear system for x, applies the proximal maps of f2 and f1 to the copied blocks z and w, and updates two unscaled multipliers from the residuals Ax-z and x-w.
assumptions_latex: f_1:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ and }f_2:\mathbb{R}^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ are proper, closed, and convex}
A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}
x^0,w^0,y_2^0\in\mathbb{R}^n
z^0,y_1^0\in\mathbb{R}^m
\rho>0
k\geq0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}x^{k+1}&=(I+A^TA)^{-1}\left(A^T(z^k-\rho^{-1}y_1^k)+w^k-\rho^{-1}y_2^k\right),\\z^{k+1}&=\operatorname{prox}_{f_2/\rho}(Ax^{k+1}+\rho^{-1}y_1^k),\\w^{k+1}&=\operatorname{prox}_{f_1/\rho}(x^{k+1}+\rho^{-1}y_2^k),\\y_1^{k+1}&=y_1^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}-z^{k+1}),\\y_2^{k+1}&=y_2^k+\rho(x^{k+1}-w^{k+1}).\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unscaled ADMM for a composite linear-map problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: ADMM in original multiplier coordinates for the splitting constraint \(Ax-z=0\); the iteration requires a solution of each displayed x-subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the problem \(\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\{f_1(x)+f_2(Ax)\}\), initialize \(x^0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(z^0,y^0\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and choose \(\rho>0\). For each \(k\geq0\), choose
\[
x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left[f_1(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\left\|Ax-z^k+\frac{1}{\rho}y^k\right\|^2\right],
\]
and set
\[
z^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{f_2/\rho}\left(Ax^{k+1}+\frac{1}{\rho}y^k\right),\qquad
y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho\left(Ax^{k+1}-z^{k+1}\right).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a positive penalty and an unscaled multiplier y, the method alternates an x-subproblem, a proximal update for z, and a multiplier update using the residual Ax-z. The iteration is defined only when the x-subproblem admits a minimizer.
assumptions_latex: f_1:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ and }f_2:\mathbb{R}^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ are proper, closed, and convex}
A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}
x^0\in\mathbb{R}^n,\quad z^0,y^0\in\mathbb{R}^m
\rho>0
k\geq0
\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left[f_1(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\left\|Ax-z^k+\rho^{-1}y^k\right\|^2\right]\neq\varnothing
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}x^{k+1}&\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left[f_1(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\left\|Ax-z^k+\rho^{-1}y^k\right\|^2\right],\\z^{k+1}&=\operatorname{prox}_{f_2/\rho}(Ax^{k+1}+\rho^{-1}y^k),\\y^{k+1}&=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}-z^{k+1}).\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded specification of classical two-block ADMM in the original multiplier coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(x^0\in\mathbb R^n\), \(z^0\in\mathbb R^p\), \(y^0\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\rho>0\). For each \(k=0,1,\ldots\), choose
\[
x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_x\left\{h_1(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\left\|Ax+Bz^k-c+\frac{1}{\rho}y^k\right\|^2\right\},
\]
\[
z^{k+1}\in\arg\min_z\left\{h_2(z)+\frac{\rho}{2}\left\|Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c+\frac{1}{\rho}y^k\right\|^2\right\},
\]
and set
\[
y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho\bigl(Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c\bigr).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unscaled two-block ADMM alternately minimizes the two augmented subproblems, using the newly computed x block in the z update, and then adds rho times the new coupling residual to the original multiplier.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\quad B\in\mathbb R^{m\times p},\quad c\in\mathbb R^m
x^0\in\mathbb R^n,\quad z^0\in\mathbb R^p,\quad y^0\in\mathbb R^m
\rho>0
k\in\{0,1,2,\ldots\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x^{k+1},z^{k+1},y^{k+1})\text{ is generated by the two sequential augmented subproblem minimizations and the displayed multiplier update.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unscaled ADMM update with a regularized linear-system x-step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An explicit unscaled-multiplier ADMM recurrence; the extract supplies no convergence claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\rho>0\), define
\[
\begin{aligned}
x^{k+1}&=(I+A^\top A)^{-1}\left(A^\top\left(z^k-\frac1\rho y_1^k\right)+x^k\right),\\
z^{k+1}&=\mathcal T_{1/\rho}\left(Ax^{k+1}+\frac1\rho y_1^k-b\right)+b,\\
y_1^{k+1}&=y_1^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}-z^{k+1}).
\end{aligned}
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a linear system involving I plus A-transpose A for the new x, apply the shifted thresholding update to z, and update the unscaled multiplier y1 by the primal residual.
assumptions_latex: \rho>0
A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}
x^k\in\mathbb R^n
z^k,y_1^k,b\in\mathbb R^m
\mathcal T_\tau\text{ denotes the thresholding map used by the iteration}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x^{k+1},z^{k+1},y_1^{k+1})\text{ is defined by the displayed recurrence.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: AD-LPMM update with thresholded x-step and quadratic z-step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies the iteration only; no initialization, convergence, or solution guarantee is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L=\lambda_{\max}(A^\top A)\), \(\alpha=L\rho\), and \(\beta=\rho\). The AD-LPMM iteration is
\[
\begin{aligned}
x^{k+1}&=\mathcal T_{\lambda/(L\rho)}\!\left(x^k-\frac1L A^\top\left(Ax^k-z^k+\frac1\rho y^k\right)\right),\\
z^{k+1}&=\frac{\rho Ax^{k+1}+y^k+b}{\rho+1},\\
y^{k+1}&=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}-z^{k+1}).
\end{aligned}
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Set L to the largest eigenvalue of A-transpose A, alpha to L rho, and beta to rho. Update x by a thresholded linearized step, update z by the displayed affine closed form, and then update the multiplier y by the primal residual.
assumptions_latex: L=\lambda_{\max}(A^\top A)>0
\rho>0
\rho+1\ne0
A,x^k,z^k,y^k,b\text{ have conformable dimensions}
\mathcal T_\tau\text{ denotes the thresholding map used by the iteration}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x^{k+1},z^{k+1},y^{k+1})\text{ is defined by the displayed three-step recurrence.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Alternating direction proximal method of multipliers iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded specification of proximally regularized, unscaled two-block ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(x^0\in\mathbb R^n\), \(z^0\in\mathbb R^p\), \(y^0\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\rho>0\). Given \(G\) and \(Q\) defining the displayed quadratic terms, for each \(k=0,1,\ldots\), choose
\[
x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{h_1(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\left\|Ax+Bz^k-c+\frac{1}{\rho}y^k\right\|^2+\frac12\|x-x^k\|_G^2\right\},
\]
\[
z^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{z\in\mathbb R^p}\left\{h_2(z)+\frac{\rho}{2}\left\|Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c+\frac{1}{\rho}y^k\right\|^2+\frac12\|z-z^k\|_Q^2\right\},
\]
and set
\[
y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho\bigl(Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c\bigr).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AD-PMM adds a G-quadratic proximal term to the x subproblem and a Q-quadratic proximal term to the z subproblem, then performs the ordinary unscaled ADMM multiplier update.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\quad B\in\mathbb R^{m\times p},\quad c\in\mathbb R^m
x^0\in\mathbb R^n,\quad z^0\in\mathbb R^p,\quad y^0\in\mathbb R^m
\rho>0
G\text{ and }Q\text{ define the displayed quadratic quantities }\|\cdot\|_G^2\text{ and }\|\cdot\|_Q^2
k\in\{0,1,2,\ldots\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x^{k+1},z^{k+1},y^{k+1})\text{ is generated by the two sequential proximally regularized ADMM subproblems and the displayed multiplier update.}

knowledge_statements.title: Scaled ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent ADMM recurrence using the penalty-scaled dual variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the two-block problem \(\min_{x,z} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), fix \(\rho>0\) and define \(u^k=y^k/\rho\). Completing the square in the unscaled augmented Lagrangian gives the equivalent recurrence
\[
 x^{k+1}\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_x f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax+Bz^k-c+u^k\|^2,
\]
\[
 z^{k+1}\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_z g(z)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c+u^k\|^2,
\qquad
 u^{k+1}=u^k+Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c.
\]
Terms independent of the minimized block are omitted. Recover the original multiplier by \(y^k=\rho u^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaling the multiplier by the penalty removes explicit linear dual terms from the two minimizations and yields a residual-addition dual update.
assumptions_latex: The unscaled ADMM recurrence uses a fixed scalar penalty \(\rho>0\).
The scaled variable is initialized by \(u^0=y^0/\rho\).
The primal subproblems are solved with the same selections in both representations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under \(u^k=y^k/\rho\), scaled and unscaled ADMM generate identical primal iterates and satisfy \(y^k=\rho u^k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Alternating direction linearized proximal multiplier iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit proximal ADMM block updates obtained by linearizing the quadratic coupling terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the problem \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n,z\in\mathbb R^p}h_1(x)+h_2(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), initialize \(x^0\in\mathbb R^n\), \(z^0\in\mathbb R^p\), \(y^0\in\mathbb R^m\), and choose \(\rho>0\), \(\alpha\geq\rho\lambda_{\max}(A^TA)\), and \(\beta\geq\rho\lambda_{\max}(B^TB)\). For every \(k=0,1,\ldots\), set
\[
x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{h_1/\alpha}\!\left(x^k-\frac{\rho}{\alpha}A^T\left(Ax^k+Bz^k-c+\frac{1}{\rho}y^k\right)\right),
\]
\[
z^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{h_2/\beta}\!\left(z^k-\frac{\rho}{\beta}B^T\left(Ax^{k+1}+Bz^k-c+\frac{1}{\rho}y^k\right)\right),
\]
and \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AD-LPMM updates x and z by explicit proximal steps applied to linearizations of their augmented quadratic coupling terms, using alpha and beta at least rho times the respective largest Gram-matrix eigenvalues, and then performs the usual multiplier residual update.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\quad B\in\mathbb R^{m\times p},\quad c\in\mathbb R^m
x^0\in\mathbb R^n,\quad z^0\in\mathbb R^p,\quad y^0\in\mathbb R^m
\rho>0
\alpha\geq\rho\lambda_{\max}(A^TA)
\beta\geq\rho\lambda_{\max}(B^TB)
k\in\{0,1,2,\ldots\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x^{k+1},z^{k+1},y^{k+1})\text{ is generated by the stated sequential proximal-linearized block updates and }y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Explicit ADMM iteration for a full-column-rank stacked map
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to the splitting constraints z_i=A_i x. Full column rank of the vertically stacked map is essential for invertibility of the summed Gram matrix. This algorithm statement alone makes no convergence, feasibility, or attainment claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\rho>0\), let \(A=[A_1^T\;\cdots\;A_p^T]^T\) have full column rank, and let \(g_i:\mathbb{R}^{m_i}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex. For the constraints \(z_i=A_i x\), the iteration is
\[
x^{k+1}=\left(\sum_{i=1}^p A_i^T A_i\right)^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^p A_i^T\left(z_i^k-\rho^{-1}y_i^k\right),
\]
\[
z_i^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\rho^{-1}g_i}\left(A_i x^{k+1}+\rho^{-1}y_i^k\right),\qquad i=1,\ldots,p,
\]
\[
y_i^{k+1}=y_i^k+\rho\left(A_i x^{k+1}-z_i^{k+1}\right),\qquad i=1,\ldots,p.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the splitting constraints z_i=A_i x, full column rank of the vertically stacked map makes the summed Gram matrix invertible and gives the displayed explicit x-update. The method then applies each component proximal map and performs the corresponding unscaled-multiplier update. Writing u_i=y_i/rho gives the scaled-dual form.
assumptions_latex: p\in\mathbb{N}
\rho>0
A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{m_i\times n}\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,p
A=[A_1^T\;\cdots\;A_p^T]^T\text{ has full column rank}
g_i:\mathbb{R}^{m_i}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper, closed, and convex for }i=1,\ldots,p

children.title: Matrix-Penalty ADMM

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Penalty ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-block ADMM using a positive-definite metric on the constraint space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min_{x,z} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), choose a self-adjoint positive-definite operator \(P\) on the constraint space and define \(\|r\|_P^2=\langle r,Pr\rangle\). Starting from \((z^0,y^0)\), compute
\[
 x^{k+1}\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_x f(x)+\langle y^k,r(x,z^k)\rangle+\tfrac12\|r(x,z^k)\|_P^2,
\]
\[
 z^{k+1}\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_z g(z)+\langle y^k,r(x^{k+1},z)\rangle+\tfrac12\|r(x^{k+1},z)\|_P^2,
\qquad y^{k+1}=y^k+P r(x^{k+1},z^{k+1}),
\]
where \(r(x,z)=Ax+Bz-c\). Stop by metric-compatible residual tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrix-penalty ADMM replaces the scalar quadratic penalty by a positive-definite constraint-space metric and scales the multiplier update by that metric.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
\(P\) is self-adjoint and positive definite.
Each displayed subproblem admits a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recurrence is ADMM in the quadratic metric \(P\); choosing \(P=\rho I\) recovers scalar-penalty unscaled ADMM.

notation.meaning: constraint residual norm induced by P

children.title: ADMM-Douglas-Rachford Equivalence
children.top_down_role: The dual-space correspondence between ADMM and Douglas-Rachford splitting.

knowledge_statements.title: ADMM-Douglas-Rachford Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical two-block ADMM as Douglas–Rachford splitting of the dual optimality inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min_{x,z} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), with proper closed convex \(f,g\), and suppose a primal-dual solution exists. Its Fenchel dual minimizes
\[
 F(y)+G(y),\qquad F(y)=f^*(-A^*y),\qquad G(y)=g^*(-B^*y)+\langle c,y\rangle.
\]
For \(\gamma>0\), Douglas–Rachford splitting applied to \(0\in\partial F(y)+\partial G(y)\) uses
\[
 w^{k+1}=w^k+J_{\gamma\partial G}(2J_{\gamma\partial F}w^k-w^k)-J_{\gamma\partial F}w^k.
\]
After the standard affine identification of resolvent variables with the ADMM primal minimizers and multiplier, this recurrence generates the classical ADMM iterates with penalty \(\rho=1/\gamma\), up to interchange of the two dual summands.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classical two-block ADMM is Douglas–Rachford splitting applied to the sum of the two subdifferential operators in the Fenchel dual.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex on finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces.
A primal-dual solution exists and the displayed dual decomposition is proper.
The classical two-block ADMM subproblems and dual resolvents are well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under the standard variable identification and \(\rho=1/\gamma\), dual Douglas–Rachford splitting and classical ADMM are equivalent recurrences.

notation.meaning: the two convex summands of the Fenchel dual objective
resolvent of an operator T, equal to \((I+\gamma T)^{-1}\)

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min_{x,z} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), let \(d\) be the concave dual objective, define the convex function \(h=-d\), and let \(T=\partial h\). The exact method of multipliers satisfies the dual proximal-point step
\[
 y^{k+1}=(I+\rho T)^{-1}y^k
 =\mathop{\rm argmax}_y\left\{d(y)-\frac{1}{2\rho}\|y-y^k\|^2\right\}.
\]
ADMM replaces the joint primal minimization used by the method of multipliers with successive minimizations in \(x\) and \(z\). Equivalently, it treats the associated dual monotone inclusion through Douglas–Rachford splitting. Thus ADMM has a dual proximal-point interpretation, but its multiplier sequence is not generally the exact proximal-point sequence for \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method of multipliers is exact proximal point on the negative dual objective; ADMM realizes a related split dual iteration through alternating minimization and Douglas–Rachford splitting.

children.title: Peaceman–Rachford Relations
children.top_down_role: Connections between ADMM representations and Peaceman–Rachford splitting.

knowledge_statements.title: Peaceman–Rachford Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Peaceman–Rachford splitting as a composition of two reflected resolvents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\) and \(B\) be maximal monotone operators on a real Hilbert space, let \(\gamma>0\), define \(J_{\gamma A}=(I+\gamma A)^{-1}\), and define \(R_{\gamma A}=2J_{\gamma A}-I\), with analogous notation for \(B\). The Peaceman–Rachford fixed-point iteration for \(0\in A x+B x\) is
\[
 w^{k+1}=R_{\gamma B}R_{\gamma A}w^k.
\]
Douglas–Rachford uses the averaged Peaceman–Rachford operator,
\[
 w^{k+1}=\tfrac12\bigl(I+R_{\gamma B}R_{\gamma A}\bigr)w^k.
\]
Whenever \(w^\star\) is a fixed point and the standard solution correspondence applies, \(x^\star=J_{\gamma A}w^\star\) solves the inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Peaceman–Rachford composes two reflected resolvents; averaging this composition with the identity produces the Douglas–Rachford operator.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(B\) are maximal monotone operators on a real Hilbert space.
A fixed point exists for the stated solution correspondence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Douglas–Rachford map is \(\tfrac12(I+R_{\gamma B}R_{\gamma A})\), the one-half average of the Peaceman–Rachford map with \(I\).

children.title: Relaxed Reflection Relations
children.top_down_role: Connections between alternating-direction variants and relaxed reflected-resolvent schemes.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed Reflection Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relaxation family interpolating between identity, Douglas–Rachford, and Peaceman–Rachford updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T_{\rm PR}=R_{\gamma B}R_{\gamma A}\) be the Peaceman–Rachford composition for maximal monotone \(A,B\), and let \(\lambda\in(0,1]\). The relaxed reflection iteration is
\[
 w^{k+1}=T_\lambda w^k,
 \qquad T_\lambda=(1-\lambda)I+\lambda T_{\rm PR}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
 w^{k+1}=w^k+2\lambda\left[J_{\gamma B}\bigl(2J_{\gamma A}w^k-w^k\bigr)-J_{\gamma A}w^k\right].
\]
The choice \(\lambda=\tfrac12\) is Douglas–Rachford splitting, whereas \(\lambda=1\) is Peaceman–Rachford splitting. Fixed points are unchanged for every \(\lambda>0\), although convergence conditions can depend on \(\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex relaxation of the reflected-resolvent composition gives Douglas–Rachford at one-half and Peaceman–Rachford at one.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(B\) are maximal monotone operators on a real Hilbert space.
\(\gamma>0\) and \(\lambda\in(0,1]\).
The reflected-resolvent composition has a fixed point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(\lambda>0\), \(\operatorname{Fix}(T_\lambda)=\operatorname{Fix}(T_{\rm PR})\); \(\lambda=\tfrac12\) and \(\lambda=1\) yield Douglas–Rachford and Peaceman–Rachford, respectively.

children.title: ADMM Reflection Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between ADMM coordinates and reflection-based operator views.

knowledge_statements.title: ADMM Reflection Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: ADMM updates represented by reflected dual resolvents and their averaged composition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the dual inclusion \(0\in\partial F(y)+\partial G(y)\) associated with a solvable two-block convex program, define
\[
R_F=2J_{\gamma\partial F}-I,
\qquad R_G=2J_{\gamma\partial G}-I.
\]
The dual Douglas–Rachford variable obeys
\[
w^{k+1}=\tfrac12(I+R_G R_F)w^k.
\]
Under the standard ADMM–Douglas–Rachford affine identification, evaluating \(J_{\gamma\partial F}\) and \(J_{\gamma\partial G}\) corresponds to the two successive ADMM primal minimizations, while the displacement \(w^{k+1}-w^k\) corresponds to the multiplier residual update. With \(\rho=1/\gamma\), the averaged reflection recurrence therefore represents one classical ADMM cycle on the primal problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each ADMM primal minimization realizes a dual resolvent, and one full ADMM cycle corresponds to an averaged composition of the two reflected resolvents.
assumptions_latex: The two-block primal problem and its Fenchel dual have solutions.
\(F\) and \(G\) are proper closed convex dual summands.
The resolvent parameter and ADMM penalty satisfy \(\rho=1/\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: One classical ADMM cycle corresponds, in dual fixed-point coordinates, to \(w^{k+1}=\tfrac12(I+R_G R_F)w^k\).

notation.meaning: reflected resolvents of the dual subdifferentials

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Split Bregman iteration represented as scaled ADMM for a linearly split composite problem.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[
\min_{x,d}\ f(x)+g(d)\quad\text{subject to}\quad Bx-d=0,
\]
where \(f\) and \(g\) are proper closed convex functions and \(B\) is linear. For \(\rho>0\), split Bregman iteration is
\[
x^{k+1}\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_x f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Bx-d^k+b^k\|^2,
\]
\[
d^{k+1}\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_d g(d)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Bx^{k+1}-d+b^k\|^2,
\qquad b^{k+1}=b^k+Bx^{k+1}-d^{k+1}.
\]
These are exactly the scaled ADMM updates with \(A=B\), second constraint operator \(-I\), right-hand side \(0\), and scaled multiplier \(u^k=b^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a split linear composite model, split Bregman iteration and scaled ADMM are two representations of the same primal and scaled-dual recurrence.

children.title: Dykstra Relations
children.top_down_role: Connections between ADMM-type splitting and Dykstra-style correction frameworks.

knowledge_statements.title: Dykstra Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-set Euclidean Dykstra iteration and its ADMM correspondence for best approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C,D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty closed convex sets, and let \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\). Initialize \(x^0=v\) and \(p^0=q^0=0\). The two-set Dykstra iteration is
\[
y^k=P_D(x^k+p^k),\qquad p^{k+1}=x^k+p^k-y^k,
\]
\[
x^{k+1}=P_C(y^k+q^k),\qquad q^{k+1}=y^k+q^k-x^{k+1}.
\]
Thus each primal update is a proximal step for an indicator function, since \(P_C=\operatorname{prox}_{\delta_C}\) and \(P_D=\operatorname{prox}_{\delta_D}\), while \(p^k,q^k\) are correction variables. Under the standard Fenchel-dual reformulation of \(\min_{x\in C\cap D}\tfrac12\lVert x-v\rVert^2\), these correction-variable updates correspond to scaled ADMM dual updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dykstra alternates projections with correction variables; for two-set best approximation, these corrections correspond to scaled ADMM dual variables in a standard dual formulation.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) and \(D\) are nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(C\cap D\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_C=\operatorname{prox}_{\delta_C}\), \(P_D=\operatorname{prox}_{\delta_D}\), and Dykstra corrections admit an ADMM dual-variable interpretation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Dykstra iteration is standard, but the precise identification of its correction variables with scaled ADMM dual variables depends on the chosen dual formulation, scaling, ordering, and initialization. No source is supplied for that nontrivial correspondence.

children.title: Projection Framework Relations
children.top_down_role: Connections between alternating-direction schemes and projection-based formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Framework Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Indicator-function specialization of identity-metric proximal and ADMM block updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonempty closed convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), its indicator satisfies
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\delta_C}(v)=\arg\min_{x\in C}\frac{1}{2\gamma}\lVert x-v\rVert^2=P_C(v),\qquad \gamma>0.
\]
Consequently, whenever an ADMM block objective has the form
\[
\delta_C(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert x-v^k\rVert^2,
\]
with \(\rho>0\), its exact minimizer is \(x^{k+1}=P_C(v^k)\). If both block objectives have this Euclidean identity-metric form, the ADMM iteration can be expressed through projections and a scaled residual correction. The resulting projection scheme still depends on the constraint splitting and variable identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An indicator-function ADMM block with an identity-metric Euclidean quadratic penalty is exactly a projection. If both blocks have this form, ADMM becomes a projection-based splitting scheme with a scaled residual correction.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(\gamma>0\) and \(\rho>0\).
Each claimed projection-form ADMM block has an identity-metric Euclidean quadratic penalty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\delta_C}=P_C\), and indicator-function ADMM blocks with identity-metric penalties are projection steps.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Framework Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correspondence among ADMM, dual Douglas–Rachford splitting, and projection specializations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces, let \(A:X\to Y\) be linear, and consider
\[
\min_{x\in X} f(x)+g(Ax),
\]
where \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper, closed, and convex. Introducing \(z=Ax\) gives a two-block equality-constrained problem. Define the dual functions
\[
\phi(y)=f^*(-A^\top y),\qquad \psi(y)=g^*(y).
\]
Under a qualification condition ensuring primal-dual solvability and the required subdifferential calculus, the dual optimality inclusion is
\[
0\in\partial\phi(y)+\partial\psi(y).
\]
ADMM applied to the split primal problem corresponds, after the standard convention-dependent affine identification of iterates, to Douglas–Rachford splitting for this dual inclusion. Indicator-function specializations turn the corresponding proximal mappings into projections. In best-approximation models, additional problem-specific identifications can yield Dykstra-type correction variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: ADMM on a split primal problem corresponds, under a convention-dependent iterate identification, to Douglas–Rachford splitting for the dual problem. Indicator specializations produce projections, and certain best-approximation formulations yield Dykstra-type corrections.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces and \(A:X\to Y\) is linear.
\(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
A qualification condition ensures primal-dual solvability and the stated dual subdifferential formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: ADMM and dual Douglas–Rachford splitting represent the same splitting architecture under a suitable iterate identification; projection and Dykstra specializations require the stated additional structure.

notation.meaning: convex subdifferentials of the dual component functions

children.title: Exact Block Minimization

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Block Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical two-block ADMM with globally exact augmented-Lagrangian subproblem solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given proper closed convex \(f\) and \(g\), matrices \(A,B\), vector \(c\), penalty \(\rho>0\), and \((z^0,u^0)\), exact scaled ADMM for
\[
\min_{x,z} f(x)+g(z)\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax+Bz=c
\]
performs
\[
x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_x f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Ax+Bz^k-c+u^k\rVert^2,
\]
\[
z^{k+1}\in\arg\min_z g(z)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c+u^k\rVert^2,
\]
\[
u^{k+1}=u^k+Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c.
\]
Each displayed argmin must be solved exactly. The method returns a current primal pair and scaled multiplier, and may stop when prescribed primal and dual residual tests hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact ADMM alternately minimizes each augmented-Lagrangian block to global optimality and then updates the scaled multiplier by the constraint residual.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
Each block argmin is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every outer iteration applies two exact block solution maps followed by the scaled dual update.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Block Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction of identity-coupled ADMM block minimizations to proximal mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the consensus problem \(\min_{x,z} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(x-z=0\), scaled ADMM with \(\rho>0\) has block solutions
\[
x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{f/\rho}(z^k-u^k),\qquad
z^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{g/\rho}(x^{k+1}+u^k),
\]
followed by \(u^{k+1}=u^k+x^{k+1}-z^{k+1}\), where
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{h/\rho}(v)=\arg\min_w h(w)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert w-v\rVert^2.
\]
More generally, an ADMM block is a directly accessible proximal solve whenever its quadratic penalty has Euclidean identity metric after an explicit change of variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For identity-coupled consensus constraints, both ADMM block minimizations are ordinary proximal mappings followed by a residual-based scaled-dual update.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two exact block solution maps are \(\operatorname{prox}_{f/\rho}\) and \(\operatorname{prox}_{g/\rho}\).

notation.meaning: proximal map with quadratic weight rho

children.title: Linear-System Block Solves

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-System Block Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal-equation representation of quadratic ADMM block minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose an ADMM block has objective
\[
\frac12 x^TQx+q^Tx+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Ax-d^k\rVert^2,
\]
where \(Q\succeq0\) and \(d^k\) contains the fixed current values of the other block and scaled multiplier. Its exact minimizers satisfy
\[
(Q+\rho A^TA)x^{k+1}=\rho A^Td^k-q.
\]
If \(Q+\rho A^TA\succ0\), this system has a unique solution. When its coefficient matrix is iteration-independent, a factorization or preconditioner may be reused across outer iterations; otherwise, any iterative linear solver must meet the exactness or controlled-inexactness regime imposed by the surrounding ADMM method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic ADMM block reduces to a normal-equation linear system whose factorization or preconditioner can often be reused between iterations.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\) and \(\rho>0\).
The block is unconstrained and finite-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((Q+\rho A^TA)x^{k+1}=\rho A^Td^k-q\), uniquely when \(Q+\rho A^TA\succ0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Nested Block Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: ADMM architecture in which an inner iterative method approximates each difficult block minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At outer iteration \(k\), let \(\Phi_k(x)\) and \(\Psi_k(z)\) denote the two augmented-Lagrangian block objectives. Starting from chosen warm starts, run inner algorithms for \(m_k^x\) and \(m_k^z\) steps and set
\[
x^{k+1}=\mathcal{I}_{k,x}^{m_k^x}(x^{k,0}),\qquad
z^{k+1}=\mathcal{I}_{k,z}^{m_k^z}(z^{k,0}),
\]
so that computable optimality residuals satisfy
\[
\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial\Phi_k(x^{k+1}))\leq\varepsilon_k^x,
\qquad
\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial\Psi_k(z^{k+1}))\leq\varepsilon_k^z.
\]
Then update the ADMM multiplier using the resulting primal constraint residual. The stopping rules for the inner algorithms must implement a declared accuracy regime for \(\varepsilon_k^x,\varepsilon_k^z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested ADMM uses iterative inner solvers for block subproblems, stopping each when a computable block-optimality residual meets its assigned tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Each block objective is proper, closed, and convex.
Inner methods produce computable optimality residuals.
The outer penalty parameter is positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inner outputs replace exact block minimizers while satisfying declared residual tolerances \(\varepsilon_k^x\) and \(\varepsilon_k^z\).

notation.meaning: m steps of an inner solver

children.title: Inexact Block Solves
children.top_down_role: ADMM architectures permitting controlled approximation of block subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Block Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbed optimality conditions defining an inexact two-block ADMM update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For augmented-Lagrangian block objectives \(\Phi_k\) and \(\Psi_k\), an inexact ADMM block update may be described by error vectors \(e_x^{k+1}\) and \(e_z^{k+1}\) satisfying
\[
0\in\partial\Phi_k(x^{k+1})+e_x^{k+1},
\qquad
0\in\partial\Psi_k(z^{k+1})+e_z^{k+1}.
\]
An absolute summable-error regime requires
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lVert e_x^{k+1}\rVert<\infty,
\qquad
\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lVert e_z^{k+1}\rVert<\infty.
\]
The multiplier is then updated exactly from the computed primal residual. These inclusions define approximate block stationarity; convergence additionally requires the solvability and operator assumptions of the selected inexact-ADMM theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact block solve satisfies a perturbed subproblem optimality inclusion; one standard regime requires both sequences of perturbation norms to be summable.
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi_k\) and \(\Psi_k\) are proper, closed, and convex.
The error vectors are measurable from, or bounded by, the inner stopping test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\partial\Phi_k(x^{k+1})+e_x^{k+1}\) and \(0\in\partial\Psi_k(z^{k+1})+e_z^{k+1}\), with summable errors in the stated regime.

children.title: Inner-Accuracy Regimes
children.top_down_role: Accuracy policies governing acceptable inner-solve approximation.

knowledge_statements.title: Inner-Accuracy Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute, summable, and relative stopping regimes for iterative ADMM block solvers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r_{x,k}\) and \(r_{z,k}\) be computable optimality residuals for the two inner block solves. Common accuracy regimes include fixed absolute tolerances
\[
\lVert r_{x,k}\rVert\leq\varepsilon_x,
\qquad \lVert r_{z,k}\rVert\leq\varepsilon_z,
\]
vanishing summable tolerances
\[
\lVert r_{x,k}\rVert\leq\varepsilon_k^x,
\quad \lVert r_{z,k}\rVert\leq\varepsilon_k^z,
\quad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}(\varepsilon_k^x+\varepsilon_k^z)<\infty,
\]
and relative criteria \(\lVert r_{x,k}\rVert\leq\eta_k d_{x,k}\), \(\lVert r_{z,k}\rVert\leq\eta_k d_{z,k}\), where the nonnegative scales \(d_{x,k},d_{z,k}\) are specified by the convergence theorem. A fixed nonzero tolerance generally certifies only bounded inner error, not exact asymptotic ADMM convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inner solves may use fixed, summably vanishing, or theorem-specific relative tolerances; fixed nonzero tolerances alone generally do not ensure exact asymptotic convergence.
assumptions_latex: Residuals vanish at exact block minimizers.
All tolerance and scaling sequences are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A convergence-compatible accuracy schedule must match the error condition required by the chosen inexact-ADMM theorem.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The taxonomy of accuracy regimes is reasonable, but admissible residuals, relative scales, and the conclusion about asymptotic convergence are theorem-specific. A source identifying a concrete inexact-ADMM framework is required.

children.title: Linearized ADMM
children.top_down_role: ADMM with explicit treatment of difficult smooth or quadratic block structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Linearized ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus ADMM with the quadratic penalty linearized in one block and proximally stabilized.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min_{x,z} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(x-z=0\), choose \(\rho>0\) and \(\tau>\rho\). Given \((x^k,z^k,u^k)\), linearized ADMM performs
\[
x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{f/\tau}\!\left(x^k-\frac{\rho}{\tau}(x^k-z^k+u^k)\right),
\]
\[
z^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{g/\rho}(x^{k+1}+u^k),
\qquad
u^{k+1}=u^k+x^{k+1}-z^{k+1}.
\]
The first update is obtained by linearizing the smooth quadratic penalty at \(x^k\) and adding \(\tfrac{\tau}{2}\lVert x-x^k\rVert^2\). Stop using prescribed primal and dual residual tolerances and return the current primal-dual iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linearized ADMM replaces one quadratic block solve by a forward penalty-gradient step followed by a proximal map, while retaining the other ADMM updates.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
\(\rho>0\) and \(\tau>\rho\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The difficult first block is replaced by an explicit proximal-gradient update with curvature \(\tau\).

knowledge_statements.title: Function-Linearized Proximal ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: ADMM with a smooth objective component linearized and stabilized by a quadratic proximal term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[
\min_{x,z} p(x)+h(x)+g(z)\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax+Bz=c,
\]
where \(h\) is differentiable. Given \((x^k,z^k,u^k)\), penalty \(\rho>0\), and a self-adjoint matrix \(H\succeq0\), the function-linearized proximal \(x\)-update is
\[
x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_x p(x)+\langle\nabla h(x^k),x-x^k\rangle+\frac12\lVert x-x^k\rVert_H^2
+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Ax+Bz^k-c+u^k\rVert^2.
\]
Then minimize the usual augmented-Lagrangian \(z\)-block exactly and set
\[
u^{k+1}=u^k+Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c.
\]
The matrix \(H\) must provide sufficient curvature to majorize the linearization error of \(h\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This ADMM variant linearizes a smooth objective term, adds proximal curvature controlling the approximation error, and retains the augmented penalty and multiplier update.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
\(h\) is convex with Lipschitz-continuous gradient.
\(H\succeq0\) supplies a valid quadratic majorizer for \(h\).
The displayed block argmins are nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The \(x\)-block uses a proximal first-order model of \(h\), followed by the standard \(z\)-block and multiplier updates.

notation.meaning: quadratic form v transpose H v

children.title: Semi-Proximal ADMM
children.top_down_role: ADMM with selective proximal regularization across blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Semi-Proximal ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-block ADMM augmented by selective positive-semidefinite proximal terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[
\min_{x,z} f(x)+g(z)\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax+Bz=c,
\]
choose \(\rho>0\) and self-adjoint matrices \(S\succeq0\) and \(T\succeq0\), allowing either matrix to be zero. Semi-proximal ADMM computes
\[
x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_x f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Ax+Bz^k-c+u^k\rVert^2+\frac12\lVert x-x^k\rVert_S^2,
\]
\[
z^{k+1}\in\arg\min_z g(z)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c+u^k\rVert^2+\frac12\lVert z-z^k\rVert_T^2,
\]
followed by
\[
u^{k+1}=u^k+Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c.
\]
Selective regularization can make a block strongly convex or easier to solve without changing the constraint-residual multiplier update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Semi-proximal ADMM adds optional positive-semidefinite proximal regularizers to either block while retaining exact minimization of the regularized subproblems and the usual multiplier update.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
\(\rho>0\), \(S\succeq0\), and \(T\succeq0\).
Both regularized block argmins are nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The ADMM blocks are stabilized selectively by \(S\) and \(T\), with zero matrices recovering ordinary exact ADMM.

notation.meaning: quadratic form v transpose S v

children.title: Majorized ADMM

knowledge_statements.title: Majorized ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A two-block convex ADMM using upper models and proximal curvature in each primal subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x,z}\{f(x)+g(z):Ax+Bz=c\}\) with scaled multiplier \(u\) and penalty \(\rho>0\). Choose models \(m_f^k(x)\geq f(x)\) and \(m_g^k(z)\geq g(z)\), tight at \(x^k\) and \(z^k\), and positive-semidefinite operators \(P_k,Q_k\). Majorized ADMM performs \[x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_x\left\{m_f^k(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax+Bz^k-c+u^k\|^2+\frac12\|x-x^k\|_{P_k}^2\right\},\] \[z^{k+1}\in\arg\min_z\left\{m_g^k(z)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c+u^k\|^2+\frac12\|z-z^k\|_{Q_k}^2\right\},\] followed by \(u^{k+1}=u^k+Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace difficult objective terms by iterationwise tight upper models, solve the resulting stabilized ADMM block subproblems, and update the scaled multiplier with the new feasibility residual.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
Each model is tight at the current iterate and majorizes its corresponding function.
\(P_k\succeq0\), \(Q_k\succeq0\), and both displayed subproblems attain minimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed rules define one majorized-ADMM iteration \((x^k,z^k,u^k)\mapsto(x^{k+1},z^{k+1},u^{k+1})\).

notation.meaning: Quadratic form given by the positive-semidefinite operator P.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_{x,z}\{f(x)+g(z):Ax+Bz=c\}\), fix \(\rho>0\), \(P\succeq0\), and \(Q\succeq0\). children.title: Metric-Change Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Metric-Change Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard boundedness and controlled-growth regimes for changing ADMM metrics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_k\) denote a self-adjoint positive-definite metric on the product primal-dual space. A uniformly nondegenerate, bounded regime satisfies \[mI\preceq M_k\preceq MI\qquad(k\geq0)\] for constants \(0<m\leq M<\infty\). A controlled-growth regime additionally admits numbers \(\eta_k\geq0\) such that \[M_{k+1}\preceq(1+\eta_k)M_k,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\eta_k<\infty.\] A stronger finite-variation regime requires \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|M_{k+1}-M_k\|<\infty\). These predicates restrict metric drift and are typical hypotheses in variable-metric convergence analyses; they are not consequences of the ADMM updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Admissible metric sequences remain uniformly positive and bounded, with multiplicative growth or total variation summable across iterations.
assumptions_latex: Each \(M_k\) is a bounded self-adjoint operator on a fixed finite-dimensional product space.
The operator order \(S\preceq T\) means \(T-S\) is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any sequence satisfying the displayed inequalities belongs to the corresponding bounded, controlled-growth, or finite-variation metric-change regime.

children.title: Relaxation Boundary Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Boundary Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Endpoint and exterior regimes for relaxed fixed-point forms of ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write a relaxed ADMM splitting step abstractly as \(w^{k+1}=w^k+\alpha(Tw^k-w^k)\), where \(T\) is firmly nonexpansive. The standard open relaxation interval is \(0<\alpha<2\). At \(\alpha=0\), \(w^{k+1}=w^k\), so no progress occurs unless the initial point is fixed. At \(\alpha=2\), the map \(2T-I\) is generally only nonexpansive; convergence of its Picard iterates is not guaranteed without additional structure. For \(\alpha<0\) or \(\alpha>2\), even the scalar firmly nonexpansive map \(T=0\) gives \(w^{k+1}=(1-\alpha)w^k\), whose magnitude grows whenever \(|1-\alpha|>1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero relaxation stalls; the value two loses averagedness; parameters outside the closed interval can diverge even for a scalar firmly nonexpansive map.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a firmly nonexpansive self-map of a real Hilbert space.
The relaxed iteration uses a constant scalar \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generic convergence-safe interval is open: \(0<\alpha<2\); its endpoints and exterior require separate analysis or stronger assumptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Inertial ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An ADMM fixed-point map evaluated at an extrapolated state carrying one-step history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be the fixed-point operator representing one complete ADMM cycle on a product state \(w=(x,z,u)\). Given \(w^{-1}=w^0\) and parameters \(\beta_k\geq0\), form the inertial point \[\bar w^k=w^k+\beta_k(w^k-w^{k-1}),\] and apply one ADMM cycle there: \[w^{k+1}=T(\bar w^k).\] Equivalently, every primal and dual subproblem in that cycle uses the components of \(\bar w^k\) wherever the preceding ADMM state would ordinarily appear. A stopping rule may terminate when both the primal feasibility residual and \(\|w^{k+1}-w^k\|\) are below prescribed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extrapolate the full primal-dual state from its last displacement, then evaluate one complete ADMM cycle at that inertial point.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a single-valued fixed-point realization of one ADMM cycle.
\(w^{-1}=w^0\) and \(\beta_k\geq0\) are specified before iteration.
Each ADMM subproblem invoked by \(T\) is solvable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed recurrence defines full-state inertial ADMM with one-step memory.

children.title: Momentum ADMM

knowledge_statements.title: Momentum ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A post-update momentum realization of a one-cycle ADMM fixed-point operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) denote one complete ADMM cycle on the state \(w=(x,z,u)\). Given \(w^{-1}=w^0\), first compute the ordinary candidate \(v^{k+1}=T(w^k)\), then set \[w^{k+1}=v^{k+1}+\beta_k(v^{k+1}-v^k),\qquad \beta_k\geq0,\] with \(v^0=w^0\). Thus the history term is applied after the ADMM candidate has been produced, unlike pre-update inertial evaluation \(T(w^k+\beta_k(w^k-w^{k-1}))\). Output the latest \(w^k\) when prescribed primal and dual residual tolerances are met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute an ordinary ADMM candidate, then add a multiple of the displacement between consecutive candidates as a post-update momentum term.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a single-valued realization of one complete ADMM cycle.
\(w^{-1}=w^0\), \(v^0=w^0\), and the coefficients \(\beta_k\geq0\) are specified.
Every ADMM cycle used to evaluate \(T\) is well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recurrence defines post-update momentum ADMM and distinguishes it from pre-update inertial ADMM by history-term placement.

children.title: History-Term Placement
children.top_down_role: Architectural locations where past-iterate information enters ADMM.

knowledge_statements.title: History-Term Placement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical placements of one-step history within an abstract ADMM cycle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be one complete ADMM fixed-point cycle and let \(h^k=\beta_k(w^k-w^{k-1})\). Three distinct history placements are \[w^{k+1}=T(w^k+h^k)\quad\text{(pre-cycle)},\] \[w^{k+1}=T(w^k)+h^k\quad\text{(post-cycle)},\] and \[w^{k+1}=T_k(w^k;h_x^k,h_z^k,h_u^k)\quad\text{(blockwise)},\] where selected history components enter only their associated primal or dual update. Because \(T\) is generally nonlinear, \(T(w^k+h^k)\neq T(w^k)+h^k\); consequently these placements define different algorithms even when they use the same coefficients and stored states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: History may enter before the ADMM cycle, after it, or inside selected block updates; nonlinear ADMM maps make these placements inequivalent.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a well-defined one-cycle ADMM map on a product state space.
\(w^{k-1}\), \(w^k\), and \(\beta_k\) are available at iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pre-cycle, post-cycle, and blockwise history placements are generally inequivalent representations of history-dependent ADMM.

notation.meaning: ADMM cycle with history inserted into selected block updates.

children.title: Randomized Block ADMM
children.top_down_role: ADMM with sampled primal blocks or constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Block ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A multi-block ADMM iteration updating a sampled subset of primal blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_m}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\) subject to \(\sum_{i=1}^m A_ix_i=c\). Given \(x^0,u^0\), penalty \(\rho>0\), and probabilities \(p_i>0\), sample \(I_k\) independently with \(\mathbb P(I_k=i)=p_i\). Set \[x_{I_k}^{k+1}\in\arg\min_x\left\{f_{I_k}(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\left\|A_{I_k}x+\sum_{j\neq I_k}A_jx_j^k-c+u^k\right\|^2+\frac12\|x-x_{I_k}^k\|_{P_{I_k}}^2\right\},\] keep \(x_j^{k+1}=x_j^k\) for \(j\neq I_k\), and update \(u^{k+1}=u^k+\sum_iA_ix_i^{k+1}-c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample one primal block, minimize its stabilized augmented-Lagrangian subproblem with other blocks fixed, then update the scaled multiplier using the new residual.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is proper, closed, and convex, and each sampled subproblem attains a minimizer.
Each proximal operator satisfies \(P_i\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed rule defines a serial randomized block-ADMM iteration in which every block is sampled with positive probability.

notation.meaning: Random block index selected at iteration k.
Scaled multiplier for the coupling constraint.

children.title: Stochastic ADMM
children.top_down_role: ADMM with stochastic objective or oracle information.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linearized stochastic ADMM for a two-block convex expectation model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min_{x,z}\{f(x)+g(z):Ax+Bz=c\}\), where \(f(x)=\mathbb E[F(x;\xi)]\). Given \((x^0,z^0,y^0)\), penalty \(\rho>0\), stepsizes \(\eta_k>0\), and samples \(\xi_k\), choose \(G_k\) with \(\mathbb E[G_k\mid\mathcal F_k]\in\partial f(x^k)\), and iterate
\[
x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_x\left\{F(x^k;\xi_k)+\langle G_k,x-x^k\rangle+\langle y^k,Ax+Bz^k-c\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax+Bz^k-c\|^2+\frac{1}{2\eta_k}\|x-x^k\|^2\right\},
\]
\[
z^{k+1}\in\arg\min_z\left\{g(z)+\langle y^k,Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c\|^2\right\},\qquad y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c).
\]
A stopping rule may use averaged objective and feasibility residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each iteration replaces one ADMM block objective by a sampled stochastic linearization, retains the other proximal augmented-Lagrangian update, and then updates the multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, convex functions on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
\(G_k\) is conditionally unbiased and has finite conditional second moment.
\(\arg\min\) sets in the displayed updates are nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x^{k+1},z^{k+1},y^{k+1})\) is the next stochastic-ADMM iterate.

notation.meaning: Information available before sampling at iteration k.

children.title: Online ADMM
children.top_down_role: Sequential-data ADMM organized through online performance criteria.

knowledge_statements.title: Online ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential two-block ADMM with regret and cumulative feasibility criteria.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For rounds \(t=1,\ldots,T\), let \((x_t,z_t)\) be chosen from past information and incur \(f_t(x_t)+g(z_t)\) for the constraint \(Ax+Bz=c\). After observing convex \(f_t\), update
\[
x_{t+1}\in\arg\min_x\left\{f_t(x)+\langle y_t,Ax+Bz_t-c\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax+Bz_t-c\|^2+\frac{1}{2\eta_t}\|x-x_t\|^2\right\},
\]
\[
z_{t+1}\in\arg\min_z\left\{g(z)+\langle y_t,Ax_{t+1}+Bz-c\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax_{t+1}+Bz-c\|^2\right\},\quad y_{t+1}=y_t+\rho(Ax_{t+1}+Bz_{t+1}-c).
\]
Performance is measured by regret \(R_T=\sum_{t=1}^T[f_t(x_t)+g(z_t)]-\min_{Ax+Bz=c}\sum_{t=1}^T[f_t(x)+g(z)]\) together with cumulative feasibility violation \(V_T=\sum_{t=1}^T\|Ax_t+Bz_t-c\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Online ADMM processes losses sequentially and is evaluated by objective regret relative to the best fixed feasible pair and by cumulative constraint violation.
assumptions_latex: \(f_t\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, convex functions.
\(\rho>0\), \(\eta_t>0\), and the update subproblems attain minimizers.
\(\{(x,z):Ax+Bz=c\}\cap(\operatorname{dom}f_t\times\operatorname{dom}g)\neq\varnothing\) for relevant \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recursion defines online iterates and the criteria \(R_T\) and \(V_T\).

notation.meaning: Static objective regret through round T.
Cumulative norm of primal constraint residuals.

review_flags: exact online-ADMM timing and performance convention require an authoritative source

children.title: Grouped Two-Block Reductions
children.top_down_role: Multi-component models reorganized into a two-block structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Grouped Two-Block Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact regrouping of a separable multi-component constraint into two product-space blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\dot\cup J=\{1,\ldots,m\}\). For the model
\[
\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_m}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\quad\text{subject to}\quad\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i=c,
\]
define \(u=(x_i)_{i\in I}\), \(v=(x_j)_{j\in J}\), \(F(u)=\sum_{i\in I}f_i(x_i)\), \(G(v)=\sum_{j\in J}f_j(x_j)\), \(A_Iu=\sum_{i\in I}A_ix_i\), and \(A_Jv=\sum_{j\in J}A_jx_j\). Then the original problem is exactly
\[
\min_{u,v}\;F(u)+G(v)\quad\text{subject to}\quad A_Iu+A_Jv=c.
\]
Consequently, ordinary two-block ADMM applies to \((u,v)\); internal block separability yields parallel component updates only when each grouped augmented subproblem itself separates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partitioning components into two product-space groups converts the multi-component model exactly into two-block form, though the grouped subproblems need not remain separable.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is proper, closed, and convex.
All \(A_i\) map into a common finite-dimensional constraint space.
\(I\) and \(J\) are nonempty and disjoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The multi-component and grouped two-block formulations have identical feasible points and objective values under the product-space identification.

notation.meaning: A disjoint two-group partition of component indices.

children.title: Proximal Multi-Block ADMM
children.top_down_role: Multi-block variants stabilized by blockwise proximal geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Multi-Block ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gauss–Seidel multi-block ADMM stabilized by positive-semidefinite block proximal terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min\{\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i):\sum_{i=1}^mA_ix_i=c\}\), define
\[
\mathcal L_\rho(x;y)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)+\left\langle y,\sum_{i=1}^mA_ix_i-c\right\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\left\|\sum_{i=1}^mA_ix_i-c\right\|^2.
\]
Given \((x^0,y^0)\), \(\rho>0\), and self-adjoint \(P_i\succeq0\), perform for \(i=1,\ldots,m\)
\[
x_i^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x_i}\left\{\mathcal L_\rho(x_1^{k+1},\ldots,x_{i-1}^{k+1},x_i,x_{i+1}^k,\ldots,x_m^k;y^k)+\frac12\|x_i-x_i^k\|_{P_i}^2\right\},
\]
then set \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\tau\rho(\sum_iA_ix_i^{k+1}-c)\). Output an iterate when prescribed primal and dual residual tolerances hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method performs sequential augmented-Lagrangian block minimizations, adding a blockwise proximal metric before the relaxed multiplier update.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(P_i\succeq0\), \(\rho>0\), and \(\tau>0\).
Every displayed block subproblem attains a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x^{k+1},y^{k+1})\) is the next proximal multi-block ADMM iterate.

notation.meaning: Quadratic form given by the block proximal operator.

children.title: Corrected Multi-Block ADMM Family
