children.title: Corrected Multi-Block ADMM
children.top_down_role: Multi-block ADMM variants equipped with an explicit correction phase.

knowledge_statements.title: Corrected Multi-Block ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predictor–corrector architecture for sequential multi-block augmented-Lagrangian updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(w=(x_1,\ldots,x_m,y)\). From \(w^k\), first compute a Gauss–Seidel ADMM predictor \(\widetilde w^k\): sequentially minimize the augmented Lagrangian in every primal block and then form \(\widetilde y^k=y^k+\rho(\sum_iA_i\widetilde x_i^k-c)\). Given a fixed linear correction operator \(M\), set
\[
w^{k+1}=w^k-M(w^k-\widetilde w^k).
\]
The correction is admissible relative to a self-adjoint metric \(H\succ0\) when there exists \(\gamma>0\) such that
\[
\|w^{k+1}-w^\star\|_H^2\leq\|w^k-w^\star\|_H^2-\gamma\|w^k-\widetilde w^k\|^2
\]
for every primal-dual solution \(w^\star\). Stop when the predictor residual and primal feasibility residual meet prescribed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sequential multi-block ADMM prediction is followed by a linear correction chosen to restore metric descent toward the primal-dual solution set.
assumptions_latex: The separable linearly constrained convex problem has a primal-dual solution.
All predictor subproblems attain minimizers.
\(M\) and \(H\succ0\) satisfy the displayed descent condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The predictor–correction recursion defines a corrected multi-block ADMM sequence with Fejér-type metric descent.

notation.meaning: Metric in which correction descent is required.

review_flags: named correction architecture has multiple literature variants
authoritative algorithm and admissibility conditions required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Predictor–corrector multi-block ADMM has several inequivalent formulations. A source is required for the predictor definition, correction operator, metric, and asserted Fejér-type descent condition.

children.title: Back-Substitution Multi-Block ADMM
children.top_down_role: Multi-block ADMM variants using backward substitution to repair coupled block progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Back-Substitution Multi-Block ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Triangular backward correction of a forward multi-block ADMM predictor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Partition \(w=(x_2,\ldots,x_m,y)\), leaving the first primal block uncorrected. At iteration \(k\), compute a forward Gauss–Seidel ADMM predictor \(\widetilde w^k\). Let \(D\succ0\) be block diagonal and \(L\) strictly block lower triangular, and assume \(D+L\) is nonsingular. Define the corrected variables by the backward triangular solve
\[
(D+L^*)\bigl(w^{k+1}-w^k\bigr)=-\alpha D\bigl(w^k-\widetilde w^k\bigr),\qquad 0<\alpha<2.
\]
Equivalently, process the corrected blocks in reverse order using already corrected later blocks. The full next iterate combines the predictor for the first block with this corrected \(w^{k+1}\). Stop when primal feasibility and \(\|w^k-\widetilde w^k\|\) satisfy prescribed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After a forward multi-block prediction, a reverse triangular solve corrects the coupled later blocks and multiplier before the next iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(D\succ0\), \(L\) is strictly block lower triangular, and \(D+L\) is nonsingular.
The forward predictor subproblems attain minimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed reverse solve produces the back-substituted corrected iterate \(w^{k+1}\).
review_flags: matrix convention varies across back-substitution ADMM sources
exact corrected block set and relaxation range require citation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but the corrected block set, triangular system, adjoint convention, and range 0<alpha<2 are variant-dependent and unsupported.

children.title: Correction Architecture Relations
children.top_down_role: Structural comparison of correction placement across repaired multi-block schemes.

knowledge_statements.title: Correction Architecture Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common linear representation connecting direct, triangular, and symmetric-sweep corrections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\widetilde w^k=P(w^k)\) be a multi-block ADMM predictor. A linear correction architecture has the common form
\[
w^{k+1}=w^k-C(w^k-\widetilde w^k).
\]
The uncorrected method corresponds to \(C=I\). A back-substitution correction is obtained when \(C\) is applied through a nonsingular block-triangular solve. If the predictor coupling has decomposition \(Q=D+L+L^*\) with \(D\succ0\), a symmetric Gauss–Seidel sweep induces the self-adjoint effective metric
\[
Q_{\mathrm{sGS}}=Q+LD^{-1}L^*=(D+L)D^{-1}(D+L^*).
\]
Thus triangular correction and symmetric sweeping are distinct implementations of a predictor correction; they coincide only when their induced correction operators agree, and both reduce to the direct predictor when the off-diagonal coupling vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Direct prediction, backward substitution, and symmetric Gauss–Seidel sweeping fit one predictor–correction form but generally induce different correction operators and metrics.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a well-defined multi-block predictor.
\(Q=D+L+L^*\) with \(D\succ0\) and \(L\) strictly block lower triangular.
All displayed linear solves are nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The three architectures are related by their choices of \(C\) and the induced factorized metric \(Q_{\mathrm{sGS}}\).

notation.meaning: Correction operator applied to the predictor residual.

review_flags: architectural equivalence requires a source fixing matrix conventions
sGS factorization is standard but its ADMM identification needs confirmation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sGS factorization is algebraically consistent, but the claimed common ADMM predictor–correction interpretation and reductions require a source fixing the operator and matrix conventions.

children.title: Symmetric Gauss-Seidel ADMM
children.top_down_role: Multi-block methods organized through symmetric block sweeps.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric Gauss-Seidel ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multi-block ADMM using one forward and one backward primal sweep per multiplier update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For augmented Lagrangian \(\mathcal L_\rho(x_1,\ldots,x_m;y)\), define the block minimizer map
\[
\mathcal M_i(v_{-i};y)\in\arg\min_u\mathcal L_\rho(v_1,\ldots,v_{i-1},u,v_{i+1},\ldots,v_m;y).
\]
Starting from \((x^k,y^k)\), perform a forward sweep \(i=1,\ldots,m\), setting \(\widetilde x_i^k=\mathcal M_i(\widetilde x_1^k,\ldots,\widetilde x_{i-1}^k,x_{i+1}^k,\ldots,x_m^k;y^k)\). Set \(x_m^{k+1}=\widetilde x_m^k\), then perform the backward sweep \(i=m-1,\ldots,1\), setting
\[
x_i^{k+1}=\mathcal M_i(\widetilde x_1^k,\ldots,\widetilde x_{i-1}^k,x_{i+1}^{k+1},\ldots,x_m^{k+1};y^k).
\]
Finally update \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\tau\rho(\sum_iA_ix_i^{k+1}-c)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each iteration symmetrizes sequential block minimization by a forward sweep followed by a reverse sweep, then updates the multiplier.
assumptions_latex: Each block minimizer map \(\mathcal M_i\) is nonempty.
The objective is block-separable and the coupling constraint is linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two sweeps and multiplier step define the next symmetric Gauss–Seidel ADMM iterate.

notation.meaning: Exact augmented-Lagrangian minimizer in block i.

review_flags: exact sGS-ADMM sweep conventions and admissible variants require citation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and two-sweep architecture fit the leaf, but no citation supports this exact forward/backward minimization order, unchanged last block, and multiplier-update convention.

children.title: Averaged-Operator Mechanism

knowledge_statements.title: Averaged-Operator Mechanism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric descent generated by an averaged fixed-point operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H\) be \(\alpha\)-averaged on a real Hilbert space, meaning
\[
T=(1-\alpha)I+\alpha R,
\]
where \(0<\alpha<1\) and \(R\) is nonexpansive. Then, for every \(x,y\in\mathcal H\),
\[
\|Tx-Ty\|^2\leq\|x-y\|^2-\frac{1-\alpha}{\alpha}\|(I-T)x-(I-T)y\|^2.
\]
In particular, if \(z\in\operatorname{Fix}T\), the Picard update \(x^{k+1}=Tx^k\) satisfies
\[
\|x^{k+1}-z\|^2\leq\|x^k-z\|^2-\frac{1-\alpha}{\alpha}\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2.
\]
This descent inequality is the averaged-operator mechanism used to control fixed-point residuals in splitting iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averagedness strengthens nonexpansiveness by a quantitative decrease proportional to the squared fixed-point residual.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) is a real Hilbert space.
\(T=(1-\alpha)I+\alpha R\), where \(0<\alpha<1\) and \(R\) is nonexpansive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed averagedness and fixed-point descent inequalities hold.

notation.meaning: Set of fixed points of T.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Point Mechanism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak convergence of averaged Picard iteration in Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H\) be \(\alpha\)-averaged with \(0<\alpha<1\), and suppose \(\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\). For any \(x^0\in\mathcal H\), define \(x^{k+1}=Tx^k\). Then \((x^k)\) is Fejér monotone with respect to \(\operatorname{Fix}T\),
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2<\infty,
\]
and hence \(\|x^k-Tx^k\|\to0\). Moreover, \(x^k\rightharpoonup x^\star\) for some \(x^\star\in\operatorname{Fix}T\). If \(\mathcal H\) is finite-dimensional, this convergence is in norm. Thus a splitting iteration represented by such a fixed-point map converges once its fixed points encode the desired primal-dual solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Picard iteration of an averaged operator with a fixed point is asymptotically regular and converges weakly to a fixed point, strongly in finite dimensions.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) is a real Hilbert space.
\(T\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged for some \(0<\alpha<1\).
\(\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(x^\star\in\operatorname{Fix}T\) such that \(x^k\rightharpoonup x^\star\), with norm convergence in finite dimensions.

notation.meaning: Weak convergence in the Hilbert space.

children.title: Averagedness–Fixed-Point Interface

knowledge_statements.title: Averagedness–Fixed-Point Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface transferring operator convergence to primal-dual solution convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H\) be \(\alpha\)-averaged with \(\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\), let \(S\) be a primal-dual solution set, and let \(D:\mathcal H\to\mathcal U\) be continuous with
\[
D(\operatorname{Fix}T)=S.
\]
For the iteration \(w^{k+1}=Tw^k\), averagedness supplies Fejér descent and \(\|w^k-Tw^k\|\to0\); the fixed-point identity supplies the solution interpretation. If \(w^k\rightharpoonup w^\star\in\operatorname{Fix}T\) and \(D\) is weak-to-weak sequentially continuous, then
\[
D(w^k)\rightharpoonup D(w^\star)\in S.
\]
In finite dimensions, continuity of \(D\) and norm convergence of \(w^k\) give \(D(w^k)\to D(w^\star)\in S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averagedness proves convergence of the fixed-point state; a continuous decoding map then transfers that convergence to primal-dual solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is averaged and \(\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\).
\(D(\operatorname{Fix}T)=S\).
\(D\) has the stated continuity for the selected convergence topology.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The decoded iterates converge to an element of the primal-dual solution set \(S\).

notation.meaning: Map decoding a fixed-point state into primal-dual variables.

children.title: Fejér Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Distance-based convergence organization for unperturbed splitting sequences.

knowledge_statements.title: Fejér Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distance descent relative to a nonempty target set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be a nonempty subset of a Hilbert space \(\mathcal H\). A sequence \((x^k)\) is Fejér monotone with respect to \(C\) when
\[
\|x^{k+1}-z\|\leq\|x^k-z\|\qquad\text{for every }z\in C\text{ and every }k\geq0.
\]
More quantitatively, if there exist \(\eta_k\geq0\) and residuals \(r^k\) such that
\[
\|x^{k+1}-z\|^2\leq\|x^k-z\|^2-\eta_k\|r^k\|^2
\]
for every \(z\in C\), then each distance sequence \((\|x^k-z\|)\) converges and
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\eta_k\|r^k\|^2<\infty.
\]
If \(\inf_k\eta_k>0\), then \(r^k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fejér descent makes every distance to the target set nonincreasing; quantitative descent additionally forces weighted residual square summability.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathcal H\) is nonempty.
The displayed descent inequality holds for every \(z\in C\).
\(\eta_k\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Distances to \(C\) converge and \(\sum_k\eta_k\|r^k\|^2<\infty\); if \(\inf_k\eta_k>0\), then \(r^k\to0\).

notation.meaning: Target set, typically a fixed-point or solution set.
Residual controlled by the descent inequality.

knowledge_statements.title: Quasi-Fejér Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic quasi-Fejér convergence relative to a nonempty solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space, let \(S\subset H\) be nonempty and closed, and let \((z^k)_{k\geq 0}\subset H\). If there exists \((\varepsilon_k)_{k\geq 0}\subset[0,\infty)\) with \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_k<\infty\) such that \[\|z^{k+1}-s\|^2\leq \|z^k-s\|^2+\varepsilon_k\quad\text{for every }s\in S\text{ and }k\geq0,\] then \((z^k)\) is bounded and \(\|z^k-s\|\) converges for every \(s\in S\). If every weak sequential cluster point of \((z^k)\) belongs to \(S\), then \((z^k)\) converges weakly to a point of \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A summably perturbed Fejér inequality yields boundedness and convergent distances; if all weak cluster points are solutions, the entire sequence converges weakly to a solution.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a Hilbert space and \(S\subset H\) is nonempty and closed.
\(\varepsilon_k\geq0\) and \(\sum_k\varepsilon_k<\infty\).
Every weak sequential cluster point of \((z^k)\) lies in \(S\) for the weak-convergence conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((z^k)\) is bounded, every distance \(\|z^k-s\|\) converges, and \(z^k\rightharpoonup z^\star\in S\) under cluster-point identification.

notation.meaning: nonempty target or primal-dual solution set

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elementary scalar recursion and explicit counterexample
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between summable and persistent errors in Fejer-type recursions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((d_k)_{k\geq0}\) and \((\varepsilon_k)_{k\geq0}\) be nonnegative real sequences satisfying \[d_{k+1}^2\leq d_k^2+\varepsilon_k\quad\text{for every }k\geq0.\] If \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_k<\infty\), then \((d_k^2)\) converges to a finite limit. Without summability, the inequality alone need not yield boundedness or convergence, even when \(\varepsilon_k\to0\): setting \(d_0=0\), \(\varepsilon_k=1/(k+1)\), and \[d_k^2=\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\frac{1}{j+1}\quad(k\geq1)\] gives equality in the recursion, while \(d_k\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summable nonnegative errors force a scalar Fejer-type distance sequence to converge. Mere pointwise decay of the errors is insufficient because nonsummable vanishing errors can accumulate and make the distance unbounded.

knowledge_statements.title: Lyapunov Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lyapunov convergence template for deterministic primal-dual splitting iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((z^k)_{k\geq0}\) be iterates, let \(V_k=V(z^k)\geq0\), and let \(r_k\geq0\) measure a fixed-point, feasibility, or primal-dual residual. If constants \(c>0\) and errors \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\) satisfy \[V_{k+1}+c r_k^2\leq V_k+\varepsilon_k,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_k<\infty,\] then \((V_k)\) converges and \(\sum_k r_k^2<\infty\); hence \(r_k\to0\). If the sublevel sets of \(V\) are bounded, then \((z^k)\) is bounded, enabling cluster-point identification by the optimality or fixed-point conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower-bounded energy with summable errors and definite residual decrease converges, makes squared residuals summable, and yields bounded iterates when its sublevel sets are bounded.
assumptions_latex: \(V_{k+1}+c r_k^2\leq V_k+\varepsilon_k\) with \(\sum_k\varepsilon_k<\infty\).
Bounded sublevel sets are required only for boundedness of the iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_k\) converges, \(\sum_k r_k^2<\infty\), \(r_k\to0\), and coercive energy control makes \((z^k)\) bounded.

knowledge_statements.title: Descent Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient-decrease mechanism for residual decay and finite-length estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((V_k)_{k\geq0}\subset\mathbb R\) be bounded below, and let \((s_k)_{k\geq0}\subset[0,\infty)\). If \[V_{k+1}\leq V_k-cs_k^2\] for some \(c>0\) and every \(k\), then telescoping gives \[c\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}s_k^2\leq V_0-V_N\leq V_0-\inf_j V_j.\] Consequently \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}s_k^2<\infty\) and \(s_k\to0\). When \(s_k=\|z^{k+1}-z^k\|\), this yields asymptotic regularity, although square summability alone does not imply the finite-length property \(\sum_k s_k<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower-bounded energy with uniform quadratic decrease makes step or residual squares summable and forces them to vanish, but does not alone give finite trajectory length.
assumptions_latex: \((V_k)\) is bounded below.
\(s_k\geq0\) and \(V_{k+1}\leq V_k-cs_k^2\) for a constant \(c>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_k s_k^2<\infty\) and \(s_k\to0\); for step lengths, the iterates are asymptotically regular.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((V_k)_{k\geq0}\subset\mathbb R\), \((D_k)_{k\geq0}\subset[0,\infty)\), and \((\varepsilon_k)_{k\geq0}\subset\mathbb R\). If \[V_{k+1}+D_k\leq V_k+\varepsilon_k\quad\text{for every }k\geq0,\] then, for every integer \(N\geq1\), \[V_N+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}D_k\leq V_0+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\varepsilon_k.\] If, in addition, \((V_k)\) is bounded below and \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_k\) converges to a finite real value, then \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}D_k<\infty\). The cumulative inequalities alone do not, in general, imply each corresponding one-step inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-step energy-descent inequality yields its cumulative telescoped bound. A lower energy bound and a finite total error then imply finite total dissipation, but the family of cumulative upper bounds is not generally equivalent to the one-step inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Demiclosedness Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-limit identification through demiclosedness of a fixed-point residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space and let \(T:H\to H\) be nonexpansive. Then \(I-T\) is demiclosed at \(0\): for every sequence \((z^k)\subset H\), \[z^k\rightharpoonup \bar z\quad\text{and}\quad z^k-Tz^k\to0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \bar z-T\bar z=0.\] Hence, if an ADMM or primal-dual splitting iteration is represented as an asymptotically regular fixed-point iteration of a nonexpansive or averaged operator, each weak cluster point is a fixed point of that operator. A separate decoding relation is required to translate that fixed point into a primal-dual solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonexpansive fixed-point map, weak convergence plus a strongly vanishing residual identifies the weak limit as a fixed point.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a Hilbert space.
\(T:H\to H\) is nonexpansive.
\(z^k\rightharpoonup\bar z\) and \(z^k-Tz^k\to0\) strongly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar z\in\operatorname{Fix}T\), equivalently \(\bar z-T\bar z=0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Weak-Limit Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Opial-type weak convergence criterion for deterministic splitting sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space, let \(S\subset H\) be nonempty, and let \((z^k)\subset H\). Assume that, for every \(s\in S\), the limit \(\lim_{k\to\infty}\|z^k-s\|\) exists, and that every weak sequential cluster point of \((z^k)\) lies in \(S\). Then there exists \(z^\star\in S\) such that \(z^k\rightharpoonup z^\star\). In splitting analyses, the first hypothesis is usually supplied by Fejér or quasi-Fejér estimates, while demiclosedness or closed optimality relations supply the second.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If distances to every solution converge and all weak cluster points are solutions, a Hilbert-space sequence converges weakly to one solution.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-based certificate that a cluster point satisfies the splitting fixed-point condition.

knowledge_statements.title: Duality-Based ADMM Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: ADMM as Douglas–Rachford splitting on the dual inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x,y}\{f(x)+g(y):Ax+By=c\}\), where \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, convex functions on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces and a primal-dual saddle point exists. Its dual optimality condition is \[0\in \partial(f^*\circ(-A^*))(\lambda)+\partial(g^*\circ(-B^*))(\lambda)+c,\] with the constant term assigned to either summand. For penalty \(\rho>0\), the scaled ADMM primal updates and multiplier update are equivalent, after the standard affine identification of auxiliary variables, to Douglas–Rachford splitting with stepsize \(\rho\) applied to this dual inclusion. Thus fixed points decode to dual solutions and associated primal minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a linearly constrained two-block convex problem, ADMM is Douglas–Rachford splitting on the dual optimality inclusion after an affine change of variables.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
The constraint is \(Ax+By=c\), and a primal-dual saddle point exists.
The standard exact two-block ADMM with penalty \(\rho>0\) is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The ADMM orbit is affinely equivalent to a Douglas–Rachford orbit for the dual inclusion, and its fixed points encode primal-dual solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Energy Recursions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robbins–Siegmund almost-supermartingale convergence for stochastic splitting energies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal F_k)_{k\geq0}\) be a filtration, and let \(V_k,U_k,A_k,B_k\) be nonnegative, \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable random variables satisfying \[\mathbb E[V_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]\leq(1+A_k)V_k-U_k+B_k\quad\text{almost surely}.\] If \(\sum_k A_k<\infty\) and \(\sum_k B_k<\infty\) almost surely, then \((V_k)\) converges almost surely to a finite random variable and \(\sum_kU_k<\infty\) almost surely. In stochastic ADMM analyses, \(V_k\) is an adapted primal-dual energy and \(U_k\) is the conditionally expected dissipation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An adapted nonnegative energy satisfying an almost-supermartingale recursion with summable multiplicative and additive errors converges almost surely, while its dissipation is summable.

\(\sum_kA_k<\infty\) and \(\sum_kB_k<\infty\) almost surely.

knowledge_statements.title: Summable Perturbation Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Almost-sure accumulated-error condition for stochastic and inexact splitting updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal F_k)\) be a filtration and let \(e_k\geq0\) be an \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable error entering a conditional energy inequality as \[\mathbb E[V_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]\leq V_k-U_k+e_k.\] A sufficient accumulated-error condition is \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}e_k<\infty\quad\text{almost surely}.\] If a raw perturbation \(\xi_{k+1}\) enters only through its conditional second moment, it suffices to set \(e_k=C\mathbb E[\|\xi_{k+1}\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\) and require the resulting series to be almost surely finite. Under these conditions the additive errors do not prevent almost-supermartingale convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stochastic or computational errors are controlled when their conditional contribution to the energy recursion has finite accumulated mass almost surely.
assumptions_latex: \(V_k,U_k,e_k\) are nonnegative and adapted to \((\mathcal F_k)\).
The displayed conditional energy recursion holds almost surely.
\(\sum_ke_k<\infty\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The perturbation term satisfies the additive-error hypothesis needed for almost-supermartingale energy convergence and summability of \((U_k)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P,(\mathcal F_k)_{k\geq0})\) be a filtered probability space, let \(H=H_1\oplus\cdots\oplus H_m\) be a finite orthogonal product of Hilbert spaces, and let \(z^k,\widehat z^{k+1},z^\star\) be \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable \(H\)-valued random variables. For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), suppose \(\delta_{i,k}\in\{0,1\}\) satisfies \(\mathbb P(\delta_{i,k}=1\mid\mathcal F_k)=p_i\in(0,1]\), and define \[z_i^{k+1}=z_i^k+\delta_{i,k}(\widehat z_i^{k+1}-z_i^k).\] With \[\|z\|_{P^{-1}}^2=\sum_{i=1}^m p_i^{-1}\|z_i\|^2,\] one has \[\mathbb E[\|z^{k+1}-z^\star\|_{P^{-1}}^2\mid\mathcal F_k]=\|z^k-z^\star\|_{P^{-1}}^2+\|\widehat z^{k+1}-z^\star\|^2-\|z^k-z^\star\|^2.\] Thus a deterministic full-update distance decrease transfers to a conditional expected decrease. Independence among the block indicators is not required for this identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a conditionally specified randomized block update, inverse-probability weighting gives an exact conditional distance identity. This transfers a full-update distance decrease to conditional expectation, without requiring independence among different block indicators.

children.title: Stochastic Quasi-Fejér Mechanism
children.top_down_role: Distance-based stochastic convergence organization for random fixed-point iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Quasi-Fejér Mechanism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional distance recursion used to organize almost-sure convergence of finite-dimensional stochastic primal-dual fixed-point iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_k)_{k\geq0},\mathbb P)\) be a filtered probability space, let \(S\subset H\) be nonempty and closed, and let \((z^k)\) be an adapted \(H\)-valued sequence. Suppose common nonnegative adapted sequences \((a_k),(b_k),(c_k)\) satisfy, for every \(z^\star\in S\), \[\mathbb E[\|z^{k+1}-z^\star\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\leq(1+a_k)\|z^k-z^\star\|^2-b_k+c_k\quad\text{a.s.},\] and suppose \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}a_k<\infty\) and \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}c_k<\infty\) almost surely. Then, for every \(z^\star\in S\), the sequence \((\|z^k-z^\star\|^2)\) converges almost surely, and \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}b_k<\infty\) almost surely. If every cluster point of \((z^k)\) belongs to \(S\) almost surely, then \((z^k)\) converges almost surely to an \(S\)-valued random variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In finite dimensions, summable multiplicative and additive errors in a stochastic quasi-Fejér recursion yield almost-sure distance convergence and finite accumulated descent; if all cluster points are solutions, the iterates converge almost surely to a solution.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a finite-dimensional Hilbert space and \(S\subset H\) is nonempty and closed.
\((z^k)\), \((a_k)\), \((b_k)\), and \((c_k)\) are adapted, and the latter three sequences are nonnegative.
\(\sum_k a_k<\infty\) and \(\sum_k c_k<\infty\) almost surely.
Every cluster point belongs to \(S\) almost surely for the final convergence assertion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(z^\star\in S\), \(\|z^k-z^\star\|^2\) converges and \(\sum_k b_k<\infty\) almost surely; under cluster-point identification, \(z^k\to z^\infty\in S\) almost surely.

children.title: Variance Control
children.top_down_role: Stochastic regimes organized by oracle variance behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Variance Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional second-moment condition sufficient for summable stochastic perturbations in a quasi-Fejér recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space, let \((\mathcal F_k)\) be a filtration, and let \(\widehat G_k\) be an \(H\)-valued, conditionally square-integrable stochastic oracle value. Define \(\xi_k=\widehat G_k-\mathbb E[\widehat G_k\mid\mathcal F_k]\). Let \((\sigma_k^2)\) be a nonnegative deterministic or adapted sequence satisfying \[\mathbb E[\|\xi_k\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\leq\sigma_k^2\quad\text{a.s.}\] If \(\gamma_k\geq0\) is deterministic or \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable and \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\gamma_k^2\sigma_k^2<\infty\) almost surely, then \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\gamma_k^2\mathbb E[\|\xi_k\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]<\infty\quad\text{a.s.}\] Thus the conditional quadratic contribution of the stepsize-scaled centered oracle noise is summable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A summable stepsize-weighted conditional variance envelope makes the quadratic contribution of centered oracle noise summable.
assumptions_latex: \(\widehat G_k\) is an \(H\)-valued, conditionally square-integrable random variable.
\(\sigma_k^2\geq0\) is deterministic or adapted.
\(\gamma_k\geq0\) is deterministic or \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable.
\(\sum_k\gamma_k^2\sigma_k^2<\infty\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_k\gamma_k^2\mathbb E[\|\xi_k\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]<\infty\) almost surely.

knowledge_statements.title: Sampling Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Filtration-compatible sampling rule for conditionally unbiased finite-block stochastic primal-dual oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_k\) take values in a finite component set \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\), let \(z^k\) be an \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable oracle query, and let \(g(z^k;i)\) be an integrable oracle value for each component \(i\). Suppose \[\mathbb P(I_k=i\mid\mathcal F_k)=p_{k,i},\qquad p_{k,i}\geq p_{\min}>0,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^{m}p_{k,i}=1\quad\text{a.s.}\] and \[\mathbb E[g(z^k;I_k)\mid\mathcal F_k]=G(z^k)\quad\text{a.s.}\] Then \(g(z^k;I_k)-G(z^k)\) is a martingale-difference oracle error. Moreover, every component \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) is sampled infinitely often almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many eligible blocks, uniformly positive conditional probabilities prevent starvation, while conditional unbiasedness makes the sampled-oracle error a martingale difference.
assumptions_latex: \(I_k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and \(z^k\) is \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable.
The oracle values \(g(z^k;i)\) are conditionally integrable.
\(p_{k,i}\geq p_{\min}>0\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^{m}p_{k,i}=1\) almost surely.
\(\mathbb E[g(z^k;I_k)\mid\mathcal F_k]=G(z^k)\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(z^k;I_k)-G(z^k)\) is a martingale difference, and each component is sampled infinitely often almost surely.

children.title: Oracle Bias Regimes
children.top_down_role: Analytical distinctions between unbiased, biased, and asymptotically controlled oracle access.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Bias Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification of stochastic oracle bias by its stepsize-weighted cumulative contribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space, let \(z^k\) be \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable, let \(G(z^k)\in H\) be the exact oracle value, and let \(\widehat G_k\) be a conditionally integrable stochastic estimate. Define \[b_k=\mathbb E[\widehat G_k\mid\mathcal F_k]-G(z^k).\] For coefficients \(\gamma_k\geq0\), the oracle is conditionally unbiased when \(b_k=0\) almost surely for every \(k\); it has summable effective bias when \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\gamma_k\|b_k\|<\infty\) almost surely; and it has nonsummable effective bias when this series diverges. A quasi-Fejér analysis whose bias contribution is bounded by a constant multiple of \(\gamma_k\|b_k\|\) can absorb the summable-effective regime as an additive summable error. The nonsummable-effective regime cannot be absorbed by that argument alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle bias is classified by whether its stepsize-weighted cumulative contribution is zero, summable, or nonsummable; only the summable cases can be absorbed directly as quasi-Fejér errors.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a Hilbert space and \(\widehat G_k\) is conditionally integrable.
\(z^k\) is \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable.
\(\gamma_k\geq0\) is the coefficient multiplying the oracle error.
For the quasi-Fejér consequence, the bias term is bounded by a constant multiple of \(\gamma_k\|b_k\|\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Zero or summable effective bias supplies a summable quasi-Fejér error term; nonsummable effective bias requires an argument beyond that summability mechanism.

children.top_down_role: Global convergence families for canonical convex saddle and inclusion models.

knowledge_statements.title: Basic Convex Primal-Dual Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional fixed-point convergence form covering averaged primal-dual splitting maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, let \(T:H\to H\) be \(\alpha\)-averaged with \(0<\alpha<1\), and suppose \(\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\). For \(z^0\in H\), define \[z^{k+1}=z^k+\lambda_k(Tz^k-z^k),\] where \(0<\underline\lambda\leq\lambda_k\leq\overline\lambda<1/\alpha\). Then \((z^k)\) converges to some \(z^\star\in\operatorname{Fix}T\), and \(Tz^k-z^k\to0\). If \(D:H\to X\times Y\) is continuous and maps every point of \(\operatorname{Fix}T\) to a saddle solution of the underlying proper closed convex-concave problem, then \(D(z^k)\to D(z^\star)\), a primal-dual saddle solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxed iteration of an averaged primal-dual fixed-point map converges globally under admissible relaxation; any continuous decoder of fixed points into saddle solutions preserves this convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is finite-dimensional and \(T\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged for \(0<\alpha<1\).
\(\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\).
\(0<\underline\lambda\leq\lambda_k\leq\overline\lambda<1/\alpha\).
For the decoded conclusion, \(D\) is continuous and maps fixed points to saddle solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^k\to z^\star\in\operatorname{Fix}T\) and \(\|Tz^k-z^k\|\to0\); when the stated decoder exists, \(D(z^k)\to D(z^\star)\).

children.title: Ergodic Saddle-Gap Rates
children.top_down_role: Averaged-iterate complexity for general convex-concave saddle systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Ergodic Saddle-Gap Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted-average restricted-gap bound for a finite-dimensional convex-concave saddle problem under a primal-dual energy inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, let \(\mathcal L:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty,-\infty\}\) be convex in \(x\) and concave in \(y\), and let \(Q\subset X\times Y\) be a nonempty bounded test set on which the relevant saddle expressions are defined. Let \(M\) be a self-adjoint positive-definite operator on \(X\times Y\). Suppose iterates \((x^{k+1},y^{k+1})\) and weights \(w_k>0\) satisfy, for every \(z=(x,y)\in Q\), \[\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}w_k\bigl(\mathcal L(x^{k+1},y)-\mathcal L(x,y^{k+1})\bigr)\leq\tfrac12\|z-z^0\|_M^2.\] Define \(W_N=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}w_k\), \(\bar x^N=W_N^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}w_kx^{k+1}\), \(\bar y^N=W_N^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}w_ky^{k+1}\), and \[\mathcal G_Q(\bar x^N,\bar y^N)=\sup_{(x,y)\in Q}\bigl(\mathcal L(\bar x^N,y)-\mathcal L(x,\bar y^N)\bigr).\] If \(R_Q^2=\sup_{z\in Q}\|z-z^0\|_M^2\), then \[\mathcal G_Q(\bar x^N,\bar y^N)\leq\frac{R_Q^2}{2W_N}.\] Hence \(W_N=\Omega(N)\) yields an \(O(N^{-1})\) restricted saddle-gap rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted primal-dual energy inequality yields an inverse-total-weight bound for the restricted saddle gap of the weighted averaged iterates.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces and \(\mathcal L\) is convex-concave.
\(Q\subset X\times Y\) is nonempty and bounded.
\(M\) is self-adjoint and positive definite.
The weighted energy inequality holds for every comparison pair in \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal G_Q(\bar x^N,\bar y^N)\leq R_Q^2/(2W_N)\), hence \(O(N^{-1})\) when \(W_N=\Omega(N)\).

notation.meaning: saddle gap restricted to the bounded test set Q
metric radius of the test set about the initial point

knowledge_statements.title: Last-Iterate Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ergodic decay alone does not imply a rate, or even convergence, for the unaveraged iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An \(O(N^{-1})\) ergodic bound does not by itself imply any last-iterate rate. Indeed, in \(H=\mathbb R\), let \(z^k=(-1)^k\) and \(\bar z^N=N^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}z^k\). Then \[|\bar z^N|\leq N^{-1},\qquad |z^N|=1\quad\text{for every }N.\] Hence the averages converge to \(0\) at rate \(O(N^{-1})\), while the last iterates neither converge nor approach \(0\). A last-iterate rate for a primal-dual splitting scheme therefore requires additional structure, such as contraction, strong monotonicity, metric subregularity, or a method-specific nonergodic estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fast convergence of averages does not control the current iterate; last-iterate rates need additional regularity or a dedicated nonergodic estimate.
assumptions_latex: The only available information is an ergodic estimate on averages.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No last-iterate convergence rate follows from an ergodic \(O(N^{-1})\) bound alone.

notation.meaning: Cesàro average of the first N iterates

children.title: Residual Rates
children.top_down_role: Complexity regimes stated for fixed-point, feasibility, or stationarity residuals.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonergodic fixed-point residual bound obtained from a Fejér descent inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\to H\) have a fixed point \(z^\star\), and suppose \(z^{k+1}=Tz^k\) satisfies \[\|z^{k+1}-z^\star\|_M^2\leq\|z^k-z^\star\|_M^2-c\|z^{k+1}-z^k\|_M^2\] for some \(c>0\) and every \(k\). Then, for every \(N\geq1\), \[\min_{0\leq k<N}\|z^{k+1}-z^k\|_M^2\leq\frac{\|z^0-z^\star\|_M^2}{cN}.\] Consequently the best fixed-point step residual is \(O(N^{-1/2})\) in norm and \(O(N^{-1})\) when squared. If the splitting residual is bounded by a constant multiple of this step, it has the same rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fejér descent makes squared step residuals summable and yields inverse-iteration best-residual decay.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) defines a positive-definite norm.
\(z^\star\in\operatorname{Fix}T\).
The displayed Fejér descent inequality holds with \(c>0\).

children.title: Best-Iterate Rate Comparisons

knowledge_statements.title: Best-Iterate Rate Comparisons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic comparison between best-iterate, weighted-average, and last-iterate residual measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_k\geq0\), let \(w_k>0\), and set \(W_N=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}w_k\). Then \[\min_{0\leq k<N}r_k\leq\frac{1}{W_N}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}w_kr_k\leq\max_{0\leq k<N}r_k.\] Therefore any cumulative estimate \(\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}w_kr_k^p\leq C\), with \(p>0\), yields \[\min_{0\leq k<N}r_k\leq(C/W_N)^{1/p}.\] This best-iterate conclusion does not bound \(r_{N-1}\) unless residual monotonicity or another last-iterate comparison is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cumulative residual bound immediately controls the best iterate, but it does not control the final iterate without extra structure.
assumptions_latex: \(\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}w_kr_k^p\leq C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{0\leq k<N}r_k\leq(C/W_N)^{1/p}\), with no general implication for \(r_{N-1}\).

notation.meaning: total weight through iteration N minus one

knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Curvature Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accelerated gap regime produced by strong convexity in one saddle component and growing estimate weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x\max_y\mathcal L(x,y)=f(x)+\langle Kx,y\rangle-g^*(y)\), where \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex with \(\mu>0\), while \(g^*\) is merely convex. Suppose an accelerated primal-dual scheme generates an ergodic pair \((\bar x^N,\bar y^N)\), weights \(t_N\), and an energy \(E_0<\infty\) such that \[t_N^2\bigl(\mathcal L(\bar x^N,y)-\mathcal L(x,\bar y^N)\bigr)\leq E_0\] for every comparison pair in a bounded test set, with \(t_N\geq c(N+1)\). Then the restricted saddle gap is at most \(E_0/[c^2(N+1)^2]\), hence is \(O(N^{-2})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity on one side can support quadratic inverse-iteration decay when the accelerated energy uses linearly growing weights.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex and \(g^*\) is convex.
The accelerated energy inequality holds on a bounded test set.
\(t_N\geq c(N+1)\) for some \(c>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal L(\bar x^N,y)-\mathcal L(x,\bar y^N)\leq E_0/[c^2(N+1)^2]=O(N^{-2})\).

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sided Curvature Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong convexity of both saddle components induces strong monotonicity and uniqueness of the saddle point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be real Hilbert spaces, let \(K:X\to Y\) be bounded and linear, let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and \(\mu_x\)-strongly convex, and let \(g^*:Y\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and \(\mu_y\)-strongly convex, where \(\mu_x,\mu_y>0\). Define \[\mathcal L(x,y)=f(x)+\langle Kx,y\rangle-g^*(y),\qquad A(x,y)=\bigl(\partial f(x)+K^*y,\ \partial g^*(y)-Kx\bigr).\] For \(z=(x,y)\), \(z'=(x',y')\), \(u=(u_x,u_y)\in A(z)\), and \(u'=(u'_x,u'_y)\in A(z')\), \[\langle u-u',z-z'\rangle\geq\mu_x\|x-x'\|^2+\mu_y\|y-y'\|^2\geq\mu\|z-z'\|^2,\] where \(\mu=\min\{\mu_x,\mu_y\}\) and \(X\times Y\) carries its product norm. Thus \(A\\) is \(\mu\)-strongly monotone and has at most one zero. If a zero exists, it is the unique saddle point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the product Hilbert space, strong convexity of both primal and dual components makes the saddle operator strongly monotone; existence then gives a unique saddle point.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are real Hilbert spaces.
\(f\) and \(g^*\) are proper, closed, and strongly convex with moduli \(\mu_x,\mu_y>0\).
\(K:X\to Y\) is bounded and linear.
A zero of \(A\) exists for the existence-and-uniqueness conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\) is \(\min\{\mu_x,\mu_y\}\)-strongly monotone, and \(\operatorname{zer}A\) contains at most one point.

notation.meaning: minimum of the two curvature moduli

children.title: Linear Rate Regimes
children.top_down_role: Geometric convergence regimes for suitably structured primal-dual methods.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Rate Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resolvent contraction theorem giving a canonical linear regime under strong monotonicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximally \(\mu\)-strongly monotone on a Hilbert space, with \(\mu>0\), and assume \(\operatorname{zer}A=\{z^\star\}\). For a fixed \(\gamma>0\), define the proximal iteration \[z^{k+1}=J_{\gamma A}z^k=(I+\gamma A)^{-1}z^k.\] The resolvent is Lipschitz with constant \(q=(1+\gamma\mu)^{-1}<1\). Consequently, \[\|z^k-z^\star\|\leq q^k\|z^0-z^\star\|.\] Any primal-dual splitting map that is contractive in an equivalent metric obeys the analogous geometric estimate in that metric, with its own contraction factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong monotonicity makes the proximal resolvent contractive, producing geometric convergence to the unique primal-dual solution.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is maximally \(\mu\)-strongly monotone with \(\mu>0\).
\(\operatorname{zer}A\neq\varnothing\).
The proximal parameter \(\gamma\) is fixed and positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|z^k-z^\star\|\leq(1+\gamma\mu)^{-k}\|z^0-z^\star\|\).

children.title: Curvature–Rate Interface
children.top_down_role: Structural relationship between bilateral curvature and geometric rate behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature–Rate Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lyapunov interface through which curvature yields a linear primal-dual rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_k\ge 0\) be a Lyapunov error for a primal-dual splitting sequence, with \(E_k=0\) exactly on the solution set. Suppose curvature of the primal-dual model and metric regularity of its coupling imply, for some \(\delta>0\), the one-step inequality \[E_{k+1}+\delta E_{k+1}\le E_k.\] Then \[E_k\le (1+\delta)^{-k}E_0.\] Consequently, every error quantity \(d_k\) satisfying \(d_k^2\le cE_k\), where \(c>0\), converges R-linearly with factor at most \((1+\delta)^{-1/2}\). Thus curvature produces a linear rate precisely when it strengthens ordinary descent into a uniform error-to-decrease inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Curvature yields a linear primal-dual rate when it converts Lyapunov descent into a uniform contraction; quantities controlled by that Lyapunov error inherit the rate.
assumptions_latex: \(E_k\ge 0\) and \(E_k=0\) exactly at solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Error-Bound Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear fixed-point convergence under a global residual error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be an \(\alpha\)-averaged mapping on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, where \(0<\alpha<1\), and let \(S=\operatorname{Fix}T\ne\varnothing\). For \(w^{k+1}=Tw^k\), suppose the residual error bound \[\operatorname{dist}(w,S)\le \kappa\lVert w-Tw\rVert\] holds on the invariant level set containing the iterates. If \(\kappa^2>(1-\alpha)/\alpha\), then \[\operatorname{dist}(w^{k+1},S)^2\le q^2\operatorname{dist}(w^k,S)^2,\qquad q^2=1-\frac{1-\alpha}{\alpha\kappa^2}<1.\] Hence any ADMM realization whose primal-dual state is governed by \(T\) converges Q-linearly in distance to its fixed-point set on that level set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An averaged ADMM fixed-point map converges linearly when distance to its solution set is uniformly bounded by a multiple of its fixed-point residual.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged with \(0<\alpha<1\), and \(S=\operatorname{Fix}T\ne\varnothing\).
\(\operatorname{dist}(w,S)\le\kappa\lVert w-Tw\rVert\) on an invariant level set.
\(\kappa^2>(1-\alpha)/\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(w^{k+1},S)\le q\operatorname{dist}(w^k,S)\) with \(q=\sqrt{1-(1-\alpha)/(\alpha\kappa^2)}<1\).

knowledge_statements.title: Sharpness Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rate transfer from merit decay to distance under sharp growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be the nonempty solution set of a primal-dual problem, and let \(\Phi\) be a nonnegative merit function with \(\Phi^*=\inf\Phi\). Suppose that, on a set containing the iterates, \[\Phi(w)-\Phi^*\ge \mu\operatorname{dist}(w,S)\] for some \(\mu>0\). Then every bound \(\Phi(w^k)-\Phi^*\le a_k\) implies \[\operatorname{dist}(w^k,S)\le \frac{a_k}{\mu}.\] In particular, a merit rate \(a_k=C(k+1)^{-p}\) yields the same \(O(k^{-p})\) distance rate, while a geometric merit bound \(a_k=Cq^k\), with \(0<q<1\), yields R-linear convergence in distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sharp growth converts any merit-function rate directly into the same-order distance-to-solution rate, including sublinear and geometric regimes.
assumptions_latex: \(S\ne\varnothing\) and \(\Phi^*=\inf\Phi\).
\(\Phi(w)-\Phi^*\ge\mu\operatorname{dist}(w,S)\) with \(\mu>0\) on the iterate region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(w^k,S)\le a_k/\mu\) whenever \(\Phi(w^k)-\Phi^*\le a_k\).

children.title: Local–Global Growth Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Local–Global Growth Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes contraction valid from initialization from eventual contraction within an invariant growth neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a nonempty solution set, let \(w^k\) be iterates, and define \(R_k=R(w^k)\). Suppose that on a region containing the relevant iterates, \[E_{k+1}\le E_k-cR_k^2,\qquad E_k\le C\operatorname{dist}(w^k,S)^2,\] where \(E_k\ge0\), \(c>0\), and \(C>0\). If \[\operatorname{dist}(w,S)\le\kappa R(w)\] holds on that region for some \(\kappa>0\), and \(0<c\le C\kappa^2\), then \[E_{k+1}\le\left(1-\frac{c}{C\kappa^2}\right)E_k.\] When the comparison and growth bounds hold globally on an invariant level set, this contraction holds from initialization. When they hold only for \(\operatorname{dist}(w,S)\le r\), it holds only after an index \(K\) at which the iterates enter and subsequently remain in that neighborhood. Local growth alone does not provide a uniform global iteration bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global comparison and growth bounds give contraction from initialization, whereas local bounds give contraction only after the iterates enter and remain in the applicable neighborhood.
assumptions_latex: \(S\ne\varnothing\), \(E_k\ge0\), and \(R_k=R(w^k)\).
\(E_{k+1}\le E_k-cR_k^2\) and \(E_k\le C\operatorname{dist}(w^k,S)^2\), with \(c,C>0\).
\(\operatorname{dist}(w,S)\le\kappa R(w)\), with \(\kappa>0\), on the applicable global or local region.
\(0<c\le C\kappa^2\); in the local regime, the neighborhood is invariant after entry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_{k+1}\le(1-c/(C\kappa^2))E_k\) globally on an invariant level set or locally for every \(k\ge K\) after invariant neighborhood entry.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity, subproblem solvability, relative-interior feasibility, and primal attainment conditions for a two-block linearly constrained AD-PMM model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(h_1:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,\infty]\) and \(h_2:\mathbb R^p\to(-\infty,\infty]\) be proper closed convex functions; let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times p}\), \(c\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\rho>0\); and let \(G\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^p\). Assume that, for every \(a\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), both sets
\[
\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{h_1(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax\|^2+\frac12\|x\|_G^2+\langle a,x\rangle\right\},
\quad
\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in\mathbb R^p}\left\{h_2(z)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Bz\|^2+\frac12\|z\|_Q^2+\langle b,z\rangle\right\}
\]
are nonempty. Assume also that there exist \(\hat x\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}h_1)\) and \(\hat z\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}h_2)\) satisfying \(A\hat x+B\hat z=c\), and that the associated primal problem has a nonempty optimal set \(X^*\) with optimal value \(H_{\mathrm{opt}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The AD-PMM convergence assumptions require proper closed convex block objectives, positive penalty parameter, positive-semidefinite proximal matrices, nonempty minimizer sets for both proximal block subproblems under every linear perturbation, a feasible point in the relative interiors of both objective domains, and attainment of the primal optimum.
assumptions_latex: h_1:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,\infty]\text{ and }h_2:\mathbb R^p\to(-\infty,\infty]\text{ are proper, closed, and convex}
A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\ B\in\mathbb R^{m\times p},\ c\in\mathbb R^m,\ \rho>0
G\in\mathbb S_+^n,\ Q\in\mathbb S_+^p
\forall a\in\mathbb R^n,\ \forall b\in\mathbb R^p,\text{ the two stated block-subproblem argmin sets are nonempty}
\exists(\hat x,\hat z)\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}h_1)\times\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}h_2):A\hat x+B\hat z=c
X^*\neq\varnothing\text{ for the associated primal problem, with optimal value }H_{\mathrm{opt}}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{These conditions constitute the standing AD-PMM convergence hypothesis.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ergodic objective-difference and feasibility bounds for AD-PMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded simultaneous upper bounds for the objective difference and constraint residual of Cesàro-averaged AD-PMM iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose Assumption 15.2 holds, and let \(\{(x^k,z^k)\}_{k\geq0}\) be generated by AD-PMM for solving the primal problem. Let \((x^*,z^*)\) be a primal optimal solution, let \(y^*\) be a dual optimal solution, and choose \(\gamma>0\) with \(\gamma\geq2\|y^*\|\). Define
\[
C=\rho B^\top B+Q,\qquad x^{(n)}=\frac{1}{n+1}\sum_{k=0}^{n}x^{k+1},\qquad z^{(n)}=\frac{1}{n+1}\sum_{k=0}^{n}z^{k+1},
\]
and
\[
D=\|x^*-x^0\|_G^2+\|z^*-z^0\|_C^2+\frac{1}{\rho}\bigl(\gamma+\|y^0\|\bigr)^2.
\]
Then, for every integer \(n\geq0\),
\[
H(x^{(n)},z^{(n)})-H_{\mathrm{opt}}\leq\frac{D}{2(n+1)},
\qquad
\|Ax^{(n)}+Bz^{(n)}-c\|\leq\frac{D}{\gamma(n+1)}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every nonnegative n, the averages of the first n+1 AD-PMM updates have objective difference bounded above by D/[2(n+1)] and feasibility residual bounded by D/[gamma(n+1)]. These are ergodic O(1/n) upper bounds; the theorem does not assert an absolute objective error or a nonnegative objective gap at the generally infeasible averages.
assumptions_latex: \text{Assumption 15.2 holds}
\{(x^k,z^k)\}_{k\geq0}\text{ is generated by AD-PMM for the primal problem}
(x^*,z^*)\text{ is primal optimal and }y^*\text{ is dual optimal}
\gamma>0\quad\text{and}\quad\gamma\geq2\|y^*\|
C=\rho B^\top B+Q
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall n\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}:\quad H(x^{(n)},z^{(n)})-H_{\mathrm{opt}}\leq\frac{D}{2(n+1)},\qquad \|Ax^{(n)}+Bz^{(n)}-c\|\leq\frac{D}{\gamma(n+1)}

children.title: Two-Block Convex ADMM Convergence
children.top_down_role: The canonical global convergence family for exact two-block convex ADMM.

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Block Convex ADMM Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional two-block convex ADMM with a fixed positive penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\), \(Z\), and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces, let \(A:X\to Y\) and \(B:Z\to Y\) be linear maps, and let \(c\in Y\). Consider \[\min_{x\in X,\,z\in Z}\ f(x)+g(z)\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax+Bz=c,\] where \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Z\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper, closed, and convex. Assume that a primal-dual saddle point exists and that the following subproblems are attained. For fixed \(\rho>0\), define \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{f(x)+\langle y^k,Ax+Bz^k-c\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Ax+Bz^k-c\rVert^2\right\},\] \[z^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in Z}\left\{g(z)+\langle y^k,Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c\rVert^2\right\},\] and \[y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c).\] Then \(Ax^k+Bz^k-c\to0\), \(f(x^k)+g(z^k)\to p^*\), and \(y^k\) converges to a dual solution. Every cluster point of \((x^k,z^k)\) is primal optimal; consequently, the primal sequence converges whenever it has a unique cluster point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite-dimensional convex two-block problem with a saddle point and attained exact subproblems, fixed-penalty ADMM attains feasibility and objective convergence, its dual iterates converge, and every primal cluster point is optimal.
assumptions_latex: \(X\), \(Z\), and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces; \(A:X\to Y\) and \(B:Z\to Y\) are linear; and \(c\in Y\).
\(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
A primal-dual saddle point exists, every displayed block subproblem is attained, and \(\rho>0\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax^k+Bz^k-c\to0\), \(f(x^k)+g(z^k)\to p^*\), and \(y^k\to y^*\) for a dual solution \(y^*\); every primal cluster point is optimal.

notation.meaning: linear constraint maps and right-hand side

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact ADMM Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Summably perturbed fixed-point form of convex two-block ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let exact convex ADMM admit a fixed-point representation \(w^{k+1}=Tw^k\), where \(T\) is averaged on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space and \(S=\operatorname{Fix}T\ne\varnothing\). Consider the inexact iteration \[w^{k+1}=Tw^k+e^k\] with absolutely summable errors \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lVert e^k\rVert<\infty\). Then \((w^k)\) is quasi-Fejér with respect to \(S\), \(\lVert w^k-Tw^k\rVert\to0\), and \(w^k\) converges to a point of \(S\). Under the standard ADMM fixed-point correspondence, the associated primal residual tends to zero and every recovered primal-dual limit satisfies the saddle-point conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex ADMM remains convergent when its fixed-point updates contain absolutely summable errors; residuals vanish and the limiting fixed point represents a saddle point.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is averaged and \(\operatorname{Fix}T\ne\varnothing\).
\(w^{k+1}=Tw^k+e^k\) in a finite-dimensional Hilbert space.
\(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lVert e^k\rVert<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w^k\to w^*\in\operatorname{Fix}T\) and \(\lVert w^k-Tw^k\rVert\to0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Penalty Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence under bounded penalties with summable relative variation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a convex ADMM iteration use penalties \(\rho_k>0\) and suppose its scaled primal-dual state satisfies a variable-metric quasi-Fejér estimate with respect to a nonempty saddle set. Assume \[0<\underline\rho\le\rho_k\le\overline\rho<\infty,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\left|\frac{\rho_{k+1}}{\rho_k}-1\right|<\infty.\] If each block is solved exactly and the corresponding fixed-penalty ADMM operators have the same saddle-point set, then the variable-penalty state converges to that set and its fixed-point residual tends to zero. Under the ADMM primal-dual correspondence, primal feasibility is attained asymptotically and every limit point satisfies the convex saddle conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable-penalty convex ADMM converges when penalties stay uniformly positive and finite and their relative changes are summable.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\underline\rho\le\rho_k\le\overline\rho<\infty\).
\(\sum_k|\rho_{k+1}/\rho_k-1|<\infty\).
Exact block updates share a nonempty saddle-point set and satisfy a variable-metric quasi-Fejér estimate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal-dual state converges to the saddle set, and the ADMM residual converges to zero.

notation.meaning: uniform lower and upper penalty bounds

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional variable-metric splitting with uniform coercivity and summable metric growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, let \(S\ne\varnothing\) be the fixed-point set associated with a convex ADMM splitting on \(H\), and let \(M_k:H\to H\) be self-adjoint positive-definite operators. Suppose \[mI\preceq M_k\preceq MI,\qquad M_{k+1}\preceq(1+\eta_k)M_k,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\eta_k<\infty,\] for constants \(0<m\le M<\infty\) and numbers \(\eta_k\ge0\). If, for every \(s\in S\) and every \(k\ge0\), \[\lVert w^{k+1}-s\rVert_{M_{k+1}}^2\le(1+\eta_k)\lVert w^k-s\rVert_{M_k}^2-c\lVert w^{k+1}-w^k\rVert^2\] for some \(c>0\), and every cluster point of \((w^k)\) belongs to \(S\), then there exists \(w^*\in S\) such that \(w^k\to w^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a finite-dimensional space, uniformly equivalent metrics with summable growth preserve convergence when the sequence is variable-metric quasi-Fejér and all its cluster points are solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a finite-dimensional Hilbert space and \(S\ne\varnothing\).
Each \(M_k:H\to H\) is self-adjoint and positive definite, with \(mI\preceq M_k\preceq MI\).
\(M_{k+1}\preceq(1+\eta_k)M_k\), where \(\eta_k\ge0\) and \(\sum_k\eta_k<\infty\).
The displayed quasi-Fejér inequality holds for every \(s\in S\), and every cluster point of \((w^k)\) belongs to \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(w^*\in S\) such that \(w^k\to w^*\).

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Variation Controls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient joint control for simultaneous penalty and metric adaptation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For positive penalties \(\rho_k\) and self-adjoint positive-definite metrics \(M_k\), a summable joint-variation control is the existence of constants \(0<m\le M<\infty\) and a sequence \((\eta_k)\) such that \[mI\preceq M_k\preceq MI,\qquad (1+\eta_k)^{-1}M_k\preceq M_{k+1}\preceq(1+\eta_k)M_k,\] \[(1+\eta_k)^{-1}\rho_k\le\rho_{k+1}\le(1+\eta_k)\rho_k,\qquad \eta_k\ge0,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\eta_k<\infty.\] These inequalities make the successive energy norms uniformly equivalent and ensure that the accumulated multiplicative distortion from both adaptations is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint adaptation is controlled when penalties and metrics change by summable multiplicative factors while all metrics remain uniformly positive and bounded.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho_k>0\) and each \(M_k\) is self-adjoint positive definite.
\(0<m\le M<\infty\) and \(\eta_k\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successive penalty-metric energies are uniformly equivalent and have finite accumulated multiplicative variation.

knowledge_statements.title: Structured Multi-Block Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multi-block convergence obtained by exact grouping into two convex superblocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a separable convex problem with blocks \(x_1,\ldots,x_m\) and one linear constraint. Partition the indices into two nonempty groups \(I\) and \(J\), define \(u=(x_i)_{i\in I}\), \(v=(x_j)_{j\in J}\), and aggregate the objectives and constraint operators accordingly. If both grouped objectives are proper, closed, and convex, a saddle point exists, and each grouped augmented-Lagrangian subproblem is solved exactly, then applying two-block ADMM to \((u,v)\) has vanishing primal residual and convergent objective values and dual iterates. Every cluster point of the original block vector is optimal. Sequential uncorrected minimization inside a group is covered only when it exactly solves that grouped subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex multi-block problem inherits two-block ADMM convergence when its blocks are grouped into two superblocks and each grouped subproblem is solved exactly.
assumptions_latex: The blocks admit a partition into two nonempty groups with proper closed convex aggregate objectives.
A saddle point exists.
Each grouped augmented-Lagrangian subproblem is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The grouped ADMM residual vanishes, objective values and dual iterates converge, and all primal cluster points are optimal.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex ADMM Stationarity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract KL convergence regime for a bounded nonconvex ADMM sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((w^k)\) be a bounded sequence generated by a structured nonconvex ADMM method, and let \(\Psi\) be a proper lower-semicontinuous Lyapunov function bounded below. Suppose constants \(a,b>0\) satisfy \[\Psi(w^k)-\Psi(w^{k+1})\ge a\lVert w^{k+1}-w^k\rVert^2,\qquad \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial\Psi(w^{k+1}))\le b\lVert w^{k+1}-w^k\rVert.\] If \(\Psi\) has the Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz property at every cluster point and is continuous along the sequence, then \(\sum_k\lVert w^{k+1}-w^k\rVert<\infty\), the entire sequence converges to some \(w^*\), and \(0\in\partial\Psi(w^*)\). This certifies stationarity, not global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded nonconvex ADMM sequence converges to a stationary point when its Lyapunov function has sufficient decrease, a relative-error bound, and the KL property.
assumptions_latex: \((w^k)\) is bounded and \(\Psi\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, bounded below, and continuous along the sequence.
The displayed sufficient-decrease and relative-error inequalities hold.
\(\Psi\) has the Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz property at every cluster point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_k\lVert w^{k+1}-w^k\rVert<\infty\), \(w^k\to w^*\), and \(0\in\partial\Psi(w^*)\).

notation.meaning: limiting subdifferential of the Lyapunov function

knowledge_statements.title: Ergodic ADMM Sublinear Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional averaged variational-inequality rate for exact convex ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let exact two-block convex ADMM generate primal-dual states \(w^1,\ldots,w^N\) for a problem possessing a saddle point, using a fixed penalty \(\rho>0\). Define the ergodic state \(\bar w^N=N^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^N w^k\). For every bounded comparison set \(D\) containing a saddle point, the standard ADMM energy estimate implies a constant \(C_D<\infty\), depending on the initial energy, \(D\), and \(\rho\), such that \[\sup_{w\in D}\mathcal G(\bar w^N;w)\le\frac{C_D}{N}.\] Here \(\mathcal G\) is the primal-dual variational-inequality gap. Thus achieving ergodic gap at most \(\varepsilon>0\) requires at most \(\lceil C_D/\varepsilon\rceil\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaged exact convex ADMM iterates attain an O(1/N) bounded-set primal-dual gap, giving O(1/ε) iteration complexity.
assumptions_latex: The two-block problem is convex and has a saddle point.
ADMM uses exact block solves and a fixed penalty \(\rho>0\).
The comparison set \(D\) is bounded and contains a saddle point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{w\in D}\mathcal G(\bar w^N;w)\le C_D/N\), so \(N=O(1/\varepsilon)\) suffices for gap tolerance \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: arithmetic average of the first N primal-dual states

children.title: Nonergodic ADMM Residual Rates
children.top_down_role: Individual-iterate and best-iterate residual complexity.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonergodic ADMM Residual Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-point residual rates for exact two-block convex ADMM in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the ADMM/dual Douglas--Rachford state satisfy \(z^{k+1}=Tz^k\), where \(T\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged, \(0<\alpha<1\), and \(\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\). Let \(d_0=\operatorname{dist}(z^0,\operatorname{Fix}T)\), and suppose the reported primal-dual residual obeys \(\|R_k\|\le C\|z^k-Tz^k\|\). Then
\[\min_{0\le i\le k}\|R_i\|\le C d_0\sqrt{\frac{\alpha}{(1-\alpha)(k+1)}}.\]
Moreover, the fixed-point increments are nonincreasing and square summable, so
\[\|R_k\|=o(k^{-1/2}).\]
Thus an iterate with residual at most \(\varepsilon\) is found within \(O(\varepsilon^{-2})\) outer iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact convex ADMM has a best-iterate residual of order one over square-root iterations; under the fixed-point residual correspondence, the individual residual is little-o of that rate.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged and has a fixed point.
\(\|R_k\|\le C\|z^k-Tz^k\|\) for a constant \(C>0\).

notation.meaning: initial distance to the fixed-point set

children.title: Linear ADMM Rates under Error Bounds
children.top_down_role: Geometric rate families associated with error bounds and metric subregularity.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear ADMM Rates under Error Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global or local linear convergence derived from an error bound for the ADMM fixed-point map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T\) be \(\alpha\)-averaged on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, let \(S=\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\), and set \(z^{k+1}=Tz^k\). Suppose an invariant neighborhood \(U\) contains the orbit and satisfies the error bound
\[\operatorname{dist}(z,S)\le\kappa\|z-Tz\|\qquad(z\in U).\]
Then
\[\operatorname{dist}(z^{k+1},S)\le q\operatorname{dist}(z^k,S),\qquad q=\sqrt{\max\left\{0,1-\frac{1-\alpha}{\alpha\kappa^2}\right\}}<1.\]
Any ADMM primal-dual distance or residual locally bounded above by a constant multiple of \(\operatorname{dist}(z^k,S)\) therefore converges \(R\)-linearly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An error bound converting fixed-point residual into distance to the solution set turns averaged-map descent into geometric convergence of ADMM distances and controlled residuals.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged and \(S=\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\).
The orbit remains in \(U\), where \(\operatorname{dist}(z,S)\le\kappa\|z-Tz\|\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(z^k,S)\le q^k\operatorname{dist}(z^0,S)\) for some \(q<1\).

notation.meaning: fixed-point set corresponding to ADMM solutions

children.title: Curvature-Based ADMM Rate Regimes
children.top_down_role: Rate improvements associated with smoothness and curvature in selected blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Based ADMM Rate Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator-curvature condition yielding a contractive Douglas--Rachford map and hence linear ADMM convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the Douglas--Rachford operator \(T=(I+R_{\gamma B}R_{\gamma A})/2\), where \(R_{\gamma A}=2(I+\gamma A)^{-1}-I\). A sufficient curvature regime is: \(A\) is maximally monotone, \(\mu\)-strongly monotone, and single-valued \(L\)-Lipschitz, while \(B\) is maximally monotone. Then \(R_{\gamma B}\) is nonexpansive and
\[\|R_{\gamma A}u-R_{\gamma A}v\|\le\delta\|u-v\|,\qquad \delta=\sqrt{\frac{1-2\gamma\mu+\gamma^2L^2}{1+2\gamma\mu+\gamma^2L^2}}<1.\]
Consequently, \(T\) is Lipschitz with factor at most \((1+\delta)/2<1\), giving a geometric rate for the corresponding ADMM state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong monotonicity plus Lipschitz curvature in one operator makes its reflected resolvent contractive; composing with the other nonexpansive reflection yields a linear ADMM regime.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is maximally monotone, \(\mu\)-strongly monotone, and \(L\)-Lipschitz with \(\mu>0\).
\(B\) is maximally monotone and \(\gamma>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Lip}(T)\le(1+\delta)/2<1\), so \(\|z^k-z^\star\|\le((1+\delta)/2)^k\|z^0-z^\star\|\).

notation.meaning: reflected resolvent of the curved operator

children.title: Local ADMM Rate Regimes
children.top_down_role: Asymptotic rates near regular solutions or identified active structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Local ADMM Rate Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic linear rate after entry into a regular neighborhood of an ADMM solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the ADMM state be represented by \(z^{k+1}=Tz^k\), with \(z^k\to z^\star\in\operatorname{Fix}T\). Suppose there are a neighborhood \(U\) of \(z^\star\), a solution manifold \(M\), and \(q<1\) such that the iterates identify \(M\) after some \(k_0\) and
\[\operatorname{dist}(Tz,\operatorname{Fix}T\cap M)\le q\operatorname{dist}(z,\operatorname{Fix}T\cap M)\qquad(z\in U\cap M).\]
Then, once \(z^k\in U\cap M\),
\[\operatorname{dist}(z^k,\operatorname{Fix}T\cap M)\le q^{k-k_0}\operatorname{dist}(z^{k_0},\operatorname{Fix}T\cap M).\]
Locally Lipschitz primal-dual reconstructions inherit the same \(R\)-linear rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After a regular active structure is identified, contraction of the restricted ADMM map gives an asymptotic geometric rate, inherited by locally Lipschitz primal-dual variables.
assumptions_latex: \(z^k\to z^\star\in\operatorname{Fix}T\).
A manifold \(M\) is finitely identified and the restricted map contracts distance by \(q<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The fixed-point distance, and any locally Lipschitz reconstruction, converges locally \(R\)-linearly with factor at most \(q\).

notation.meaning: identified active or smooth solution manifold
regular neighborhood of the limiting solution

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of a certified ADMM convergence rate into an outer-iteration count.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m_k\ge0\) be a certified ADMM gap, residual, or solution-distance measure, let \(\varepsilon>0\), and define
\[N_{\mathrm{out}}(\varepsilon)=\min\{k\ge0:m_k\le\varepsilon\}.\]
If \(m_k\le C(k+1)^{-p}\) for constants \(C>0\) and \(p>0\), then
\[N_{\mathrm{out}}(\varepsilon)\le\left\lceil(C/\varepsilon)^{1/p}\right\rceil-1.\]
If instead \(m_k\le Cq^k\) with \(0<q<1\), then
\[N_{\mathrm{out}}(\varepsilon)\le\max\left\{0,\left\lceil\frac{\log(C/\varepsilon)}{-\log q}\right\rceil\right\}.\]
These counts exclude the internal cost of performing an outer update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial rate gives a power-law outer-iteration count. A geometric rate gives a nonnegative logarithmic count, equal to zero when the initial bound already meets the tolerance. Inner solution, oracle, and communication costs are excluded.

children.title: Oracle Complexity

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counting model for primitive smooth-function and linear-operator evaluations used by ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix primitive oracles \(\mathcal O_1,\ldots,\mathcal O_s\), such as value-gradient evaluations and products by \(A\) or \(A^*\). If outer iteration \(k\) invokes \(n_{k,j}\) calls to \(\mathcal O_j\), define the oracle-count vector through termination by
\[N_{\mathrm{orc}}(\varepsilon)=\left(\sum_{k=0}^{N_{\mathrm{out}}(\varepsilon)-1}n_{k,1},\ldots,\sum_{k=0}^{N_{\mathrm{out}}(\varepsilon)-1}n_{k,s}\right).\]
When \(n_{k,j}\le c_j\) uniformly, the \(j\)-th count is at most \(c_jN_{\mathrm{out}}(\varepsilon)\). Arithmetic performed inside an oracle and proximal evaluations are excluded unless explicitly declared primitive oracles.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle complexity counts each declared gradient or operator-product primitive separately. Uniformly bounded calls per ADMM iteration scale with the outer-iteration count.
assumptions_latex: The primitive oracle family and stopping measure are fixed before counting.
\(n_{k,j}\) counts only calls made during outer iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{orc},j}(\varepsilon)\le c_jN_{\mathrm{out}}(\varepsilon)\) whenever \(n_{k,j}\le c_j\).

notation.meaning: calls to oracle j during outer iteration k

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each block \(j\), let \(h_j:\mathcal H_j\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space \(\mathcal H_j\), and let \(\gamma>0\). Count one evaluation whenever an outer update requests
\[\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma h_j}(v)=\mathop{\arg\min}_{u\in\mathcal H_j}\left\{h_j(u)+\frac{1}{2\gamma}\|u-v\|^2\right\},\qquad v\in\mathcal H_j.\]
If iteration \(k\) makes \(p_{k,j}\) such requests, define
\[N_{\mathrm{prox},j}(\varepsilon)=\sum_{k=0}^{N_{\mathrm{out}}(\varepsilon)-1}p_{k,j}.\]
Hence \(p_{k,j}\le b_j\) for every counted iteration implies
\[N_{\mathrm{prox},j}(\varepsilon)\le b_jN_{\mathrm{out}}(\varepsilon).\]
If a proximal subproblem is solved iteratively, this count records the request; its internal oracle and linear-algebra costs must be reported separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For proper lower-semicontinuous convex block functions, proximal complexity counts blockwise proximal requests. A uniformly bounded number of requests per ADMM iteration scales with the outer-iteration count; iterative work inside a request is accounted for separately.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Evaluation Accounting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted scalarization and vector reporting of heterogeneous ADMM primitive evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(N(\varepsilon)=(N_1(\varepsilon),\ldots,N_s(\varepsilon))\in\mathbb N^s\) collect separately the gradient, linear-map, adjoint-map, proximal, projection, and other declared evaluation counts required to reach tolerance \(\varepsilon\). The lossless mixed accounting is the vector \(N(\varepsilon)\). Given nonnegative platform-dependent costs \(w_j\), its scalarized evaluation cost is
\[C_w(\varepsilon)=\sum_{j=1}^s w_jN_j(\varepsilon).\]
If each outer iteration uses at most \(c_j\) evaluations of type \(j\), then
\[C_w(\varepsilon)\le N_{\mathrm{out}}(\varepsilon)\sum_{j=1}^s w_jc_j.\]
Comparisons using \(C_w\) require the same primitive partition and weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Heterogeneous evaluations should be reported as a count vector, or scalarized using declared platform costs. Comparable scalar totals require identical primitives and weights.
assumptions_latex: Evaluation types form a fixed, nonoverlapping accounting convention.
Scalar weights satisfy \(w_j\ge0\) and are declared before comparison.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_w(\varepsilon)=\langle w,N(\varepsilon)\rangle\le N_{\mathrm{out}}(\varepsilon)\langle w,c\rangle\).

children.title: Inner-Solve Complexity
children.top_down_role: Computational cost attributable to nested optimization subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Inner-Solve Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cumulative iterations required by inexact solvers for ADMM block subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose outer iteration \(k\) solves block subproblems to tolerances \(\eta_{k,j}>0\), using \(I_j(\eta_{k,j};\theta_{k,j})\) inner iterations under instance parameters \(\theta_{k,j}\). The total inner-solve complexity through ADMM tolerance \(\varepsilon\) is
\[N_{\mathrm{inner}}(\varepsilon)=\sum_{k=0}^{N_{\mathrm{out}}(\varepsilon)-1}\sum_{j=1}^m I_j(\eta_{k,j};\theta_{k,j}).\]
If \(I_j(\eta;\theta)\le a_j(\theta)\log(b_j/\eta)\), then
\[N_{\mathrm{inner}}(\varepsilon)\le\sum_{k,j}a_j(\theta_{k,j})\log(b_j/\eta_{k,j}).\]
The tolerance schedule must also satisfy the inexact-ADMM convergence conditions used to justify \(N_{\mathrm{out}}(\varepsilon)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inner-solve complexity sums all iterative subproblem steps before termination. Its bound depends on solver conditioning and the tolerance schedule, which must preserve outer convergence.
assumptions_latex: Each inner solver has a declared tolerance criterion and bound \(I_j\).
The tolerance schedule is compatible with the invoked inexact-ADMM convergence result.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{inner}}(\varepsilon)=\sum_{k<N_{\mathrm{out}}(\varepsilon)}\sum_j I_j(\eta_{k,j};\theta_{k,j})\).

children.title: Linear-Algebra Complexity
