knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Algebra Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic accounting for factorizations and linear solves occurring in ADMM block updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose an ADMM run to tolerance \(\varepsilon\) performs \(F(\varepsilon)\) matrix factorizations with costs \(C_{\mathrm{fac},r}\), \(S(\varepsilon)\) triangular or direct solves with costs \(C_{\mathrm{sol},r}\), and iterative matrix-vector work totaling \(C_{\mathrm{it}}(\varepsilon)\). Its linear-algebra complexity is
\[C_{\mathrm{LA}}(\varepsilon)=\sum_{r=1}^{F(\varepsilon)}C_{\mathrm{fac},r}+\sum_{r=1}^{S(\varepsilon)}C_{\mathrm{sol},r}+C_{\mathrm{it}}(\varepsilon).\]
For a dense \(n\times n\) system with one reusable factorization and one solve per outer iteration,
\[C_{\mathrm{LA}}(\varepsilon)=O(n^3+n^2N_{\mathrm{out}}(\varepsilon)).\]
Sparse or structured systems require replacing these terms by structure-dependent costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear-algebra cost separates factorization, repeated solves, and iterative matrix-vector work. A reusable dense factorization costs cubic preprocessing plus quadratic work per ADMM iteration.
assumptions_latex: The arithmetic model counts scalar operations and declares matrix structure.
The dense example uses one \(n\)-dimensional factorization and one associated solve per outer iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_{\mathrm{LA}}(\varepsilon)=O(n^3+n^2N_{\mathrm{out}}(\varepsilon))\) in the stated dense reuse regime.

notation.meaning: numbers of factorizations and associated solves

children.title: Factorization-Reuse Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cost regimes distinguished by reusable versus changing linear-system structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Factorization-Reuse Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Amortized cost reduction when ADMM linear systems retain a fixed coefficient matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose every ADMM block solve has coefficient matrix \(H\) independent of the outer index, while only its right-hand side changes. If factorizing \(H\) costs \(C_{\mathrm{fac}}\) and applying the factors costs \(C_{\mathrm{sol}}\), then \(K\) outer solves cost
\[C_{\mathrm{reuse}}(K)=C_{\mathrm{fac}}+K C_{\mathrm{sol}},\qquad \frac{C_{\mathrm{reuse}}(K)}{K}=C_{\mathrm{sol}}+\frac{C_{\mathrm{fac}}}{K}.\]
Without reuse, refactorization costs \(K(C_{\mathrm{fac}}+C_{\mathrm{sol}})\). Reuse is invalidated when penalty adaptation, changing metrics, or changing active linear structure alters \(H\), unless an update or refactorization cost is separately included.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed ADMM coefficient matrix permits one factorization followed by cheap repeated solves. Changing penalties, metrics, or linear structure can remove this amortization.
assumptions_latex: The coefficient matrix \(H\) and its ordering remain fixed across the counted solves.
Stored factors remain applicable and memory costs are accounted separately if relevant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The amortized cost per solve is \(C_{\mathrm{sol}}+C_{\mathrm{fac}}/K\), rather than \(C_{\mathrm{fac}}+C_{\mathrm{sol}}\).

notation.meaning: cost of one solve using stored factors

children.title: Parallel Work Complexity
children.top_down_role: Work, span, processor utilization, and load distribution in parallel realizations.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Work Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Total local computation and critical-path time for parallel block ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(P\) workers, let \(w_{k,p}\) be worker \(p\)'s local operations during outer iteration \(k\), and let \(s_k\) be serial coordination work. Through \(K=N_{\mathrm{out}}(\varepsilon)\) iterations, define total work and ideal synchronized span by
\[W_P(\varepsilon)=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\left(s_k+\sum_{p=1}^P w_{k,p}\right),\qquad T_P^{\mathrm{ideal}}(\varepsilon)=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\left(s_k+\max_{1\le p\le P}w_{k,p}\right).\]
Thus \(T_P^{\mathrm{ideal}}\le W_P\), while load imbalance is exposed by the maxima. Communication latency, bandwidth, and waiting must be added to obtain realized parallel time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel work sums all worker operations; ideal elapsed computation follows the largest worker load per synchronized iteration. Real time additionally includes communication and waiting.
assumptions_latex: Workers execute local block work concurrently within each outer iteration.
The ideal span excludes communication, latency, and synchronization waiting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_P^{\mathrm{ideal}}(\varepsilon)\le W_P(\varepsilon)\), with per-iteration span governed by \(\max_p w_{k,p}\).

notation.meaning: local work of worker p in outer iteration k
total parallel work across all workers

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a distributed ADMM implementation and a tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\). Suppose iteration \(k\) uses \(m_k\geq0\) messages containing altogether \(b_k\geq0\) transmitted scalars. Let \(K_\varepsilon\) be the first iteration whose prescribed residual satisfies \(R_k\leq\varepsilon\), and suppose this iteration exists. Define \[M_\varepsilon=\sum_{k=1}^{K_\varepsilon}m_k,\qquad B_\varepsilon=\sum_{k=1}^{K_\varepsilon}b_k.\] If \(K_\varepsilon\leq\lceil C\varepsilon^{-p}\rceil\) for constants \(C,p>0\), and \(m_k\leq\bar m\), \(b_k\leq\bar b\) for every \(k\in\{1,\ldots,K_\varepsilon\}\), then \[M_\varepsilon\leq\bar m\lceil C\varepsilon^{-p}\rceil,\qquad B_\varepsilon\leq\bar b\lceil C\varepsilon^{-p}\rceil.\] Thus an iteration rate becomes a communication bound only after the communication performed per iteration is specified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive tolerance attained in finitely many iterations, message and scalar communication bounds follow by multiplying the iteration bound by valid nonnegative per-iteration communication limits.

children.title: Synchronization Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Cost regimes shaped by barriers, coordination frequency, and worker imbalance.

assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon>0\), \(q\in\mathbb N\), and \(q\geq1\).
\(\tau_{\mathrm{loc}},\tau_{\mathrm{sync}}\geq0\).
Local-update and synchronization costs are additive, constant per event, and do not overlap.
\(K_\varepsilon(q)\in\mathbb N\) is finite for each admissible \(q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_\varepsilon(q)=K_\varepsilon(q)(q\tau_{\mathrm{loc}}+\tau_{\mathrm{sync}})\), and any cost-model-optimal \(q\) belongs to the stated argmin set.

notation.meaning: synchronization rounds needed at interval q

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost model for choosing local work between global ADMM synchronizations.

source_refs.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\). Suppose a parallel splitting method performs \(q\in\mathbb N\), \(q\geq1\), local block updates between successive global synchronizations and requires a finite number \(K_\varepsilon(q)\in\mathbb N\) of synchronization rounds to reach tolerance \(\varepsilon\). If one local update costs \(\tau_{\mathrm{loc}}\geq0\), one synchronization costs \(\tau_{\mathrm{sync}}\geq0\), and these costs are additive and do not overlap, then its modeled wall-clock cost is \[T_\varepsilon(q)=K_\varepsilon(q)\bigl(q\tau_{\mathrm{loc}}+\tau_{\mathrm{sync}}\bigr).\] Its synchronization complexity is \(K_\varepsilon(q)\), while its local-work complexity is \(qK_\varepsilon(q)\). Hence, provided \(K_\varepsilon(q)\) is known or bounded, every cost-model-optimal synchronization interval belongs to \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{q\in\mathbb N,\ q\geq1}K_\varepsilon(q)\bigl(q\tau_{\mathrm{loc}}+\tau_{\mathrm{sync}}\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated additive nonoverlapping cost model, the synchronization interval should minimize the number of required rounds times the local-work-plus-synchronization cost of each round.
knowledge_statements.title: Synchronization Tradeoffs

children.title: Primal Feasibility Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual measures for linear coupling and consensus feasibility.

assumptions_latex: \(X,Z,Y\) are finite-dimensional normed spaces.
\(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Z\to(-\infty,+\infty]\).
\(A:X\to Y\) and \(B:Z\to Y\) are linear, and \(c\in Y\).
\(x^k\in X\), \(z^k\in Z\), and \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm p}\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm p}^k=0\iff Ax^k+Bz^k=c\).

notation.meaning: norm of the primal feasibility residual

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residuals for two-block linear coupling, including consensus as a specialization.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X,Z,Y\) be finite-dimensional normed spaces, let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Z\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), let \(A:X\to Y\) and \(B:Z\to Y\) be linear, and let \(c\in Y\). For the constrained problem \[\min_{x\in X,\ z\in Z} f(x)+g(z)\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax+Bz=c,\] the primal feasibility residual at \((x^k,z^k)\in X\times Z\) is \[r_{\mathrm p}^k=Ax^k+Bz^k-c,\qquad R_{\mathrm p}^k=\lVert r_{\mathrm p}^k\rVert.\] The iterate is exactly primal feasible if and only if \(R_{\mathrm p}^k=0\). For consensus coupling \(x=z\), obtained when \(X=Z=Y\), \(A=I\), \(B=-I\), and \(c=0\), this reduces to \(r_{\mathrm p}^k=x^k-z^k\). For a prescribed \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm p}\geq0\), a tolerance certificate declares approximate feasibility when \(R_{\mathrm p}^k\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm p}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a two-block linear constraint, the primal residual is the constraint violation and vanishes exactly at feasible iterates; consensus is the specialization with residual x minus z.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Feasibility Residuals

children.title: Dual Feasibility Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual evidence concerning consistency of the dual-side conditions.

assumptions_latex: \(X,Z,Y\) are finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
\(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Z\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper closed convex functions.
\(A:X\to Y\) and \(B:Z\to Y\) are linear, \(c\in Y\), and \(y\in Y\).
\(\operatorname{dom}f^*\) and \(\operatorname{dom}g^*\) are closed for the stated equivalence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm{df}}(y)=0\iff -A^*y\in\operatorname{dom}f^*\ \text{and}\ -B^*y\in\operatorname{dom}g^*\).

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugates of the block objectives

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distance-based feasibility of the dual arguments in Fenchel conjugate domains.

source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Minimization Algorithms II: Advanced Theory and Bundle Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X,Z,Y\) be finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:Z\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex functions, let \(A:X\to Y\) and \(B:Z\to Y\) be linear, and let \(y\in Y\) be a multiplier for \(Ax+Bz=c\), where \(c\in Y\). The multiplier induces conjugate arguments \(-A^*y\in X\) and \(-B^*y\in Z\). Define \[R_{\mathrm{df}}(y)=\left(\operatorname{dist}(-A^*y,\operatorname{dom}f^*)^2+\operatorname{dist}(-B^*y,\operatorname{dom}g^*)^2\right)^{1/2}.\] If both conjugate domains are closed, then \(y\) is feasible for the Fenchel dual if and only if \(R_{\mathrm{df}}(y)=0\). Without closedness, zero residual certifies membership only in the closures of those domains. This residual tests finiteness of the dual objective; it does not by itself certify primal-dual stationarity or optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, the dual feasibility residual measures the distances of the multiplier-induced conjugate arguments from the effective domains of the conjugates; closedness of those domains is required for zero distance to imply membership.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Feasibility Residuals

source_witnesses.source_title: Convex Analysis and Minimization Algorithms II: Advanced Theory and Bundle Methods

children.title: Block Stationarity Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual evidence concerning optimality consistency within individual blocks.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper closed convex functions.
The primal and dual spaces are finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
\(y\) is a multiplier for \(Ax+Bz=c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm{stat}}=0\iff 0\in\partial f(x)+A^*y\ \text{and}\ 0\in\partial g(z)+B^*y\).

notation.meaning: stationarity residual for the x block
stationarity residual for the z block

knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT stationarity violations measured separately for the two primal blocks.

source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Minimization Algorithms II: Advanced Theory and Bundle Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a primal-dual point \((x,z,y)\) of the problem with constraint \(Ax+Bz=c\), define the block stationarity residuals \[R_x(x,y)=\operatorname{dist}\bigl(0,\partial f(x)+A^*y\bigr),\qquad R_z(z,y)=\operatorname{dist}\bigl(0,\partial g(z)+B^*y\bigr).\] Their aggregate is \[R_{\mathrm{stat}}(x,z,y)=\bigl(R_x(x,y)^2+R_z(z,y)^2\bigr)^{1/2}.\] Exact block stationarity holds if and only if \(R_{\mathrm{stat}}(x,z,y)=0\). If either subdifferential is empty at the evaluated point, the corresponding distance is defined as \(+\infty\). These residuals measure stationarity and are logically distinct from the primal constraint residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each block residual is the distance from zero to its KKT stationarity inclusion; their Euclidean aggregate vanishes exactly when both inclusions hold.
knowledge_statements.title: Block Stationarity Residuals

source_witnesses.source_title: Convex Analysis and Minimization Algorithms II: Advanced Theory and Bundle Methods

children.title: Dual-Stationarity Consistency
children.top_down_role: Interpretive relationships between dual feasibility signals and block optimality signals.

assumptions_latex: \((x,z,y)\) belongs to the common domain of the three constituent residuals.
\(R_{\mathrm{df}}(y),R_x(x,y),R_z(z,y)\in[0,+\infty]\).
\(\varepsilon\geq0\).
The conjugate domains are closed when zero dual-domain distance is interpreted as membership.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm{ds}}(x,z,y)\leq\varepsilon\Rightarrow \max\{R_{\mathrm{df}}(y),R_x(x,y),R_z(z,y)\}\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency certificate joining dual-domain feasibility with blockwise KKT stationarity.

source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Minimization Algorithms II: Advanced Theory and Bundle Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x,z,y)\) belong to the common domain of the dual-domain residual \(R_{\mathrm{df}}(y)\) and the block stationarity residuals \(R_x(x,y)\) and \(R_z(z,y)\). Define \[R_{\mathrm{ds}}(x,z,y)=\left(R_{\mathrm{df}}(y)^2+R_x(x,y)^2+R_z(z,y)^2\right)^{1/2}.\] For every \(\varepsilon\geq0\), the inequality \(R_{\mathrm{ds}}(x,z,y)\leq\varepsilon\) certifies that every constituent residual is at most \(\varepsilon\). At \(\varepsilon=0\), and with closed conjugate domains, it certifies dual feasibility and both stationarity inclusions simultaneously. It does not certify primal feasibility unless the independent residual \(\lVert Ax+Bz-c\rVert\) also vanishes or meets its prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonnegative tolerance, the aggregate certificate controls dual-domain feasibility and both block stationarity residuals, while primal feasibility remains a separate requirement.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Stationarity Consistency

children.title: Fixed-Point Residuals
children.top_down_role: Defect measures tied to the fixed-point representation of an iteration.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space.
\(T:H\to H\) is single-valued.
For the step identity, \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_T(w)=0\iff w\in\operatorname{Fix}T\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual of a splitting iteration represented by a single-valued fixed-point map.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space and let \(T:H\to H\) be the single-valued fixed-point operator generating \(w^{k+1}=T(w^k)\). For \(w\in H\), define \[r_T(w)=w-T(w),\qquad R_T(w)=\lVert w-T(w)\rVert.\] It is an exact certificate for the fixed-point equation because \[R_T(w)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad w\in\operatorname{Fix}T.\] For a relaxed update \(w^+=w+\lambda(T(w)-w)\) with \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}\), the observable step satisfies \(\lVert w^+-w\rVert=|\lambda|R_T(w)\), so step norms and fixed-point residuals must be compared using the relaxation factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-point residual is the norm of the displacement under the iteration map and vanishes exactly at a fixed point; a nonzero real relaxation factor scales the observable step norm.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Point Residuals

children.title: Operator Residuals
children.top_down_role: Defect measures tied to inclusions, mappings, or split operators.

knowledge_statements.title: Operator Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual for a monotone inclusion evaluated through distance to the operator value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:H\rightrightarrows H\) be a set-valued operator on a Hilbert space. For \(u\in H\), define the inclusion or operator residual by \[R_F(u)=\operatorname{dist}(0,F(u))=\inf_{v\in F(u)}\lVert v\rVert,\] with \(R_F(u)=+\infty\) when \(F(u)=\varnothing\). If \(F(u)\) is closed, then \[R_F(u)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in F(u).\] For a primal-dual KKT operator, its components encode primal feasibility and block stationarity, so a product-space norm on the operator value provides one aggregate optimality residual. The chosen product norm remains part of the residual specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An operator residual is the smallest norm among values of the inclusion operator; with closed values it vanishes exactly at a zero.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a Hilbert space.
\(F:H\rightrightarrows H\) has closed values for the zero-residual equivalence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_F(u)=0\iff 0\in F(u)\).

notation.meaning: distance from zero to the operator value

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Correspondence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and one-sided correspondence for resolvent fixed-point and inclusion residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:H\rightrightarrows H\), let \(\gamma>0\), and suppose the resolvent \(T=J_{\gamma F}=(I+\gamma F)^{-1}\) is single-valued. For any \(w\in H\), set \(u=T(w)\). The resolvent identity gives \[\frac{w-u}{\gamma}\in F(u),\qquad R_F(u)\leq\frac{R_T(w)}{\gamma}.\] Conversely, for any \(u\in\operatorname{dom}F\) and \(v\in F(u)\), choosing \(w=u+\gamma v\) yields \(T(w)=u\) and \(R_T(w)=\gamma\lVert v\rVert\). Thus the two residuals correspond exactly along a selected graph element, but an arbitrary fixed-point residual generally supplies only an upper bound for the minimal operator residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resolvent displacement produces an inclusion value after division by the stepsize; exact equality holds when a particular graph element generates the resolvent input.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a Hilbert space and \(\gamma>0\).
\(T=(I+\gamma F)^{-1}\) is single-valued.
\(R_F(u)=\operatorname{dist}(0,F(u))\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u=T(w)\Rightarrow R_F(u)\leq R_T(w)/\gamma\), with equality along a minimum-norm selected graph element when attained.

children.title: Scaled Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual representations adjusted using variable, constraint, or operator scales.

assumptions_latex: \(r\in\mathbb R^m\).
\(D\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is invertible.
The residual magnitude uses the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_D(r)=0\iff r=0\), with the stated singular-value comparison bounds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residuals expressed in a prescribed weighted metric or physical scaling.

source_refs.locator: 1.2 Limitations of monotone operator theory p. 2

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r\in\mathbb R^m\) be a residual vector and let \(D\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) be invertible. Define the scaled residual vector and its magnitude by \[r_D=Dr,\qquad R_D(r)=\lVert Dr\rVert_2.\] Then \(R_D(r)=0\) if and only if \(r=0\). Moreover, \[\sigma_{\min}(D)\lVert r\rVert_2\leq R_D(r)\leq\sigma_{\max}(D)\lVert r\rVert_2.\] Thus scaling preserves the exact zero set but changes nonzero magnitudes and tolerances according to the conditioning of \(D\). A stopping threshold for \(R_D\) is meaningful only when the scaling operator is recorded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible linear scaling preserves the residual zero set but changes nonzero Euclidean magnitudes within bounds determined by its extreme singular values.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Residuals

children.title: Normalized Residuals
children.top_down_role: Dimensionless or reference-relative residual representations.

assumptions_latex: \(U\) is nonempty and \(u\in U\).
\(R,S:U\to[0,+\infty)\).
\(R(u)\) and \(S(u)\) have identical physical units.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat R(u)=R(u)/\max\{S(u),\delta\}\), and simultaneous multiplication of \(R(u)\), \(S(u)\), and \(\delta\) by any \(\alpha>0\) leaves \(\widehat R(u)\) unchanged.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimensionless residual ratio relative to an explicitly chosen positive reference scale.

source_refs.locator: 1.2 Limitations of monotone operator theory p. 2
source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be a nonempty set, let \(R,S:U\to[0,+\infty)\), and fix \(u\in U\). Suppose \(R(u)\) is a residual magnitude, \(S(u)\) is a reference scale with the same physical units, and \(\delta>0\) is a safeguard with those units. Define \[\widehat R(u)=\frac{R(u)}{\max\{S(u),\delta\}}.\] Then \(\widehat R(u)=0\) if and only if \(R(u)=0\). If \(R(u)\), \(S(u)\), and \(\delta\) are all multiplied by a common factor \(\alpha>0\), the normalized value is unchanged. Consequently, normalization is scale-invariant only relative to a specified transformation rule for every denominator term.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized residual divides a nonnegative residual magnitude by a positive safeguarded reference of matching units; it is invariant only when the numerator, reference, and safeguard scale together.
knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Residuals

children.title: Cross-Scale Interpretation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on comparing transformed residual values across models or solver configurations.

assumptions_latex: \(r\in\mathbb R^m\setminus\{0\}\).
\(D_1,D_2\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) are invertible.
Both reported residuals use the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Cross-scale comparison requires bounds on \(D_2D_1^{-1}\); without such scaling information, the residual ratio can be multiplied by an arbitrary positive factor while the zero set remains unchanged.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits on comparing residual magnitudes across differently scaled formulations or implementations.

source_refs.locator: 1.2 Limitations of monotone operator theory p. 2
source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r\in\mathbb R^m\setminus\{0\}\), and let two equivalent formulations report \(R_1(r)=\lVert D_1r\rVert_2\) and \(R_2(r)=\lVert D_2r\rVert_2\), where \(D_1,D_2\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) are invertible. Their ratio is not intrinsically fixed: replacing \(D_2\) by \(\alpha D_2\), for any \(\alpha>0\), multiplies \(R_2(r)/R_1(r)\) by \(\alpha\) without changing the exact zero set. Therefore raw residual magnitudes or absolute tolerances cannot be compared across scales unless the scaling maps are known. If \(D_2D_1^{-1}\) is known, then \[\sigma_{\min}(D_2D_1^{-1})R_1(r)\leq R_2(r)\leq\sigma_{\max}(D_2D_1^{-1})R_1(r),\] which supplies a valid comparison boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonzero residual vector, raw magnitudes under different invertible scalings are not intrinsically comparable; a known relative scaling supplies the stated singular-value conversion bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Scale Interpretation Boundaries

children.title: Scale-Aware Tolerance Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Scale-aware residual-based termination families.

children.title: Absolute Tolerance Certificates
children.top_down_role: Termination evidence based on fixed-scale residual thresholds.

knowledge_statements.title: Absolute Tolerance Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute stopping certificate for a finite collection of solver residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r_1,\ldots,r_m\) be residual vectors in finite-dimensional normed spaces, and let \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}>0\). An iterate has an absolute-tolerance certificate when
\[
\max_{1\le i\le m}\|r_i\|_i\le \varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}.
\]
The certificate is directly verifiable from the reported residuals and chosen norms. It is invariant under neither rescaling of the model data nor changes of physical units; consequently, \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\) must be interpreted in the units and normalization of the corresponding residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every monitored residual is at most one fixed positive threshold, measured in its prescribed norm; the threshold depends on the model's units and scaling.
assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb{N}\) and every residual norm is computable.
\(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_i\|r_i\|_i\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\) certifies absolute residual accuracy.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

children.title: Relative Tolerance Certificates
children.top_down_role: Termination evidence calibrated to problem data or iterate magnitudes.

assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb{N}\).
For every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), \(r_i\in E_i\), \(\|\cdot\|_i\) is a norm on \(E_i\), and \(s_i\ge 0\) is computable.
\(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|r_i\|_i\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}s_i\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) certifies relative residual accuracy.

notation.meaning: The ith monitored residual vector and its prescribed norm.
Computable reference magnitude for the ith residual.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-normalized stopping certificate with an explicit treatment of zero reference magnitudes.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m\in\mathbb{N}\). For every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), let \(r_i\) belong to a normed space \((E_i,\|\cdot\|_i)\), and let \(s_i\ge0\) be a computable reference scale. Fix \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}>0\). A relative-tolerance certificate is valid when
\[
\|r_i\|_i\le \varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}s_i\quad\text{for every }i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}.
\]
When every \(s_i>0\), this is equivalent to
\[
\max_{1\le i\le m}\frac{\|r_i\|_i}{s_i}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}.
\]
If some \(s_i=0\), the corresponding purely relative condition requires \(r_i=0\), so a numerically robust stopping policy ordinarily supplements it with an absolute tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each of finitely many residuals is bounded by a fixed fraction of its computable reference scale. A zero reference scale requires the corresponding residual to vanish exactly and exposes the limitation of a purely relative rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative Tolerance Certificates

source_witnesses.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

children.title: Mixed-Tolerance Certificate Regimes
children.top_down_role: Scale regimes governing the joint interpretation of absolute and relative criteria.

assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb{N}\), and \(d_i\in\mathbb{N}\) for every \(i\in\{1,ldots,m\}\).
For every \(i\), \(r_i\in\mathbb{R}^{d_i}\) and \(s_i\ge0\) is declared and computable.
\(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequalities \(\|r_i\|_2\le\sqrt{d_i}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}s_i\) for all \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) jointly certify the prescribed mixed absolute-relative accuracy.

notation.meaning: Dimension of the ith Euclidean residual vector.
Reference magnitude for relative error in the ith residual.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combined absolute-relative certificate avoiding degeneracy at small scales.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m\in\mathbb{N}\). For every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), let \(r_i\in\mathbb{R}^{d_i}\), where \(d_i\in\mathbb{N}\), and choose a computable reference scale \(s_i\ge0\). Fix \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}>0\). The mixed certificate accepts an iterate precisely when
\[
\|r_i\|_2\le \sqrt{d_i}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}s_i
\quad\text{for every }i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}.
\]
The absolute term supplies a nonzero tolerance when \(s_i\) is small, while the relative term scales with large reference magnitudes. The residual dimensions and reference scales must be declared before certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each Euclidean residual is bounded by a dimension-scaled absolute allowance plus a scale-proportional relative allowance, avoiding zero-scale degeneracy while retaining scale awareness.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Tolerance Certificate Regimes

children.title: Primal-Dual Gap Certificates
children.top_down_role: Gap-based termination for models with accessible primal and dual objectives.

assumptions_latex: \(x\in X\) is primal feasible and \(y\in Y\) is dual feasible.
The finite values \(p^\star=\inf_{u\in X}P(u)\) and \(d^\star=\sup_{v\in Y}D(v)\) satisfy weak duality.
\(0\le P(x)-D(y)\le\varepsilon\) for some \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le P(x)-p^\star\le\varepsilon\) and \(0\le d^\star-D(y)\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Finite primal infimum and dual supremum.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-duality certificate for feasible primal and dual objective values.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be the primal and dual feasible sets, let \(P:X\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(D:Y\to\mathbb{R}\) be their objective functions, and define finite optimal values
\[
p^\star=\inf_{u\in X}P(u),
\qquad
d^\star=\sup_{v\in Y}D(v).
\]
Assume weak duality, so \(D(v)\le d^\star\le p^\star\le P(u)\) for all \(u\in X\) and \(v\in Y\). If \(x\in X\), \(y\in Y\), and
\[
0\le P(x)-D(y)\le\varepsilon
\]
for some \(\varepsilon\ge0\), then
\[
0\le P(x)-p^\star\le\varepsilon,
\qquad
0\le d^\star-D(y)\le\varepsilon.
\]
Thus the computable gap certifies simultaneous absolute suboptimality of both feasible points. Without verified feasibility, the numerical objective difference alone is not a valid primal-dual gap certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finite primal and dual optimal values satisfying weak duality, a feasible primal-dual pair with objective gap at most epsilon certifies that each objective is within epsilon of its corresponding optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Gap Certificates

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) and \(g:\mathbb{R}^q\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) are proper, closed, and convex.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) and \(g:\mathbb{R}^q\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, convex functions, let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times q}\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and consider
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n,\,z\in\mathbb{R}^q} f(x)+g(z)
\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax+Bz=c.
\]
For \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), \(z\in\operatorname{dom}g\), and \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\), define
\[
r_{\mathrm p}=Ax+Bz-c,
\quad r_x=\operatorname{dist}\bigl(0,\partial f(x)+A^{\mathsf T}y\bigr),
\quad r_z=\operatorname{dist}\bigl(0,\partial g(z)+B^{\mathsf T}y\bigr).
\]
The tuple \((x,z,y)\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-KKT residual certificate, for \(\varepsilon\ge0\), when
\[
\max\{\|r_{\mathrm p}\|_2,r_x,r_z\}\le\varepsilon.
\]
At \(\varepsilon=0\), these conditions are exactly primal feasibility and Lagrangian stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite-dimensional two-block convex equality-constrained problem, the certificate jointly bounds Euclidean equality infeasibility and both block-stationarity distances; a zero bound recovers the exact KKT conditions.
knowledge_statements.title: KKT Residual Certificates

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a closed convex cone, define
\[
K^*=\{u\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle u,x\rangle\ge0\ \text{for every }x\in K\},
\]
and consider the constraints \(Ax=b\), \(x\in K\), where \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\). A vector \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) is a primal-infeasibility certificate when
\[
A^{\mathsf T}y\in K^*,
\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y<0.
\]
These directly checkable conditions certify that the primal constraint system has no feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For conic equality constraints, a separating multiplier whose adjoint image lies in the dual cone and whose pairing with the right-hand side is negative certifies primal infeasibility.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a convex cone.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[
\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\in K\},
\]
where \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a convex cone, \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\). A pair \((x_0,d)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^n\) is an unboundedness certificate when
\[
Ax_0=b,
\quad x_0\in K,
\quad Ad=0,
\quad d\in K,
\quad c^{\mathsf T}d<0.
\]
The certificate identifies the feasible ray \(\{x_0+td:t\ge0\}\), along which the objective is unbounded below. Requiring the feasible base point \(x_0\) distinguishes primal unboundedness from a certificate establishing only dual infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point together with a feasible conic recession direction having negative objective slope certifies that the primal objective is unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.title: Unboundedness Certificates

children.title: Ambiguous Divergence Evidence
children.top_down_role: Divergent behavior that does not uniquely distinguish infeasibility from unboundedness.

knowledge_statements.title: Ambiguous Divergence Evidence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Divergent iterates alone do not classify infeasibility or unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the feasible convex problem
\[
\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}} e^x.
\]
The sequence \(x_k=-k\) diverges in norm and satisfies \(e^{x_k}\to0\). Nevertheless, the problem is feasible and bounded below, with finite infimum \(0\); it merely has no minimizer. Therefore divergence of iterates, vanishing objective changes, or growth of an internal multiplier is not by itself a certificate of primal infeasibility, dual infeasibility, or objective unboundedness. Classification requires a separately verifiable separating vector, recession ray, or other model-specific certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A divergent minimizing sequence can occur in a feasible problem with finite infimum, so raw divergence cannot certify infeasibility or unboundedness.
assumptions_latex: The domain is \(\mathbb{R}\) and the objective is \(x\mapsto e^x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\to-\infty\) while \(\inf_x e^x=0\), so divergence alone is diagnostically ambiguous.

notation.meaning: Divergent minimizing sequence defined by x_k=-k.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Penalty Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical two-block ADMM with a constant augmented-Lagrangian penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min_{x,z} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), choose \(\rho>0\) once and initialize \((z^0,y^0)\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), compute
\[
x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_x f(x)+\langle y^k,Ax+Bz^k-c\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax+Bz^k-c\|^2,
\]
\[
z^{k+1}\in\arg\min_z g(z)+\langle y^k,Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c\|^2,
\]
\[
y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c).
\]
Stop only when the declared certificate policy passes; output the latest primal-dual tuple. The penalty \(\rho\) is not changed between iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classical ADMM alternates exact block minimizations and a multiplier update while keeping one positive penalty fixed until a stopping certificate passes.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
Each displayed block minimization attains a solution.
\(\rho>0\) is fixed before iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generated sequence uses the same augmented-Lagrangian penalty \(\rho\) at every iteration.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) and \(g:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, convex functions, let \(K\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), and consider
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n} f(x)+g(Kx).
\]
Choose fixed \(\tau,\sigma>0\) satisfying \(\tau\sigma\|K\|_2^2<1\), initialize \((x^0,y^0)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m\), and set \(\bar x^0=x^0\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), compute
\[
y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma g^*}(y^k+\sigma K\bar x^k),
\quad
x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau f}(x^k-\tau K^{\mathsf T}y^{k+1}),
\]
\[
\bar x^{k+1}=2x^{k+1}-x^k.
\]
Stop when the prescribed primal-dual certificate passes and output \((x^{k+1},y^{k+1})\). Neither stepsize changes during the run.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite-dimensional convex composite problem, PDHG uses fixed positive primal and dual steps satisfying the operator-norm product bound and terminates through the declared certificate rule.

children.title: Joint Parameter Compatibility

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Parameter Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupled metric condition for fixed-step primal-dual splitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T\succ0\) and \(\Sigma\succ0\) be self-adjoint primal and dual stepsize operators for a primal-dual splitting method with bounded linear coupling \(K\). The fixed parameters are jointly compatible when
\[
\|\Sigma^{1/2}KT^{1/2}\|<1.
\]
Equivalently, in finite dimensions,
\[
T^{-1}-K^{\mathsf T}\Sigma K\succ0.
\]
For scalar choices \(T=\tau I\) and \(\Sigma=\sigma I\), this reduces to \(\tau\sigma\|K\|^2<1\). Positivity of \(T\) and \(\Sigma\) separately is insufficient: compatibility depends on their product through the coupling operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal and dual step metrics are compatible exactly when their coupling through the linear operator has norm below one; separate positivity does not suffice.
assumptions_latex: \(T\succ0\) and \(\Sigma\succ0\) are self-adjoint.
\(K\) is a bounded linear operator.
The strict positive-definite form is interpreted in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\Sigma^{1/2}KT^{1/2}\|<1\), equivalently \(T^{-1}-K^{\mathsf T}\Sigma K\succ0\).

children.title: Residual-Balancing Policies

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Balancing Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical multiplicative ADMM penalty adaptation using normalized primal and dual residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For ADMM applied to minimize \(f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), define \(r^{k+1}=Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c\) and \(s^{k+1}=\rho_k A^{\mathsf T}B(z^{k+1}-z^k)\). Given \(\mu>1\), \(\tau_\uparrow>1\), \(\tau_\downarrow>1\), and bounds \(0<\rho_{\min}\leq\rho_{\max}\), set
\[
\rho_{k+1}=\begin{cases}
\min\{\tau_\uparrow\rho_k,\rho_{\max}\},&\|r^{k+1}\|>\mu\|s^{k+1}\|,\\
\max\{\rho_k/\tau_\downarrow,\rho_{\min}\},&\|s^{k+1}\|>\mu\|r^{k+1}\|,\\
\rho_k,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
If the scaled multiplier \(u^k=y^k/\rho_k\) is stored, replace it after changing the penalty by \(u^{k+1}\leftarrow(\rho_k/\rho_{k+1})u^{k+1}\), thereby preserving the unscaled multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increase the ADMM penalty when primal residual dominates, decrease it when dual residual dominates, and rescale the stored scaled multiplier after any change.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper closed convex functions and the displayed ADMM iterates are well defined.
Residual norms use compatible, preferably normalized, primal and dual scales.
\(0<\rho_{\min}\leq\rho_0\leq\rho_{\max}<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{k+1}\in[\rho_{\min},\rho_{\max}]\), with multiplicative changes directed toward reducing residual imbalance.

children.title: Spectral Penalty Policies
children.top_down_role: Curvature-inspired penalty estimates based on local secant information.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Penalty Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safeguarded secant estimate for an ADMM penalty or primal-dual metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p^k\) and \(q^k\) be paired residual and multiplier-like quantities in the same Euclidean space. At an update index define \(\Delta p_k=p^k-p^{k-1}\), \(\Delta q_k=q^k-q^{k-1}\), and \(c_k=\langle\Delta p_k,\Delta q_k\rangle\). Given \(0<\rho_{\min}\leq\rho_{\max}\) and \(\varepsilon>0\), accept a spectral update only if \(c_k\geq\varepsilon\|\Delta p_k\|\|\Delta q_k\|\). On acceptance set
\[
\widehat\rho_{k+1}=\sqrt{\frac{c_k}{\|\Delta p_k\|^2}\frac{\|\Delta q_k\|^2}{c_k}}=\frac{\|\Delta q_k\|}{\|\Delta p_k\|},\qquad
\rho_{k+1}=\min\{\rho_{\max},\max\{\rho_{\min},\widehat\rho_{k+1}\}\};
\]
otherwise retain \(\rho_{k+1}=\rho_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimate the penalty from a local secant ratio, accept it only under positive curvature correlation, and clip it to prescribed bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(p^k,q^k\) belong to a common finite-dimensional inner-product space.
The update is attempted only when \(\|\Delta p_k\|\|\Delta q_k\|>0\).
\(0<\rho_{\min}\leq\rho_k\leq\rho_{\max}<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted estimate satisfies \(\rho_{k+1}\in[\rho_{\min},\rho_{\max}]\) and uses positively correlated secant data.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the policy leaf, but the generic secant ratio is not tied to a specified ADMM update or established spectral-penalty construction. Spectral ADMM policies use convention-dependent primal and dual curvature estimates and safeguards, so an authoritative source with an exact locator is required.

children.title: Linesearch Acceptance Policies

knowledge_statements.title: Linesearch Acceptance Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract sufficient-decrease acceptance test for a trial primal-dual parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(w^k\) be the current primal-dual state, let \(w^+(\eta)\) be the trial state generated with parameter \(\eta>0\), and let \(\Phi\colon\mathcal W\to[0,\infty)\) be a computable merit function. For \(\sigma\in(0,1)\) and a nonnegative predicted-decrease quantity \(D_k(\eta)\), the trial parameter is accepted exactly when
\[
\Phi\bigl(w^+(\eta)\bigr)\leq \Phi(w^k)-\sigma D_k(\eta).
\]
The policy returns the first tested \(\eta\) satisfying this inequality; if no tested value is accepted, it reports search failure rather than silently using an uncertified trial.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept the first trial parameter whose new primal-dual merit achieves a prescribed fraction of the predicted decrease.
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi(w^k)\) and \(\Phi(w^+(\eta))\) are finite and computable.
\(D_k(\eta)\geq0\) is specified by the underlying splitting method.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An accepted trial satisfies the explicit sufficient-decrease certificate \(\Phi(w^+(\eta))\leq\Phi(w^k)-\sigma D_k(\eta)\).

notation.meaning: trial step, penalty, or metric parameter
predicted decrease certified by the method

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits an acceptance-policy leaf, but the merit function and predicted-decrease quantity are left entirely method-dependent. Without a cited primal-dual linesearch specifying these objects, the statement is only a generic template and cannot be confirmed as a mathematical policy for this container.

children.title: Backtracking Contraction Policies
children.top_down_role: Trial-parameter reduction regimes following failed local acceptance.

knowledge_statements.title: Backtracking Contraction Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric contraction of a rejected trial parameter until acceptance or declared failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose an initial trial \(\eta_{k,0}>0\), contraction factor \(\beta\in(0,1)\), acceptance predicate \(\mathcal A_k(\eta)\), and maximum \(J\in\mathbb N\) of contractions. For \(j=0,\ldots,J\), form \(\eta_{k,j}=\beta^j\eta_{k,0}\), compute the associated trial iterate, and test \(\mathcal A_k(\eta_{k,j})\). Stop at the least \(j_k\) for which the predicate holds and output \(\eta_k=\eta_{k,j_k}\) with its trial iterate. If no such \(j_k\leq J\) exists, return a failed-search flag. Thus a successful search performs exactly \(j_k\) contractions and satisfies \(\beta^J\eta_{k,0}\leq\eta_k\leq\eta_{k,0}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly multiply a rejected trial parameter by a fixed factor below one, stopping at the first accepted trial or a preset limit.
assumptions_latex: \(\eta_{k,0}>0\), \(\beta\in(0,1)\), and \(J\) is finite.
Each trial predicate \(\mathcal A_k(\eta_{k,j})\) is computable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On success, \(\eta_k=\beta^{j_k}\eta_{k,0}\) for the least accepted index \(j_k\leq J\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the backtracking-policy leaf and the finite geometric loop is internally coherent. However, the acceptance predicate is unspecified and no source connects this template to a primal-dual or ADMM search, so a method-specific source and locator are required.

children.title: Relaxation-Coupled Search
children.top_down_role: Search interfaces that coordinate local acceptance with relaxation choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Coupled Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint search over a primal-dual trial parameter and relaxation coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T_{\eta}\colon\mathcal W\to\mathcal W\) be a trial splitting map. Given \(w^k\), candidates \((\eta_j,\alpha_j)\) with \(\eta_j>0\) and \(0<\alpha_j<2\), form
\[
\widetilde w_j=T_{\eta_j}(w^k),\qquad w_j^+=w^k+\alpha_j(\widetilde w_j-w^k).
\]
Test a specified acceptance predicate \(\mathcal A_k(\eta_j,\alpha_j,w_j^+)\) in a fixed order. Return the first accepted pair and set \(w^{k+1}=w_j^+\). If the predicate fails, contract \(\eta_j\), move \(\alpha_j\) toward \(1\), or perform both according to the declared schedule. Report failure when the finite candidate schedule is exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search jointly over the splitting parameter and relaxation, accepting the first relaxed trial satisfying the declared test.
assumptions_latex: Each trial map \(T_{\eta_j}\) and predicate \(\mathcal A_k\) are computable.
The candidate schedule keeps \(\eta_j>0\) and \(0<\alpha_j<2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every successful output has \(w^{k+1}=w^k+\alpha_j(T_{\eta_j}(w^k)-w^k)\) for an accepted admissible pair \((\eta_j,\alpha_j)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the search leaf, but the joint candidate schedule, acceptance predicate, and universal-looking relaxation range are method-dependent. No source supports this particular coupling or its admissible range.

children.title: Adaptive-Parameter Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Controls on the magnitude, frequency, and persistence of parameter changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive-Parameter Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded, infrequent parameter adaptation with controlled cumulative variation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A positive adaptive sequence \((\theta_k)_{k\geq0}\) is safeguarded by constants \(0<\theta_{\min}\leq\theta_{\max}<\infty\), \(\gamma\geq1\), and an update set \(U\subseteq\mathbb N\) if
\[
\theta_{\min}\leq\theta_k\leq\theta_{\max},\qquad
\gamma^{-1}\leq\frac{\theta_{k+1}}{\theta_k}\leq\gamma,
\]
for every \(k\), \(\theta_{k+1}=\theta_k\) whenever \(k\notin U\), and either \(U\) is finite or
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\left|\log\theta_{k+1}-\log\theta_k\right|<\infty.
\]
These requirements respectively control magnitude, individual update size, update frequency, and persistent variation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keep adaptive parameters bounded, limit each multiplicative change, update only at declared times, and require finite or summable long-run variation.
assumptions_latex: \(\theta_k>0\) for all \(k\).
The update set \(U\) is fixed by a declared deterministic or history-measurable rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sequence remains uniformly positive and bounded, while its cumulative logarithmic variation is finite whenever updates persist indefinitely.

notation.meaning: adaptive penalty, step, or relaxation parameter
indices at which changes are permitted

The cited ADMM chapter locator does not confirm this combined bounded-ratio, update-set, and summable-log-variation package; the exact convergence safeguard must be supported by a specific result or section.

children.title: Automatic Tuning Interface Family
children.top_down_role: Policies intended to reduce dependence on unavailable operator scales or manual tuning.

children.title: Parameter-Free Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Solver interfaces designed to avoid user-supplied scale parameters.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-Free Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: User-facing solver interface with no problem-dependent numerical tuning input.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a problem class \(\mathcal P\), a solver interface is parameter-free relative to a declared accuracy and resource model if its user input consists only of a problem instance \(P\in\mathcal P\), a stopping specification \(\varepsilon>0\), and optional resource limits, while every internal numerical parameter sequence \((\theta_k)\) is generated by a fixed rule
\[
\theta_k=F_k(P,H_k),
\]
where \(H_k\) is the observable iteration history. No user-supplied Lipschitz constant, operator norm, penalty, step size, relaxation coefficient, or problem-dependent bound may enter \(F_k\). The label concerns the interface, not the absence of internal parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parameter-free interface asks only for the problem, accuracy, and resource limits; all numerical tuning is generated internally by fixed rules.
assumptions_latex: The problem class \(\mathcal P\), stopping rule, and permitted resource limits are declared.
Each history \(H_k\) contains only information computed by the solver through iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All numerical parameters are reproducible functions of \(P\) and the observed history, with no problem-dependent tuning supplied by the user.

notation.meaning: observable solver history through iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the interface leaf, but “parameter-free” is terminology whose scope varies across methods. The proposed exclusion of all user-supplied problem-dependent numerical information requires a canonical source and a clearer distinction between data contained in the problem instance and separate tuning input.

children.title: Self-Tuned Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Solver interfaces that infer or adapt parameter scales from observed behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Self-Tuned Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver interface whose internal parameters adapt from observable runtime data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A self-tuned primal-dual interface is a solver specified by an initial state \(w^0\), an initial admissible parameter \(\theta_0\in\Theta\), an iteration map \(w^{k+1}=T_{\theta_k}(w^k)\), and an internal tuning rule
\[
\theta_{k+1}=F_k(H_{k+1}),
\]
where \(H_{k+1}\) contains computed iterates, residuals, accepted trials, and oracle values through iteration \(k+1\). The rule must return \(\theta_{k+1}\in\Theta\) without external intervention. Unlike a parameter-free interface, a self-tuned interface may expose \(\theta_0\) or safeguard bounds while adapting subsequent values automatically.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A self-tuned interface updates its numerical parameters automatically from observed iterates, residuals, trials, and oracle values.
assumptions_latex: \(T_\theta\) and \(F_k\) are specified before execution.
The admissible parameter set \(\Theta\) is nonempty.
The tuning history uses no future information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every completed iteration, \(\theta_{k+1}\) is an admissible history-measurable parameter selected without external intervention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the interface leaf and the history-based rule is internally coherent, but the asserted distinction between self-tuned and parameter-free interfaces is terminological rather than universal. A canonical source with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Automatic-Tuning Robustness Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Problem regimes where automatic calibration becomes unreliable or overly sensitive.

knowledge_statements.title: Automatic-Tuning Robustness Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation invariance fails when a tuner is not equivariant under equivalent constraint rescalings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider equivalent constraint representations \(h(w)=0\) and \(ch(w)=0\) with \(c>0\). Let an automatic tuner select \(\theta_{k+1}=F(H_k)\), and let \(S_cH_k\) denote the history obtained after this rescaling. If the algorithm requires the parameter transformation \(G_c\) to preserve identical primal iterates, but
\[
F(S_cH_k)\neq G_c(F(H_k))
\]
for some attainable history, then the tuned method is not representation-equivariant: two algebraically equivalent formulations can produce different parameter sequences and primal iterates. Consequently, a robustness guarantee stated uniformly over such rescalings requires either equivariance of \(F\), scale-normalized diagnostics, or explicit bounds on \(c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Automatic tuning is not formulation-robust when equivalent constraint rescalings change diagnostics without inducing the matching parameter transformation.
assumptions_latex: \(c>0\) and the two constraint representations have the same feasible set.
\(G_c\) is the parameter transformation required for algorithmic equivalence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of \(F(S_cH)=G_c(F(H))\) at an attainable history precludes representation-equivariant tuning over unrestricted rescalings.

notation.meaning: history transformation induced by constraint scaling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the robustness-boundary leaf, but the conclusion depends on a method-specific equivalence transformation G_c and on how histories and primal iterates transform. No source or concrete algorithm establishes those requirements, so the claimed boundary cannot yet be confirmed.

children.title: Runtime Behavior Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Observable behavior used to distinguish poor scaling, inaccurate block solves, and unstable adaptation.

children.title: Persistent Residual Imbalance
children.top_down_role: One-sided feasibility or stationarity progress associated with poor parameter scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Residual Imbalance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed diagnostic for sustained one-sided primal or dual residual dominance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\bar r_k,\bar s_k>0\) be scale-normalized primal and dual residual norms, let \(m\in\mathbb N\), \(\mu>1\), and \(q\in(1/2,1]\). Persistent primal dominance at iteration \(k\geq m-1\) is the predicate
\[
\sum_{i=k-m+1}^{k}\mathbf 1\{\bar r_i\geq\mu\bar s_i\}\geq qm;
\]
persistent dual dominance is defined by interchanging \(\bar r_i\) and \(\bar s_i\). Persistent residual imbalance holds when either predicate is true. The diagnostic is undefined if the residuals have not been placed on declared compatible scales; it identifies imbalance but does not by itself prove that the penalty is its cause.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Flag imbalance when one normalized residual exceeds the other by a fixed factor during a prescribed fraction of a recent window.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar r_i\) and \(\bar s_i\) use declared compatible normalizations.
At least \(m\) residual pairs are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The predicate certifies sustained one-sided residual dominance over the window, not causal attribution to a particular parameter.

notation.meaning: normalized primal and dual residual norms
dominance factor and required window fraction

children.title: Extrapolation Instability Diagnostic Family
children.top_down_role: Alternating or amplifying progress measures associated with aggressive extrapolation.

children.title: Residual Oscillation Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Alternating or cyclic patterns visible in feasibility, stationarity, or gap measures.

assumptions_latex: \(e_i>0\) is a residual statistic measured with a fixed normalization.
At least \(m+1\) statistic values are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The flag certifies frequent sign reversals and inadequate windowed decay, but does not identify their cause.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed detection of repeated residual reversals without sufficient envelope decay.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(e_i>0\) be a scalar residual statistic, choose a window length \(m\geq3\), reversal fraction \(q\in(0,1]\), and decay threshold \(\delta\in(0,1)\). At iteration \(k\geq m\), define
\[
R_k=\sum_{i=k-m+2}^{k}\mathbf 1\{(e_i-e_{i-1})(e_{i-1}-e_{i-2})<0\}.
\]
A residual-oscillation flag is raised when \(R_k\geq q(m-1)\) and
\[
\min_{k-m+1\leq i\leq k}e_i>(1-\delta)\max_{k-m+1\leq i\leq k}e_i.
\]
Thus the statistic must reverse direction frequently while its window envelope fails to contract by the required fraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Flag oscillation when a residual repeatedly reverses direction and its recent envelope fails to shrink sufficiently.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Oscillation Diagnostics

children.title: Relaxation Instability Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Amplification or divergence patterns associated with aggressive relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Instability Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rollback comparison certificate associating instability with an aggressive relaxation value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let two trials start from the same state \(w^k\), use the same splitting parameter and oracle data, and differ only in relaxation: an aggressive value \(\alpha_a\) and a reference value \(\alpha_r=1\). For a declared merit function \(\Phi\geq0\), tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), and factor \(\kappa>1\), the pair is a relaxation-instability certificate when
\[
\Phi(w_a^+)\geq\kappa\Phi(w^k),\qquad
\Phi(w_r^+)\leq\Phi(w^k)-\varepsilon.
\]
Because all other trial inputs are held fixed, the certificate verifies that the aggressive relaxation fails the local acceptance standard while the unrelaxed control succeeds. It is a local comparative certificate, not a proof of global divergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare matched aggressive and unrelaxed trials; flag relaxation instability when only the aggressive trial enlarges merit substantially.
assumptions_latex: The two trials share the same starting state, splitting parameter, and oracle information.
\(\Phi\) is finite and evaluated identically for both trials.
\(\alpha_a\neq1\), \(\kappa>1\), and \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The matched comparison certifies local failure attributable to the changed relaxation input, without certifying global divergence.

notation.meaning: aggressively relaxed and reference trial states

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The matched-trial comparison is coherent, but certificate is a stronger and less natural role than a diagnostic condition for this leaf. More importantly, no source establishes these merit inequalities as a recognized relaxation-instability certificate or supports the stated attribution boundary.

children.title: Oscillation Attribution Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where oscillation alone cannot identify relaxation as the governing cause.

knowledge_statements.title: Oscillation Attribution Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates oscillation caused by extrapolation from oscillation explainable by the unextrapolated splitting map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be the fixed-parameter, unextrapolated iteration map and let \(x^{k+1}=T(x^k+\beta_k(x^k-x^{k-1}))\). Define the matched control step \(\widehat x^{k+1}=T(x^k)\). An observed oscillation is attributable to extrapolation only if it persists in the monitored quantity for the extrapolated steps but disappears, or decreases by a prescribed factor, in matched control steps computed with identical penalty, metric, and inner-solve tolerances. If the same oscillation occurs for \(\widehat x^{k+1}\), the observation does not distinguish extrapolation instability from scaling, conditioning, or inexact-solve effects.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oscillation is assigned to extrapolation only when matched unextrapolated control steps suppress it; otherwise the diagnostic cannot isolate extrapolation from competing causes.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) and the extrapolated iteration use identical problem data, penalty parameters, metrics, and stopping tolerances.
The monitored oscillation statistic and its suppression threshold are fixed before comparison.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Extrapolation attribution is valid only when the matched control comparison separates the two behaviors.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but the matched-control attribution rule and suppression threshold are bespoke diagnostic claims with no cited evidence. A source is needed to justify when this comparison supports causal attribution rather than merely correlation.

children.title: Inner-Solve Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Outer progress limited by inaccurate or disproportionately costly block solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Inner-Solve Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A runtime certificate that inaccurate or costly inner solves are limiting outer ADMM progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For outer iteration \(k\), let \(e_k\) be a verifiable inner optimality residual, \(R_k\) an outer primal-dual residual, and \(c_k\) the inner work. Given a window length \(m\), progress factor \(\eta\in(0,1)\), tolerance \(\tau>0\), and work threshold \(C>0\), certify inner-solve stagnation when \(R_k>\tau\), \(R_k>\eta R_{k-m}\), and either \(e_k\) exceeds its prescribed forcing tolerance or \(\sum_{j=k-m+1}^{k}c_j>C\). The certificate states that acceptable outer progress was not obtained while inner accuracy or cost violated its declared budget; it does not by itself identify the underlying conditioning defect.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stagnation is certified when outer residuals remain above tolerance and fail to improve while inner accuracy or cumulative inner work violates its budget.
assumptions_latex: \(k\ge m\ge1\), and all residuals and work measures are finite and computed consistently.
Inner forcing tolerances and diagnostic thresholds are fixed or recorded for the inspected window.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequalities constitute a checkable certificate of inner-solve stagnation over the window.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits the runtime-diagnostic leaf, and the quantities are introduced consistently. However, the window test, disjunctive accuracy-or-cost condition, and interpretation as inner-solve stagnation are unsupported policy choices requiring a direct source.

children.title: Scaling-Conditioning Diagnostic System
children.top_down_role: Slow or imbalanced progress induced by anisotropic operators and poorly scaled variables.

children.title: Problem-Scaling Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Observable progress distortions associated with mismatched variable or constraint scales.

knowledge_statements.title: Problem-Scaling Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Detects poor numerical scaling through coordinatewise magnitudes of data, iterates, and residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a scaled constrained model \(D_r(Ax+Bz-c)=0\) with variable transformation \((x,z)=D_c(\widetilde x,\widetilde z)\), fix an admissible dynamic-range bound \(\Gamma>1\). A problem-scaling warning is certified if a recorded nonzero data, iterate, or residual component family \(v\) satisfies \(\max_i|v_i|/\min_{i:|v_i|>0}|v_i|>\Gamma\), and admissible diagonal equilibration reduces this ratio below \(\Gamma\) without changing the represented optimization problem. The certificate concerns magnitude imbalance; it does not establish spectral ill-conditioning of the scaled subproblem operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Poor scaling is indicated by excessive componentwise dynamic range that admissible diagonal equilibration reduces without changing the represented problem.
assumptions_latex: \(D_r\) and \(D_c\) are invertible diagonal matrices representing an equivalent change of constraint and variable coordinates.
The component family and dynamic-range threshold \(\Gamma\) are declared before diagnosis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successful reduction of excessive componentwise dynamic range certifies a problem-scaling defect, not spectral ill-conditioning.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits the diagnostic leaf, but componentwise dynamic range alone is not a generally established certificate of poor problem scaling. The admissible equilibration and equivalence conditions are model-dependent, so the proposed rule needs direct support.

children.title: Ill-Conditioning Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Slow or anisotropic progress associated with unfavorable operator geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Conditioning Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A spectral diagnostic for sensitivity and slow inner convergence in ADMM subproblem systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_k\) be the self-adjoint positive-definite operator defining an inner quadratic solve at outer iteration \(k\), and let \(\kappa(H_k)=\lambda_{\max}(H_k)/\lambda_{\min}(H_k)\). Suppose validated bounds satisfy \(0<\underline\lambda_k^{\min}\le\lambda_{\min}(H_k)\le\overline\lambda_k^{\min}\) and \(0<\underline\lambda_k^{\max}\le\lambda_{\max}(H_k)\le\overline\lambda_k^{\max}\). For a declared threshold \(K>1\), the inequality \(\underline\lambda_k^{\max}/\overline\lambda_k^{\min}>K\) certifies \(\kappa(H_k)>K\). Conversely, \(\overline\lambda_k^{\max}/\underline\lambda_k^{\min}\le K\) certifies \(\kappa(H_k)\le K\). If neither inequality holds, these bounds are inconclusive. Componentwise magnitude imbalance alone is insufficient for this certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validated lower and upper spectral bounds can certify that the inner operator is above or below a declared condition-number threshold; otherwise the test is inconclusive.
assumptions_latex: \(H_k\) is self-adjoint and positive definite in the inner product used by the linear solver.
All four spectral bounds are valid for the same operator and metric used in the solve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lower condition-number bound certifies \(\kappa(H_k)>K\), while the upper condition-number bound certifies \(\kappa(H_k)\le K\); intermediate cases remain inconclusive.

notation.meaning: validated lower and upper bounds on the smallest eigenvalue
validated lower and upper bounds on the largest eigenvalue

children.title: Scaling-Conditioning Discrimination
children.top_down_role: Diagnostic evidence used to distinguish remediable scaling defects from intrinsic conditioning.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Conditioning Discrimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A controlled rescaling test that distinguishes magnitude imbalance from persistent spectral conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an equivalent family of diagonal scalings \((D_r,D_c)\), first record componentwise dynamic range \(g\), spectral condition estimate \(\widehat\kappa\), and normalized inner-solver convergence. Apply an admissible equilibration and recompute \((g',\widehat\kappa')\) using the same estimator and stopping rule. Classify the primary defect as scaling when \(g'\ll g\) and normalized convergence improves without persistently large \(\widehat\kappa'\); classify it as conditioning when \(\widehat\kappa'\) remains above its declared threshold under well-scaled coordinates. Otherwise output “undetermined.” The procedure must retain both measurements and must not infer spectral conditioning solely from residual imbalance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare dynamic range, spectral estimates, and solver behavior before and after equivalent equilibration; unresolved or conflicting evidence yields an undetermined diagnosis.
assumptions_latex: The diagonal transformation preserves equivalence of the optimization model and is numerically nonsingular.
Before-and-after condition estimates and convergence statistics use identical metrics and stopping conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The controlled comparison returns scaling, conditioning, or undetermined according to the stated decision rule.

notation.meaning: componentwise dynamic range before and after equilibration
condition-number estimates before and after equilibration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the discrimination leaf, but the meanings of “much less than,” normalized improvement, and persistent conditioning are not operationally specified. The controlled classification protocol and its thresholds require a direct source.

children.title: Subproblem Linear-Algebra Interfaces

children.title: Factorization Reuse Lifecycle
children.top_down_role: Reuse of fixed linear-system structure across outer iterations.

children.title: Factorization Caching
children.top_down_role: Storage and lifecycle choices for factorizations retained across outer iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Factorization Caching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stores a direct-solver factorization under a key that identifies the inner system matrix and factorization configuration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For inner systems \(H(\theta_k)u=b_k\), define a cache key \(q_k\) containing every parameter, matrix version, precision choice, ordering, and factorization option that determines both \(H(\theta_k)\) and its factorization representation. On the first occurrence of \(q_k\), compute a factorization object \(F_k=\operatorname{factor}(H(\theta_k))\), validate the associated solve operation for the selected representation, and store \((q_k,F_k)\) with its validation metadata. On a later occurrence, retrieve \(F_k\) only when the current key matches and the metadata remains valid; then solve the new right-hand side using the cached factors. Otherwise compute and cache a new factorization. Return the inner solution and updated cache.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cache a validated factorization object keyed by every matrix- and representation-determining choice, and reuse it for new right-hand sides only while that key and its metadata remain valid.
assumptions_latex: For each cacheable key, the selected direct factorization exists and its associated solve operation is numerically admissible.
The key includes matrix values or a reliable matrix-version identifier, as well as factorization configuration and precision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A cached factorization object is reused exactly when its key and validation metadata establish compatibility with the current system and solver representation.

notation.meaning: inner-system matrix determined by the current state
cache key for matrix- and factorization-determining state
stored factorization object and solve representation

children.title: Numerical Factor Reuse
children.top_down_role: Repeated application of retained factors when the linear-system structure remains compatible.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Factor Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which stored numerical factors remain valid for a later inner solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be numerical factors computed for a matrix \(H\). Reuse of \(F\) to solve \(H'u=b'\) is valid only when \(H'=H\) in the arithmetic model represented by the cache key, the factorization type and permutations are unchanged, and the stored factors pass their declared finite-value and pivot-validity checks. Changes only to \(b'\) permit reuse. A change to a penalty, metric, regularization, active set, matrix coefficient, precision, or ordering that changes \(H\) or its factorization representation violates the reuse condition and requires renewed validation or refactorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Numerical factors may serve new right-hand sides only when the represented matrix, factorization choices, precision, and validity checks remain unchanged.
assumptions_latex: The cached factors and metadata were produced by a completed, validated factorization.
Matrix identity is determined by a collision-resistant key or an exact versioning invariant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated invariants are necessary cache-validity conditions for numerical factor reuse.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind exactly fits this leaf, and the stated matrix and representation invariants are plausible. No citation supports the detailed precision, permutation, pivot-validity, and active-set boundaries, so a direct numerical-linear-algebra source is required.

children.title: Cache Invalidation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural or numerical changes that make retained factors unsuitable for further use.

knowledge_statements.title: Cache Invalidation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies state changes after which cached symbolic or numerical factors cannot be reused without validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider cached symbolic analysis \(S(H)\) and numerical factors \(F(H)\) for an inner matrix \(H\). A change in sparsity pattern, dimensions, ordering constraints, or factorization type invalidates \(S(H)\) and consequently \(F(H)\). A change in any numerical entry of \(H\), including one induced by penalty, metric, regularization, or active-set updates, invalidates \(F(H)\) but need not invalidate \(S(H)\) when the sparsity pattern is unchanged. A right-hand-side change alone invalidates neither object. Reuse across an invalidation boundary is permitted only after an independent compatibility validation establishing the required invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Structural changes invalidate symbolic and numerical cache entries; coefficient changes invalidate numerical factors; right-hand-side changes alone invalidate neither.
assumptions_latex: Cache metadata distinguishes structural analysis from numerical factorization.
The matrix assembly map exposes all state capable of changing matrix structure or values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Cache invalidation follows the strongest affected invariant: structure for symbolic analysis and entries for numerical factors.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, and the symbolic-versus-numerical distinction is coherent. The detailed invalidation rules, including ordering and independent compatibility validation, have no source and require direct support.

children.title: Matrix-Free Iterative Solves
children.top_down_role: Operator-only inner linear algebra for large or implicit systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free Iterative Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Krylov inner solution using only operator actions, without explicitly assembling the system matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a linear system \(Hu=b\), an initial vector \(u^0\), tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), and an oracle returning \(Hv\), apply an iterative Krylov method compatible with the operator class: conjugate gradients when \(H\) is self-adjoint positive definite, or an appropriate nonsymmetric method otherwise. At inner iteration \(j\), form search quantities using oracle products and vector operations, without assembling \(H\). Stop when the declared residual test, such as \(\lVert b-Hu^j\rVert\le\varepsilon\max\{1,\lVert b\rVert\}\), holds; return \(u^j\) and the achieved residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve an inner linear system with Krylov iterations driven only by matrix-vector products, stopping at a declared residual tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The product oracle returns \(Hv\) consistently for every queried vector \(v\).
The selected Krylov method matches the symmetry and definiteness class of \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned iterate satisfies the declared residual test without explicit matrix assembly.
